News.title: Westminster's time is coming to an end, Welsh, Scottish, Northern Irish leaders say
News.content:
The first ministers of Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland have declared that "Westminster's time is coming to an end", and that the UK government should "prepare" for constitutional change.

The nationalist leaders from Plaid Cymru, Sinn FÃ©in and the SNP - who want their countries to leave the United Kingdom - signed an agreement on Monday which said no Westminster government had the right to "block democracy".

But while Scotland's John Swinney and Northern Ireland's Michelle O'Neill called for referendums at a joint press conference, Wales' Rhun ap Iorwerth refused to give a timetable for one in his country.

Sinn FÃ©in president Mary Lou McDonald also attended.

Ap Iorwerth will hold further talks with Swinney in the afternoon in their roles as government leaders, with both men expected to sign an agreement on "future collaboration in areas of shared interest".

For the first time since devolution began, Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland all have first ministers who want to leave the United Kingdom.

All three met on Monday as representatives of their parties.

The memorandum of understanding said: "For people watching across these islands - for people watching around the world - there could be no clearer sign that Westminster's time is coming to an end.

"No Westminster government has the right to block democracy or undermine the principle that our people will decide their own future.

"We recognise that our parties have different constitutional positions and that each nation will determine its own future in its own way and in its own time."

News.title: Amy Hunt tells Sydney Sweeney 'this is what a woman in sport looks like' after controversial ad
News.content:
British sprinter Amy Hunt is among the female athletes to speak out against a controversial sports gambling advert starring actress Sydney Sweeney.

The advert has gone viral online and features American Sweeney naked but covering parts of her body with various pieces of sporting equipment.

It has sparked a strong reaction, with many female athletes criticising its sexualisation of women in sport, and how they are being defined by their appearance rather than their achievements as sportswomen.

Hunt, who became a four-time European champion earlier this summer, referenced the advert after she ran a season's best 22.10 seconds to finish fourth in the 200m final at the Ultimate Championship in Budapest on Sunday.

"Sydney Sweeney, this is what women in sport look like," Hunt said in her post-race interview with BBC Sport.

Referring to Melissa Jefferson-Wooden's winning time of 21.47 seconds, the fourth fastest ever over the distance, she added: "21.4. Muscles. Hard work, blood, sweat, tears. This is a beautiful evening."

American actress Sweeney, 29, starred in the television series Euphoria and her films include Anyone But You and The Housemaid.

The backlash has included many other athletes from a range of sports posting videos of themselves competing or training, and describing the frustrations and struggles they have faced throughout their careers.

The trend was started by American gymnast Gracie Kramer, who posted a montage of herself training with the caption, "I don't know what Sydney Sweeney was doing, but this is what women in sport look like."

News.title: The Pitt is up for 25 Emmys - but the show's biggest fans are real-life doctors
News.content:
It's a familiar sight: a crowded waiting room, trolleys in corridors, stressed doctors and nurses. But this isn't a typical A&E unit in the NHS, it's a Hollywood set with actors recreating the drama of an emergency department for TV series The Pitt.

And among its biggest fans are real-life doctors.

"We finally feel validated for everything we go through every day," says Dr Tony Cirillo, President of the American College of Emergency Physicians.

On Monday, The Pitt could become this year's most decorated series at the Emmys, America's most coveted TV honours, with 25 nominations.

Doctors and others in the medical profession say, for them, it's the most realistic medical drama yet - which is why they love it.

News.title: I had 11 years of chemotherapy for a cancer I didn't have
News.content:
Becky Jones was just 21 when she was told she had a terminal brain tumour and months to live.

She had not long met her partner and dreamed of a career in policing, but suddenly the future was looking bleak.

The diagnosis, by an experienced cancer consultant, led to 11 years of chemotherapy treatment which changed her life. She regularly felt sick, she was unable to take part in family events, her career was curtailed and she felt constantly "on eggshells".

Now 34, she has recently learned she never had cancer at all but an inflammation of the brain that could have been treated with steroids.

The mother of two is one of more than 40 patients taking legal action against University Hospitals Coventry and Warwickshire (UHCW) NHS Trust due to prolonged or unnecessary cancer treatment.

"I was told time and time again without the chemotherapy I would die," she said.

News.title: Deep-fried food banned under new school dinner rules in England
News.content:
There will be a boost for fresh fruit and vegetables and deep-fried food will be banned in what the government has called the biggest shake-up to school dinners in England in over a decade.

Under new school food standards, fibre and wholegrains will also be increased, and breakfast clubs will have to follow nutrition rules for the first time, with schools also being monitored.

The Association of School and College Leaders (ASCL) welcomed the changes, but said they hoped the new rules would not become "another stick with which to beat head teachers".

The changes will come into effect from 2027 and be funded with existing money for schools, the government said.

As part of the new framework, sweet desserts, like cake, will be reduced from a regular lunch offer to twice a week in secondary schools, and once a week in primary schools. They also must now be served with a portion of fruit.

Servings of processed meats such as ham, sausages and chicken nuggets have been reduced to once a week and must come with a side of vegetables or fruit.

Education Secretary Lucy Powell said they were "once-in-a-generation changes" which would "transform school food for children across the country".

News.title: Buckingham Palace works uncover trove of everyday items dating back to 1800s
News.content:
It revealed the monarch would work the room in a "clockwise direction", and that aides were asked to encourage the 350 British guests to mingle with the diplomats at the annual gathering.

"The British guests will be distributed throughout the State Rooms, except the Music Room and West Gallery, where they should be encouraged to talk to the Diplomats," the sheet reads.

Blank Littlewoods Football Pool betting slips from 1957 and a scrap of West End theatre listings from The Standard newspaper in 1889 were also found, alongside fragments of Minton decorative ceramic tiles from a fireplace hearth, with the design dated to around the mid-1800s.

A pewter tankard, a wooden junction box and a faded box containing six Christmas cards were included in the haul.

Examples of electrical wire covered with vulcanised Indian rubber cabling were found. It was replaced as priority when the restoration began as it posed the greatest risk of fire to the building.

Also discovered were pages from the Daily Express newspaper in 1966 detailing the "maximum security" prison where the Great Train Robbers were incarcerated.

The article had pictures of Durham Prison, revealing that "the men who were found guilty of stealing a fortune in mailbags spend their week stitching them for nine shillings".

Meanwhile, the whist drive ticket, priced at 6d or sixpence, would have taken place during the reign of King Charles III's grandfather, George VI, hosted by the Buckingham palace social club.

News.title: Speedboat killer jailed for attack on girlfriend
News.content:
Speedboat killer Jack Shepherd has been jailed for 20 months with a further four years on extended licence for violently assaulting his girlfriend, including hitting her chest with a set of hot barbecue tongs.

The 38-year-old had pleaded guilty to two counts of assault occasioning actual bodily harm and damaging property at Isleworth Crown Court in July.

The attacks happened in February and June last year and sparked Shepherd's recall to prison.

He was originally jailed in 2018 for six years and six months for manslaughter over the death of 24-year-old Charlotte Brown when his speedboat crashed during a first date.

Shepherd was jailed for a further four years at Exeter Crown Court in 2019 for a drink-fuelled attack on a barman in March 2018 at a Devon hotel.

According to a prosecution summary of the case, Shepherd started dating his former partner in August 2024, but towards the end of the year she accused him of being abusive and threatening.

In February 2025, he admitted pinning down the woman and "punching her several times, causing bruising to her arm and top of leg" during an argument.

In the second incident, in June 2025, Shepherd got angry with her for burning a pizza during a barbecue, and "proceeded to hit her with the barbecue tongs on her left breast which caused a permanent scar".

Mitigating, George Payne said Shepherd, who attended by videolink from HMP Swaleside in Kent, was "genuinely very ashamed of his behaviour".

"The behaviour is driven by his abuse of alcohol and is a feature that has existed for a long time," Payne said.

Judge Martin Edmunds rejected that, and said he had "no faith" in Shepherd's remorse, adding: "Your pattern is to commit offences and afterwards apologise, and produce excuses. Your prepared statement sought to shift blame anywhere but yourself."

Judge Edmunds previously told the court the law did not allow him to add any more time to the term Shepherd was already serving, and his most recent sentence would be served concurrently to his current sentence.

He is due to be released in January 2029.

Shepherd was released on licence in January 2024, but faced recall to prison in September last year after he was accused of violence towards the woman.

News.title: Former West Ham keeper Miklosko dies aged 64
News.content:
Former West Ham, QPR and Czech Republic goalkeeper Ludek Miklosko has died at the age of 64.

Miklosko made almost 400 appearances for the Hammers from 1990 to 1998 and was much loved by supporters, who regularly sang his name long after he left the club.

He later returned as a goalkeeping coach.

Miklosko withdrew from cancer treatment in December 2024, three years after his diagnosis.

Days later he returned to West Ham's London Stadium for a Premier League match against Liverpool to a hero's reception.

A West Ham statement read: "It is with deep and profound sadness that West Ham United announces the passing of legendary former goalkeeper and coach, Ludek Miklosko.

"Rest in peace Ludek, our beloved, inspirational goalkeeper and gentle giant of a man."

News.title: MPs and Lords call for new law to address AI threat to human rights
News.content:
A cross-party group of MPs and peers has identified human rights risks posed by artificial intelligence (AI), arguing existing laws are ill-equipped to address the technology's rapid growth.

The Joint Committee on Human Rights (JCHR) published a report calling for a new bill on AI to "address the scale and seriousness" of such threats.

"Nowhere in the world, including the UK, has a current legislative and regulatory approach to AI that is fit for purpose," said Labour MP and committee chair Alex Sobel.

Labour education minister Georgia Gould said AI was creating opportunities but that it was critical the government was "responding to those risks" posed by the technology.

In a summary of its 100-page report, the JCHR argued AI has been responsible for numerous abuses of human rights, citing examples including the use of AI to create sexualised images of women and girls, and scanning people's faces without their consent.

The JCHR has advocated for the creation of a "single, independent AI oversight body... on a statutory basis", saying the current legal framework is "fragmented and difficult to navigate", "leaving gaps in protection".

The report goes on to call for "more demanding obligations for higher risk AI systems and models" at all stages of the "AI lifecycle".

It continues: "Some uses of AI should be prohibited outright because they are incompatible with human rights. Potential areas for action include subliminal techniques, and inappropriate use of profiling or biometric data."

The committee's chair said: "AI is heralded as an unprecedented era of technological development with the potential to transform our lives for better or for worse."

"It is moving with such speed and complexity that its impact is hard to accurately predict. What is clear is that at present we are unprepared to deal with its consequences however potentially dire they may be."

The JCHR's 12 members are drawn from both Houses of Parliament and they currently include MPs and peers from the Labour, Conservative and Liberal Democrat parties.

Monday's report comes amid growing anxiety over the challenges posed by AI.

Jacob Coxon, an AI researcher who quit Anthropic, told the BBC this weekend that staff developing the systems were "genuinely frightened" for the future of humanity.

An Anthropic spokesperson told BBC News that it was building "models with some of the strongest safeguards in the industry".

Labour's 2024 general election manifesto said it would "ensure the safe development and use of AI models by introducing binding regulation on the handful of companies developing the most powerful AI models".

The government used the King's Speech in July 2024 to commit to bringing forward "appropriate legislation", but no dedicated AI bill appeared in this year's King's Speech.

Asked what had happened to the law promised by Labour, Gould told BBC Breakfast that the government "has been regulating" - including action to tackle non-consensual sexualised deepfakes and a bill linked to cyber security.

She said: "There is action happening and we're continuing to really carefully monitor the rise of AI, the way the technology is evolving and making sure we're staying alongside it, and we have some of the best people in the world doing that work."

Gould said the AI Security Institute was "working through challenges coming in the future, testing models when they're coming into the UK", and that there was a need to work with other countries on the issue.

Following his arrival in No 10 in July, Prime Minister Andy Burnham ensured AI Minister Kanishka Narayan would attend cabinet meetings after scrapping the Department for Science, Innovation and Technology and splitting its responsibilities among other government departments.

On Saturday, the head of Anthropic, Dario Amodei, proposed a plan calling for the regulation of AI.

Amodei's plan included global regulation, industry-wide regulation and independent monitoring of AI models as they are developed.

He also urged the pace of development to be slowed down and the bosses of two rival AI firms, Sam Altman of OpenAI and Elon Musk, said they agreed with him.

One human rights concern raised in recent years is that AI can display biases against particular groups if trained on large datasets scraped from the internet which can include racist, sexist and other undesirable material.

AI could also be used to create and spread misinformation.

News.title: Police had councillor's fingerprints on hate mail - but dropped case
News.content:
Police had fingerprint evidence linking a high-profile councillor to a poison pen letter up to 12 months before he went on to target another politician in a "persistent and wicked" hate mail campaign.

Well-known Liverpool anti-poverty campaigner Gerard Woodhouse, 63, was given a community order last year for harassing ex-Lord Mayor Christine Banks â who he had known for 50 years â with anonymous letters and cards in the post between 2023 and 2025.

But the BBC has learned that although an investigation that pre-dated his hate campaign against Labour colleague Banks yielded fingerprint evidence from a letter sent to a housing association boss, the inquiry was stood down because officers were "unable to establish contact" with the alleged victim after she left her job.

Despite reopening the case earlier this year, police have now had to drop it because the time limit for prosecuting harassment allegations has expired.

The alleged victim, Julie Fadden, 65, said if Woodhouse had been dealt with he might have been stopped before he began harassing Banks and other suspected victims.

Merseyside Police did not respond to the BBC's questions about whether it had done enough to contact Fadden during the 2022 investigation.

News.title: 'Culture shift' needed in how UK does business, PM urges
News.content:
The UK needs a "culture shift" in how it does business, Andy Burnham has said ahead of a meeting with some of Britain's biggest bosses.

The prime minister said those who take risks in business should be backed by government and local leaders should have the power to work with companies.

The Labour government has been criticised for increasing costs for firms, such as with the employer national insurance and minimum wage changes under Burnham's predecessor Sir Keir Starmer.

The meeting comes as Chancellor John Healey prepares for his first Budget next month, with rising borrowing costs in recent weeks adding to the pressure on government finances.

Downing Street said Burnham will meet the chief executives of BP, Shell, HSBC, Morrisons, Sainsbury's, BT, Vodafone, Rolls-Royce and several others at Number 10.

Ahead of the meeting, Burnham said he would give people "the confidence that if they have a great idea, they'll get all the support they need to bring it to life".

"When local leaders have the tools to get things done and government works in partnership with business, you can pull in investment, create jobs and transform communities," he said.

He added the government would be "a partner for growth to make every part of Britain better off".

Burnham will host a reception for the business community where local leaders are invited before a private engagement with senior chief executives at Downing Street on Monday evening.

The meeting comes as higher borrowing costs in the UK and other countries present problems for governments looking to spend money on business support or investment.

Separately, hundreds of hospitality businesses have written to the prime minister, external, calling on him to cut VAT for the sector.

More than 800 pub, restaurant and hotel bosses - include celebrity chefs Heston Blumenthal and Tom Kerridge - signed the letter asking for the hospitality VAT rate to be reduced from 20% to 10%.

When he was still Mayor of Greater Manchester, Burnham said he would argue for the tax to be in line with the lower rates seen in other European countries.

News.title: Rent rises set to speed up in gloomy forecast for tenants
News.content:
The rising cost of renting a home in the UK has accelerated after a three-year slowdown - with tenants told to expect more pain to come.

Average rental costs for new tenancies were up 2.6% in July compared with a year earlier, according to property website Zoopla.

That remains lower than the rate of rising prices in general, but the property portal has forecast annual rent rises among privately rented homes will hit 4% or 5% by the end of the year.

It said there were fewer homes available to rent and - with potential first-time buyers put off by higher mortgage rates - competition for rental places in some areas was more intense.

"Our latest report shows how sensitive the rental market is to even modest changes in how many homes are available for rent," said Richard Donnell, executive director at Zoopla.

"Growing the number of homes for rent through increased investment is the most sustainable route to boosting choice for renters and ensuring stability in rent levels over the long run."

News.title: Refereeing body admits judgement error over Haaland derby winner
News.content:
The Premier League refereeing body Pro Ref has admitted an "error of judgement" in awarding Erling Haaland's Manchester City winner against Manchester United.

As City celebrated a remarkable derby victory over Manchester United, there were questions as to whether Haaland's winning goal should have stood in a match fraught with controversy.

The striker scored in the 60th minute at Old Trafford, turning home at the back post from Josko Gvardiol's cross before it was disallowed on the field for offside.

Following intervention from the video assistant referee, the goal was awarded - the Norwegian ruled to have been played onside by Patrick Dorgu's boot.

But there was debate as to whether the offside Enzo Fernandez, diving at the ball in a more central position than Haaland, was interfering with play.

In a statement, Pro Ref said: "It was established that Enzo Fernandez did not play the ball and therefore that makes any offside offence subjective.

"However, on this occasion, the VAR did not recognise the likely impact of his position and should have recommended an on-field review.

"Contact has been made with Manchester United this evening to acknowledge what we deem is an error of judgement. A review of the incident will take place."

United defender Lisandro Martinez said it was an "injustice" while boss Michael Carrick said he was "confused" by the decision.

The goal came after City had gone down to 10 men in the first half when Phil Foden was shown a straight red card for kicking out at United captain Bruno Fernandes.

Foden was dismissed by referee Michael Oliver on 23 minutes after kicking the midriff of Fernandes while he was on the turf.

News.title: Dentists issue warnings about illegal pop-up events in hotels
News.content:
A dentist says he is "deeply concerned" by illegal dental tourism pop-up consultations in Northern Irish hotels, which are not properly registered.

Paul Brennan, chair of the Northern Ireland branch of the British Dental Association (BDA), said patients' mouths were often examined at these events, which constitutes the "practice of dentistry".

The BDA has warned that when dentistry occurs and the hotels and dentists are not registered with their regulators, it can amount to "illegal practice".

The Northern Ireland Hotels Federation (NIHF) said it had shared the BDA's guidance with its members.

Anyone practising dentistry in the UK must be registered with the General Dental Council (GDC) and any venue in which it occurs must be registered with Regulation and Quality Improvement Authority (RQIA).

RQIA said it had received intelligence about 21 "unregistered entities" that have organised consultation events since October 2023.

It said "where concerns have arisen regarding the provision or promotion of dental tourism treatments in Northern Ireland", cease and desist letters had been sent to "the overseas dental practice involved" rather than the venue hosting the event.

Two upcoming events in Belfast have been cancelled either by the overseas provider or the hotel, following enquiries by BBC News NI.

News.title: Warm start to week to make way for wetter and windier conditions
News.content:
Changeable autumnal conditions are set to continue through this coming week, with spells of wetter and windier weather developing at times.

Monday will bring a short-lived burst of warmth and sunshine before temperatures drop to levels more typical for September later in the week.

A strengthening jet stream will bring deeper, low-pressure systems as the week goes on, with the potential for minor disruption towards next weekend.

Higher pressure looks set to build again for the end of the month, but prospects of a late-September heatwave remain uncertain.

News.title: Watch: Is the Bayeux Tapestry exhibition worth the hype?
News.content:
Visitors flocked to the British Museum in London on Thursday as the Bayeux Tapestry exhibition opened its doors to the general public.

The Bayeux Tapestry is an embroidery almost 70m (230ft) in length and nearly 1,000 years old. It tells the story of the Norman conquest of England and the Battle of Hastings in 1066.

Adult tickets to see the tapestry are priced at Â£33 during peak times and Â£27 at off-peak times, with an additional Â£3.50 donation.

The BBC's Katie Razzall asked the first visitors if it was worth the price.

Jobseekers are increasingly using artificial intelligence to apply for jobs – but leaving AI in charge of your applications could be a hindrance to securing new roles, new research suggests.

Applicants may use AI to fill out forms, write cover letters and answer initial questions, especially if they are applying to multiple organisations.

But one new experiment has suggested this might not be the best use of your time – and could even see you miss out on the role you really wanted.

Job resource site Kickresume set up a test to find the best and worst-performing applications for a series of sales and marketing roles, comparing AI-written CVs to those entirely created by people.

The human-written CV was the most successful, receiving a positive response for almost a third of the 200 applications (31 per cent).

At the other end of the scale, AI-only CVs were the worst performers, with just one in ten (10 per cent) receiving a positive initial response.

AI-only CVs were the worst performers, with a 10% positive initial response ( Getty Images/iStockphoto )

However, there was a notable boost (18 per cent) when people tailored the AI-written CVs afterwards.

Peter Duris, CEO of Kickresume, said: “While the strongest CV was human-written, a little tailoring of your AI-written CV to fit the job description can boost its performance significantly. In our test, tailoring nearly doubled the AI resume’s response rate.

“Pulling in the language from the posting shows recruiters and hiring managers you’re a genuine fit for the role and helps your CV read cleanly to an applicant tracking system along the way.”

The research offers an eye-opening consideration for jobseekers who are perhaps feeling the strain from repeat applying and wondering if mass-sends outs, written automatically, are a better scatter-gun approach.

There was no additional work produced, such as a cover letter for example, and the single-sector applications therefore might not have seen the same results across different employment areas.

But it serves as a reminder all the same that recruiters and employers want to see differentiation between applicants and that the jobseeker will always know their strengths and personality better than an AI model writing a CV for them.

“It was really interesting carrying out this experiment, and we hope it inspires people to keep pushing with their job search and experimenting with their own CVs,” Mr Duris concluded.

Oasis are widely expected to be announcing a new tour today, with fans poised for 4pm BST when the band will be sharing their news.

The Manchester rock legends teased the announcement last week with a spectacular drone display in Manchester, with the band’s logo showing up in lights along with the date 14/09/26 and the time 4pm BST.

Oasis have also been dropping hints about potential tour venues over the past few weeks on their social media channels, including the Etihad Stadium in Manchester, Celtic Park in Glasgow, and Knebworth in Hertfordshire.

Even before the band’s 2025 reunion concerts had concluded, fans and the media were speculating that once-warring brothers Noel and Liam Gallagher would be back on stage together again in the near future, such was the success of last year’s tour.

The announcement comes a week after Noel and Liam attended the UK premiere of the documentary film Oasis: Don’t Look Back in Anger from Steven Knight and co-directors Dylan Southern and Will Lovelace, showing behind-the-scenes footage and concert clips from the 2025 reunion.

Tickets to the Oasis Live ‘25 shows sold out within minutes of going on sale, with the tour estimated by Forbes to have generated over $400m (£293m) in revenue, and Noel and Liam each pocketing between $50m-$100m. As a result, the pair cracked the Sunday Times Rich List this year with a combined net worth of $375m.

Follow for the latest updates on today’s 4pm announcement.

Outgoing Saturday Night Live star Chloe Fineman has revived her Sydney Sweeney impression to poke fun at the Euphoria star’s controversial new sports betting ad.

Fineman — who announced her departure from SNL in July — has both impersonated Sweeney and appeared alongside her during the actor’s time on the long-running sketch show.

“Yesterday I moved out of my dressing room at SNL, but I got to take my ‘Sydney Sweeneys,’” Fineman said in a clip shared to Instagram on Sunday, showing off a pair of prosthetic breasts covering her chest.

Fineman then launched into a parody of the Novig ad, which featured Sweeney posing nude alongside an array of sporting equipment.

In her video, Fineman repeats the word “sports” over and over again — as Sweeney does in her ad — while a barrage of balls are thrown at her chest.

open image in gallery Outgoing ‘SNL’ star Chloe Fineman parodied Sydney Sweeney’s controversial new ad in a new social media skit ( chloeiscrazy/Instagram; Novig )

“Many people think this ad is about sports, but it’s actually about tits,” Fineman jokes.

She concludes the clip by breaking character, saying: “I don’t know, I got the boobs and I thought it would be funny. I know you’re probably uncomfortable, but I think they’re fun and cool.”

Fineman tagged Sweeney in the caption, writing: “SPORTS 🏀🏀 @sydney_sweeney. (took home my ‘practice sweeneys’ @nbcsnl hope that’s ok).”

In 2024, SNL’s Bowen Yang claimed Sweeney begged the cast to “make jokes about my boobs” when she hosted the show that year.

Since its release, Sweeney’s latest ad campaign has been criticized by some female athletes for “sexualizing” women’s sports.

open image in gallery Sweeney poses completely nude for Novig’s sports betting ad ( Novig )

open image in gallery The ‘Euphoria’ star is facing backlash from female athletes, some of whom have accused her of ‘sexualizing’ women’s sports ( Novig )

British Olympic runner Hannah Williams called it a “disgrace for women in sports” who are “constantly trying to be respected in a male dominated field,” while retired Australian Olympic swimmer Ariarne Titmus said she was “infuriated” by this “bulls***” marketing.

“The sexualisation of women in sport (and in life) is an ongoing issue that most (if not, all) women face,” wrote Olympic weightlifting coach Danielle Bagacay, adding: “I hope whatever Sydney Sweeney is trying to portray will be overshadowed by other women speaking/posting against the brand campaign.”

The 29-year-old has since hit back at critics on Instagram. On Sunday, she shared a series of Instagram Stories that highlighted female athletes who have posed nude in their careers.

Sweeney posted nude campaigns of Serena Williams, Ronda Rousey, Sue Bird, Megan Rapinoe and Caroline Wozniacki. She also highlighted male athletes who have done the same: Myles Garrett, Rob Gronokowski, Karl-Anthony Towns, and Jason Kelce.

In a statement, Sweeney said the campaign was “about embracing a fun idea.” She said: “The concept is simple: cut through the noise and put the focus entirely on sports. The campaign brings that idea to life with confidence, humour and a playful edge.”

The controversy follows a year on from Sweeney’s American Eagle “Great Jeans” campaign, which was heavily criticized for appearing to use the language of eugenics, with Sweeney saying in a now-deleted video: “Genes are passed down from parents to offspring, often determining traits like hair colour, personality, and even eye colour. My jeans are blue.”

In the subsequent months, the actor said she was “surprised” by the reaction, stating: “I’m against hate and divisiveness.”

Viking has floated out its second hydrogen-powered cruise ship, capable of operating without emitting carbon from its exhaust.

Viking Astrea took to the water for the first time at Fincantieri’s Ancona Shipyard last week.

The float out of the Viking Astrea began with a ceremonial cord-cutting, before water flowed into the dock.

It has now been moved to a nearby outfitting dock for the final construction and interior build-out.

Scheduled for delivery in May 2027, Astrea will join sister ship Viking Libra, which is set to become the world’s first hydrogen-powered cruise ship upon its November launch.

Viking Astrea, which has capacity for 998 guests, will spend its inaugural season sailing itineraries in the Mediterranean and northern Europe. Prices start from £1,995 per person.

Similar to Viking Libra, the vessel has a hybrid propulsion system designed by Isotta Fraschini Motori (IFM), Fincantieri’s subsidiary specialising in advanced fuel cell technology.

It uses liquified hydrogen to power a polymer electrolyte membrane fuel cell system, or PEM.

This provides the capacity to produce up to six megawatts of power and to sail with zero exhaust emissions during parts of a voyage.

There won’t be enough hydrogen to power a whole route but it will help the ship access more environmentally sensitive areas such as the Norwegian fjords.

Similar to the other ocean ships in the fleet,Viking Astrea has Nordic and Scandinavian design features throughout. Its staircases feature large replicas of the Bayeux Tapestry.

Leah Talactac, president and chief executive of Viking, said: “The float out of the Viking Astrea represents another important milestone for Viking,

“From the beginning, we have sought thoughtful ways to design more efficient ships, and the Viking Astrea is an important step forward in that ongoing effort.”

Other cruise lines are taking steps to operate with more lower emissions.

Hurtigruten completed a climate-neutral sailing in Norway using biodiesel in October 2025, and Havila Voyages sailed using biogas the following month in the region.

Havila Voyages’ ships also have battery packs that provide power for up to four hours.

The John F Kennedy Memorial Center for the Performing Arts in Washington, D.C., is facing “certain fiscal collapse” in a matter of weeks if President Donald Trump’s name is not restored to the front of the building, according to its leadership.

The New York Times and Washington Post both cite a 57-page draft resolution circulated to the venue’s board of trustees, which is chaired by Trump himself, ahead of a special meeting Tuesday, which warns it is facing bankruptcy and may soon be unable to pay staff or honor routine maintenance contracts.

The resolution reportedly reveals that the president has offered to help to raise the money needed to keep the institution open on the condition that he receives the “appropriate recognition” for doing so.

It then offers the trustees a choice of 10 inscriptions that might be added beneath the building’s name, one representative example of which reads: “Renovation Restoration and Endowment overseen by President Donald J Trump and the Trump Kennedy Center Fund.”

Norm Eisen and Nathaniel Zelinsky, lawyers for Ohio Democratic Rep. Joyce Beatty, who is leading the opposition to Trump’s rebranding, told the Post: “This constant effort to add Donald Trump’s name to the Kennedy Center facade is the definition of insanity.

open image in gallery The John F Kennedy Memorial Center for the Performing Arts in Washington, D.C., is facing ’certain fiscal collapse’ unless President Donald Trump’s can be restored to its exterior, its board has been warned ( Getty )

“This is now the third attempt to deface this sacred memorial and turn it into a vanity project for one man’s ego. Worse still, now Trump is taking the Center hostage and threatening to in effect kill it unless he gets his way. This has to stop.”

The Independent has reached out to the Kennedy Center and the White House for comment.

Trump first added his name to the Kennedy Center, which honors the assassinated 35th president, in December last year, leading to a sharp decline in ticket sales for its events and artists pulling out of scheduled engagements on political grounds.

In May, Washington, D.C., District Judge Christopher Cooper ruled that Congress had made it “crystal clear” the venue was only intended to memorialize Kennedy and “cannot bear any other formal name or public memorial” based on a “unilateral say-so.”

Cooper gave the center until June 12 to strip the current president’s name from its exterior but construction crews only started to assemble scaffolding to reach the letters that afternoon. Trump’s name plates were not removed until the early hours of the following morning.

Amid the ongoing legal wrangling, the Department of Justice has repeatedly warned the venue faces “financial ruin” unless his name remains in place.

“Many donors and companies, who have given, or will be giving, millions of dollars to the Center were only willing to do so with the name ‘Trump’ on the Building,” its lawyers wrote in one filing earlier this summer.

open image in gallery Trump’s name was removed from the venue in June by court order ( AFP/Getty )

“Without the name ‘Trump’ on the Building, our fundraising will not only come to a halt, but any and all monies raised or committed would be obligated to be returned, refunded, or terminated.”

The center’s board then voted on August 13 to reinstate Trump’s name and to close down for a two-year renovation, costing at least $250 million, which is not currently slated to happen until October 8, a month later than first planned.

The DOJ has also said the venue might have to be torn down altogether if a solution cannot be found to the controversy surrounding the president’s involvement.

Earlier this month, heavy rainfall caused a section of ceiling plaster to fall 60 feet into the building’s Grand Foyer, the debris landing near its Concert Hall entrance.

Fortunately, no one was hurt but the accident only reinforced calls for the center’s redevelopment in accordance with Trump’s wishes.

News.title: Hunter x Ganni brings a joyful twist to wet weather-ready heritage designs
News.content:
Hunter has revealed a collaboration with Ganni that brings the Danish brand’s joyful style to Hunter’s wet weather-ready heritage design. It isn’t the first time the Copenhagen designer has worked with British legacy brands – the Ganni stamp on Barbour’s classic wax jackets and quilted coats instantly comes to mind. This time though, you can expect a capsule that is made for the countryside as much as it is for the city.

Launched today (14 September), the collaboration includes three waterproof ponchos, rain hats, a protective poncho cover for the Ganni bou bag, tall and Chelsea-style Wellington boots, and an umbrella. Bringing some sunshine to gloomy days, the core colourways are bright yellow, shades of khaki, and, of course, Ganni’s signature leopard print.

“Hunter is such an iconic British brand, and bringing its legacy together with Ganni’s Copenhagen perspective feels like a very exciting conversation between two worlds,” said Ganni’s creative director, Ditte Reffstrup. “I love the idea that the most practical pieces can also be the most expressive.”

Known for its practical, high quality outwear made for the British weather, the 170-year-old heritage brand Hunter has cemented its place as a sought-after label beyond with the likes of Alex Chung, Daisy Edgar-Jones and Olivia Rodgigo following in Kate Moss’s footsteps in choosing the wellies for festival, in particular Glastonbury, style.

The collaboration brings another imagination to the Hunter’s designs as it merges its technical weatherproof materials with playful proportions and bold colours. As it goes live on the Ganni website, this is what to shop.



Hunter x Ganni poncho in 10K waterproof shell The collection features a waterproof poncho in lemon yellow, khaki and leopard print, meaning your raincoat will never be boring again. It’s not just style over substance either, as the 10K waterproofing means it can handle moderate to heavy rain while remaining cool to wear. All three coats in the range feature a front pocket, poppers and a hood which you can tighten, and have a triangular shape for an oversized look. Read more £330 from Ganni.com Prices may vary Hunter x Ganni downpour tall boots There are two styles of downpour tall boots in the collection – one in leopard print and one in green. The downpour tall boot is one of Hunter’s latest boot styles, which feature a lightweight outsole and a voluminous calf fit. The Ganni spin sees a stylish buckle side fastening and splashes of colour detailing on the rubber and edges. Read more £210 from Ganni.com Prices may vary Hunter x Ganni water resistant bucket hat A festival necessity, a bucket hat also features in the collection. There are three different styles to choose from – a full leopard print, leopard and yellow, and a khaki green – meaning there’s something to suit every style. Plus, each one fits oversized, in true Ganni style, and can be fastened with fun chin straps. Read more £110 from Ganni.com Prices may vary Hunter x Ganni Balmoral ankle boot The short boot from the collaboration is a new style of wellie for Hunter which feels city appropriate. The Balmoral ankle boot comes in leopard and brown, and features a neoprene upper and layers of coloured rubber on top of its thick base. Read more £310 from Ganni.com Prices may vary Hunter x Ganni water resistant bag poncho The most affordable piece from the collection, the water resistant bag poncho is a cover specifically created for the Ganni bou bag, so the usability is a little limited. While I can’t be sure, if you have a mini bag with similar sized curved handles, it might work for you. A segment of border wall erected in late July stands incomplete along the edge of a wildlife refuge in Alamo, Texas, after a lawsuit halted work.

Lush public land in the Santa Ana National Wildlife Refuge is a corridor for hundreds of thousands of birds and butterflies migrating to South America. Visitors glimpse rare species, walk trails and take in views from an iconic suspended bridge.

The refuge is home to armadillos, warblers, bats, snakes and two endangered cat species that run through its over 2,000 acres (about 809 hectares). An irrigation canal hugs the northern perimeter of the refuge, connecting water with farmland in this agriculture hub.

Border Patrol agents working the dense foliage patrol the park on bicycles and set up a rescue beacon with a push button that signals to them if anyone needs to be rescued, though it’s mostly used by hikers who get lost on the winding trails. Border walls are part of the landscape built under the Bush and Obama administrations to deter illegal crossings.

In late July, the Trump administration began erecting more wall — but Hidalgo County Irrigation District No. 2, which manages a canal near the refuge, filed a lawsuit last month saying the construction company entered its property without consent and began dumping “significant dirt” into its canal. An order paused construction until mid-October and remains in litigation.

The lawsuit is one of several attempting to stop construction along protected or public lands as the administration races ahead with efforts to build a $46 billion wall along the U.S.-Mexico border from the Pacific Ocean to the Gulf of Mexico. A lawsuit failed last month to halt the construction in Presidio, Texas after arguing the wall could cause flooding problems.

Construction in Southern Arizona in late August pressed forward through a Native American tribe's reservation in spite of objections. In West Texas, construction in Big Bend National Park drew public outrage from both sides of the political aisle.

All our reviewers are either resident destination experts or travel writers that specialise in hotels. Often they will have stayed at a hotel many times and so can see how it has changed for better or worse over the years. When our reviewers first visit a hotel, they stay for at least one night, eat one meal in addition to breakfast and will experience all of the facilities on offer. News.title: ‘Your home is your palace’: Queen Elizabeth II’s housekeeper answers reader questions
News.content:
Was there one surprisingly simple trick used in the palace that made things feel instantly more polished?

Jay, West Midlands

Making sure you have a routine is the best way for everything to feel polished. At the palace, the team is trained, and everyone has the right tools and time to do their job... They learned how to lift things safely and how to be confident when they were around the Royal Collection. When you’re cleaning historic areas such as palaces and castles, you have to make sure you don’t overdo it. We had a daily routine that ensured we didn’t over-clean everything.

What is the royal protocol for dealing with ironing and maintaining perfectly crisp sheets without using harsh, eco-unfriendly chemicals?

Saleem, London

Much of what would be classed as royal protocol are things we would do in our own homes. For linen, you need to treat it well and look after it by not washing it at too high a temperature or using too much detergent. Make sure the products you’re using are eco-friendly, not only for the environment, but also to care for the linen. For historic linen, it needs to be handled very gently, as it can tear quite easily.

Did the Queen get involved in any of the details of housekeeping?

Peter, East of England

I was very blessed. The Queen did leave it up to me to make those decisions because she trusted me to keep her home and the other royal residences clean and up to a great standard. I kept in touch with her, making sure the team was involved. We would have regular update meetings to ensure everyone knew what was happening and when. There was planned cleaning throughout the year depending on what was occurring, making sure certain areas were protected or closed off, for example.

I would feel very stressed cleaning around objects of great value, history and sentiment. How do you avoid disasters?

Catherine, North West

It’s important the team feels confident when cleaning those areas. We achieve that through training and building their confidence.

In the castle, we introduced a cleaning schedule that covered different areas within the state apartments – and it meant that we didn’t over-clean. The structure of this schedule was important. Every day, we would ensure we vacuumed and damp-dusted; there were no actual chemicals or any what I call “wet chemicals”. On a Monday, for instance, we would clean vases. On a Tuesday, we would do the fireplaces. On a Wednesday, it would be light fittings.

It’s crucial the team is given the right amount of time to clean, so that they don’t feel rushed or stressed. But we also have to remember that accidents happen. And if an accident happens and it was just an accident, then what can you do? It’s just one of those things.

Ultimately, making sure people are trained and confident is the key.

With limited time, what are the housekeeping priorities?

David, South West

My housekeeping priorities when at home are to make things look really tidy quickly. Putting your newspapers away, fluffing the cushions up, tidying the curtains, making sure your washing is cleared and the dishwasher is on – these are all things that will make a big difference, even if you haven’t had time to get your mop or vacuum out.

When are you satisfied a room is clean?

D, North West

I am quite a hard taskmaster and I do like perfection, but equally, that comes with making sure people understand the guidelines and what’s expected of them, after being trained properly.

I like to be visible and around the team, showing them what I’m looking at. I would get them to sit on a toilet and then shut the door, so they could see what’s behind the door – or sit in the bath, because that way you can see what other people are seeing when they’re using it. If you’re cleaning and rushing around, you don’t always see those little details.

News.title: Woeful Man Utd have no excuses, Carrick is under big pressure
News.content:
Afterwards Haaland talked about City’s “personality, character” and that was exactly what United lacked. They did not adapt a tactical plan to combat 10-man City’s desire to keep their wingers high and wide, and break with intent and still try and attack.

It was telling that so little did City’s new head coach Enzo Maresca worry about United that he did not add a defensive player, and when he took off Rayan Cherki at half-time, he replaced him with the equally creative Iliman Ndiaye who impressed. Maresca knew United needed space to run in behind and denied them that. It was that simple.

City also struck the post with United goalkeeper Senne Lammens tipping an Enzo Fernández shot against the frame of the goal, and the visitors were worthy winners as they preserved their perfect start to the season to draw level on points with leaders, Arsenal.

City handled the occasion and the – admittedly toothless – opposition superbly under their new head coach and will clearly be Arsenal’s closest challengers this season.

Maresca delivered a masterclass. For Carrick? This was a disasterclass. An object lesson in how not to use a man-advantage. And now United will have to endure even more City songs after being outplayed at home like this.

Was it complacency? Was it inability? Was it a damning lack of courage, confidence, belief even? On the pitch and in the dugout United were far too passive. This was not how a big team plays and Carrick needs to wake up.

The former midfielder did so well last season to guide United into Champions League qualification but so far this campaign he has given the impression that his job is done. Rather than that the real work starts now.

News.title: Redemption Sunday for Hull and Woad as Europe reclaim Solheim Cup
News.content:
The quiet but steely 22-year-old, who everyone seemed to have forgotten was a rookie, punched her fist when she held the decisive two-footer, before the customary hug with opponent Auston Kim and then being mobbed by her team.

“This was really important,” Woad said. “I mean, I was pretty disappointed and felt like I was kind of letting everyone down. Then the captain kind of spoke to me and said that I was third on [the most] birdies [made]. So I just had to trust that and that’s golf sometimes. And it ended up I got the winning putt.”

Some will claim that Woad was only the match-winner on a technicality. Carlota Ciganda in the penultimate game had not finished off her win against Jennifer Kupcho, but when Woad tapped in, the Spaniard was three up with three to go and was guaranteed a half. So the acclaim Woad received was granted. Not that anyone in the Europe camp cared.

The previous evening they had returned to their team room feeling slightly down that they did not hold the advantage, Kupcho holing a 91-footer on the 17th and a 30-footer on the 18th to deny Ciganda and Céline Boutier. And their mood was not helped when videos appeared on social media of the Americans taking crates of beer on to the bus back to their hotel. Yet that foolish scenario only offered extra incentive. “At least we’ll be the ones taking crates of beer on to our bus this evening,” Mel Reid, the assistant captain, said quite pointedly.

News.title: Lando Norris fumes at virtual safety car rules for costing him Spanish GP win
News.content:
Welcome to our live coverage for the 2026 Spanish Grand Prix, the first time the race has been held at the all-new, purpose-built street circuit, the Madring. The track has developed a reputation in its short life for being a bit of a tricky one. Some have gone so far as to call it a “car killer”? Is it living up to that reputation? Probably, especially if you look at some of the lower formulae that have run on it.

It has also increasingly become the case for the Formula One cars, too. The first couple of practice sessions on Friday revealed little to worry about. As the drivers began to push, though, from final practice and qualifying, the mistakes and crashes happened. The biggest so far was Oliver Bearman but also a smaller one for Lewis Hamilton.

There will almost certainly be some kind of incident in the race, but whether we see red flags, safety cars and so on remains to be seen. A bigger and perhaps more significant question will be how much overtaking will take place on this track. The drivers are not optimistic. The theory goes that if tyre degradation is high then there will be, because you will have significant pace offsets between worn and fresh tyres. The problem is that the leaders tend not to differ to greatly from one another on strategy these days...

Perhaps George Russell, who qualified down in sixth and has little to lose, will be brave and put on a set of hard tyres to start with. Russell has work to do yet again. He was not miles off Antonelli in qualifying when it came to pace, but given how close it was in the top six, finds four cars between himself and the championship leader, who just missed out on pole to McLaren’s Lando Norris.

Norris said it was the best lap of his life and seemed to come from nowhere. He improved more than a second from Q2 to Q3 and continues his fine form in 2026. He will start alongside Antonelli with Max Verstappen in third, Lewis Hamilton in fourth and Charles Leclerc in fifth, before Russell.

News.title: Tora Bora’s last midwife struggles under Taliban rule as aid runs dry
News.content:
The small clinic, crowded with pregnant women, sits in the shadow of Tora Bora in eastern Afghanistan. Twenty-five years ago, those mountains commanded the attention of the world’s most powerful military. Roughly 15 miles from the clinic, in the Tora Bora cave complex, Osama bin Laden was believed to be hiding as American bombs rained down in the hunt for the architect of 9/11.

Today, another consequence of the West’s long entanglement with Afghanistan is playing out beneath those same mountains – in the struggle to keep mothers and babies alive.

In the baking courtyard of Gandab Kharoti health centre, dozens of women enveloped in sapphire blue burqas sit shoulder to shoulder beneath trees waiting to see Shila Ibrahimi, a 27-year-old midwife.

The women rest against walls, dusty, barefoot children play, and mothers cradle sick babies beneath folds of cloth. Some have walked for hours through the mountains to reach her.

Among them is Fawzia, 30, seven-and-a-half months pregnant with her seventh child. Suffering from headaches, she has walked for miles through the heat.

Her husband works far from the village, so she makes the journey with her children and mother-in-law, hoping the Taliban do not stop her for the “crime” of travelling without a male escort.

Under the Taliban’s morality rules, women face restrictions on travelling alone, while UN monitors have documented the regime’s morality inspectors ordering some health facilities not to treat unaccompanied women.

But enforcement varies and Fawzia says nobody challenged her on her journey here. Asked where she would give birth if the clinic closed she says: “We have nowhere else to go. We cannot afford that. We are poor.”

News.title: Springboks look like World Cup champions elect… again
News.content:
In doing so, Erasmus while still relying on his veteran performers, managed to expose some of the next generation to invaluable white heat pressure, including Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu, Morne van den Berg and Cameron Hanekom, who all look to the manor born.

And the substance of the series victory is heightened by the fact it came against a regenerated and rejuvenated All Blacks side, who rediscovered their high-octane and relentless attacking identity under new coach Dave Rennie. At times the handling and precision of the All Blacks were so sumptuous that it felt like they might be in a position to level the series in Baltimore.

But the narrative of the previous two Tests continued. At key moments they were let down by their discipline and turnovers in attack to gift the Springboks’ transition ball, and their directness, backed by their power both in collisions and set piece enabled them to pick up points much more easily than their opponents.

At the end, the scoreboard ran away from the All Blacks, which was harsh on them. But one had wondered if they would be able to maintain their intensity at the end of the first half, when it took 32 phases for Will Jordan to score a try to cut the deficit to three points.

News.title: Sabalenka smashes racket and swears at cameraman after Rybakina clinches US Open
News.content:
Sabalenka and Rybankina have now played four slam finals, with the spoils evenly shared after this 6-4, 5-7, 6-2 grapple in the Apple – as a boxing promoter might have referred to it.

There is certainly something pugilistic about the way these two go toe-to-toe. The emphasis is on landing the first blow, so the rallies tend not to be particularly long: only four points out of 193 went beyond nine shots. But the precision of the ball-striking was breathtaking. At one point in the first set, Rybakina had hit eight winners to just a single unforced error – the sort of ratio to send coaches starry-eyed.

Sabalanka arrived on court in her showy jewellery – which is worth more than £300,000 for the full set, according to the manufacturers – and an orange Nike dress that put one in mind of the Dutch national football team. “Total tennis” may have been the goal, but sometimes your opponent doesn’t allow you to play. This was the case in the early stages as Rybakina – whose own yellow-and-black outfit evoked the natural warning signs of a wasp or hornet – seemed to flush every ball right out of the centre of her racket.

Sabalenka actually did a sterling job of digging herself out of trouble in her service games, saving four of five break points in the first set. But this still wasn’t enough, given that Rybakina was defending her own serve with the same serenity that characterises everything she does.

Sports.title: Ex-Arsenal flop backed for sensational Real Madrid move - ‘He’s got everything’
Sports.content:
Ex-Arsenal flop backed for sensational Real Madrid move - ‘He’s got everything’

Nuno Tavares left Arsenal permanently in 2025 following a difficult period in North London and the defender has now been touted for big things having shone for Lazio

View 2 Images Nuno Tavares left Arsenal in 2025 (Image: Getty Images)

Legendary former midfielder Gennaro Gattuso has claimed that ex-Arsenal star Nuno Tavares would be good enough to play for Real Madrid. The Portuguese defender currently plies his trade under Gattuso at Lazio, having signed for the club permanently following an initial loan move.

‌



Tavares, 26, has gone on to make 62 appearances for the Italian giants and has teed up 11 goals. His form in Italy is at odds with his spell in North London, having made just 28 appearances for Arsenal following his arrival from Benfica.

‌



Tavares is potentially more well known for being hauled off after just 34 minutes in an FA Cup clash with Nottingham Forest.

‌



Speaking at the time, Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta said: “Today was just a tactical reason for how I wanted to do it with what Palace was doing and how we could attack and control the game much better in that position.

“We wanted to put another attacking midfielder with Emile in that space and that was the only reason. I’m sorry that it was Nuno again, but we had to do it.”

And Arsenal fans might now be baffled to hear that he has been tipped for a stunning move to Real Madrid. Speaking at the weekend, Lazio boss Gattuso said: “I always said that Tavares is worthy of Real Madrid. He feels like someone who lost his parents young, received a big inheritance, and in five years it went up in smoke.

“This is a player who ought to be at Real Madrid. He’s got everything it takes, he has pace, right foot, left foot. He is unusual, but after a match he needs his time to recover, but he’s a good lad, you need to get into his head and make him understand.

‌



“He knows he has talent and could’ve had 10/12 years at Real Madrid with his qualities. You’ve just got to get him to understand.”

View 2 Images Tavares has shone in his time with Lazio (Image: Getty Images)

Tavares joined Arsenal from Portuguese giants Benfica and made 28 appearances in his debut campaign. He was then allowed to join French side Marseille the following campaign and he shone in Ligue 1, scoring six goals in 31 outings.

Article continues below

His next port of call was back in the Premier League with Nottingham Forest but he made just 12 appearances in all competitions throughout the season, before his eventual switch to Lazio.

Tavares was actually linked with a move away from the Italian side this summer, news that would have been welcomed by Arsenal given they are worth a share of any fee that Lazio receive, having written a sell-on clause into the deal.

Sports.title: Phil Foden branded 'stupid' for Bruno Fernandes kick as Wayne Rooney agrees on red card verdict
Sports.content:
Phil Foden branded 'stupid' for Bruno Fernandes kick as Wayne Rooney agrees on red card verdict

Phil Foden was sent off in the Manchester derby after an incident involving Bruno Fernandes

View 2 Images Phil Foden of Manchester City was sent off in the first half of the Manchester derby (Image: Carl Recine/Getty Images)

Wayne Rooney and Danny Murphy were in agreement with their verdicts on Phil Foden's red card for Manchester City in the Manchester derby. The England international was sent off during City’s 1-0 win over the Red Devils in the Premier League clash at Old Trafford on Sunday afternoon.

‌



Foden was given his marching orders by referee Michael Oliver in the 23rd minute of the match on Sunday, leaving City to play the vast majority of the fixture with 10 men.

‌



Oliver sent Foden off after the City star attempted to kick United captain Bruno Fernandes, but Enzo Maresca's side still managed to claim a victory thanks to a controversial goal from Erling Haaland.

‌



Fernandes, by contrast, escaped punishment despite seemingly kicking Foden while attempting to regain possession, an incident that occurred just moments before the City star was dismissed.

Wayne Rooney calls for VAR to be SCRAPPED after Pro Ref issue Man Utd apology READ MORE :

Phil Foden taunts Man Utd fans as he leaves Old Trafford after Manchester derby sending off READ MORE :

Rooney and Murphy featured on Match of the Day where Foden's sending-off became a topic of debate, and the ex-Liverpool midfielder believes that yellow cards for both Foden and Fernandes would have been the fairest resolution.

"I don't think they both should have [been sent off]," Murphy said. "Look, we could talk all day about this. Nobody would have batted an eyelid if they both got a yellow and a telling off for silly petulance and little stupid kick-outs.

‌



"They're not dangerous, I don't think.

"When you slow it down, you see the original foul from Fernandes. He gives him a little nudge with his foot while he's on the floor but Foden's foot is high and above the waist, which I think then gives the referee the idea to give him the red because it seems more dangerous.

"I don't think in this day and age you should be taking that risk, what is he thinking? Why has he done that?"

‌



Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Rooney shared Murphy's view, setting out why he believes Foden should not have received his marching orders, and that both the City midfielder and Fernandes should have been cautioned.

‌



"I can see why they give the red card, but I just think as a football fan you don't want to see a red card for that," Rooney said.

"You look at it there and think he hasn't kicked him with any force, he's almost just brushed him with the side of his leg, he hasn't gone in with the studs where he's really going to hurt him.

"I think the sensible decision is two yellows."

‌



View 2 Images Phil Foden has been told why his challenge on Bruno Fernandes was "stupid" (Image: Catherine Ivill - AMA/Getty Images)

Murphy proceeded to describe Foden's decision to retaliate against Fernandes as "stupid", while maintaining the incident did not warrant a dismissal.

"It wasn't ferocious, there wasn't speed to it, it was the side of his leg," Murphy added.

Article continues below

"I just think now with the cameras, with the VAR and the refs initiative to cut that type of thing out - you are rolling a dice if you do it, and he's [Foden] been stupid."

Sports.title: Ludek Miklosko dies aged 64 as West Ham pay tribute to club legend with iconic chant
Sports.content:
Ludek Miklosko dies aged 64 as West Ham pay tribute to club legend with iconic chant

Ludek Miklosko has sadly died after a battle with cancer and tributes have been pouring in for the West Ham icon

View 3 Images West Ham United have paid a touching tribute to Ludek Miklosko following his death aged 64 (Image: (Photo by Richard Pelham/Getty Images))

West Ham United legend Ludek Miklosko has died aged 64 following a battle with cancer. The club's former goalkeeper was diagnosed with the illness back in 2021 after discovering a small lump on his hip with the decision made a few years later to stop treatment after the cancer also spread to his stomach.

‌



During the 1990s, he made nearly 400 appearances for the Hammers which saw him become a hugely popular figure within the fanbase.

‌



For the last few years, he has been sporting director at Czech Republic side FC Banik Ostrava, who were among many to pay tribute on social media. He has also managed to attend a number of important West Ham over the last few years with their tribute particularly touching.

‌



The article on their club website read: "Everyone at West Ham United is deeply saddened by the passing of Ludek Miklosko at the age of 64, following a courageous battle with cancer.

"The hugely popular former goalkeeper, known fondly as ‘Ludo’ to the Claret and Blue Army, made 373 appearances for the club during eight years as No1 between 1990 and 1997.

View 3 Images Ludek Miklosko was West Ham's goalkeeper for eight years

‌



"The incredible impact he had on the club and the fondness with which he is remembered is heard every matchday, when supporters sing his iconic ‘My name is Ludek Miklosko, I come from near Moscow, I play in goal for West Ham’ chant.

"Miklosko was born in the small city of Prostejov, in what was then Czechoslovakia and is now the present-day Czechia, in December 1961.

"He started his career as a schoolboy with Baník Ostrava and, after spending two years with RH Cheb while on national service, Miklosko returned to Baník and spent nine seasons keeping goal for the Czechoslovak First League club.

‌



"During the 1980s, Miklosko also became a regular member of the Czechoslovakia national team, making his debut in a friendly win in Denmark in 1982 and going on to win 40 caps.

"In 1989, as change swept through the former Soviet Union, Czechoslovakia experienced the Velvet Revolution and, after the former Communist country transitioned into a parliamentary republic, previous restrictions on Czechs and Slovaks to live and work abroad were removed.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



"The following month, Miklosko was invited for a trial at West Ham United, who had been relegated to the Second Division and were in need of talented players to boost their promotion bid. The big goalkeeper was one of them and he signed for a bargain £300,000 fee. Even then, though, with the European map being redrawn almost by the day, he would have to wait two months for the British Government to issue him with a work permit.

"When it was granted, in February 1990, Miklosko moved to London and kicked-off a career that no West Ham supporter will ever forget.

"In 1991, at the end of his first full season, he was voted Hammer of the Year and into the PFA Second Division Team of the Year as he helped Billy Bonds’ Irons win promotion to the top-flight.

‌



"Over his time at the Boleyn Ground, Miklosko enjoyed winning two promotions, reached the semi-finals of both the FA Cup and Football League Cup, made hundreds of miraculous saves, and famously frustrated Sir Alex Ferguson when his man-of-the-match performance prevented Manchester United winning the Premier League title in 1995.

"In 1996/97, he made two farewell appearances for Czechia, before departing West Ham for Queens Park Rangers in 1998. He retired from playing in 2001 and returned to Chadwell Heath to take up the role as Hammers goalkeeping coach, which he fulfilled with safe hands until 2010.

"A hugely popular figure, an enduring image of Miklosko was taken in May 2005, when he carried injured goalkeeper Jimmy Walker around the pitch at Cardiff’s Millennium Stadium following the Irons’ Championship Play-Off final victory.

‌



View 3 Images Ludek Miklosko has passed away

"Miklosko returned home and worked with a sports agency developing young players, before returning to Baník Ostrava in 2022 as a Board member and Sporting Director.

"In June 2023, he joined his fellow Hammers in Prague as West Ham defeated Fiorentina to win the UEFA Conference League, and was moved to tears as the Claret and Blue Army sang his famous song at a fan zone in the Czech capital’s Letna Park.

Article continues below

"Ludek’s last visit to see his beloved Hammers came in December 2024, when he was Guest of Honour at London Stadium for our fixture against Liverpool, having confirmed publicly that he was taking the brave decision to withdraw from further treatment in his battle against cancer.

"Since then, his famous song has been sung at every single match, and in February this year a stunning tifo was displayed by Hammers fans in honour of the giant goalkeeper who will forever hold a special place in the hearts of the West Ham family.

"Everyone at West Ham United would like to extend their sincere condolences to Ludek’s family and loved ones and this very sad time."

Sports.title: Liverpool news: Florian Wirtz question emerges as Andoni Iraola lays blame
Sports.content:
Liverpool news: Florian Wirtz question emerges as Andoni Iraola lays blame

The fallout from Liverpool's underwhelming 0-0 draw with Fulham continues

View 3 Images Florian Wirtz has come in for criticism from some quarters (Image: Images)

If there ever was a game to symbolise Liverpool's current status as a work in progress, then Saturday's 0-0 draw against Fulham would be it. Andoni Iraola's team may still be unbeaten but the stalemate marked their third draw of the season.

‌



Listless in attack and struggling to dictate the tempo in the middle of the park, it was certainly an afternoon to forget at Anfield. Florian Wirtz has been on the receiving end of criticism ever since he arrived at Liverpool last season, for failing to live up to his lofty billing.

‌



Today's Liverpool news sees the German star take more flak after he failed to help the Reds against Fulham. Elsewhere, Iraola has identified just why the Reds were found wanting in the disappointing draw.

‌



Florian Wirtz question raised

Florian Wirtz has found himself at the centre of criticism again following the 0-0 draw with Fulham. Wirtz cost Liverpool an initial £100million, with a further £16m in add-ons, last summer.

He scored seven goals and bagged 10 assists across 49 appearances in all competitions last season, in a team that struggled under ex-manager Arne Slot.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



Liverpool captain Virgil van Dijk holds meeting with boss to decide future READ MORE :

This season, in five appearances, he has one assist to his name. Against Fulham, he struggled to display his quality, registering three shots with none on target. The German created two chances.

talkSPORT pundits Jason Cundy and Jamie O’Hara have targeted the Liverpool No. 10. As of September 4, a WhoScored stat claimed Wirtz has lost possession 53 times this season, more than any other player in the Premier League. O'Hara took issue with Wirtz's ability to hold onto the ball.

He said: “You know the problem I have with him? I can accept him adapting to the physical side of the game, and it takes time, right, but to then watch him, he’s getting the ball in space and giving it away.

‌



View 3 Images Florian Wirtz has started all four of Liverpool's games this season

“And it has nothing to do with the physicality of the Premier League. And I am watching and going, ‘Stop giving it away’.”

Cundy added: “Wirtz has been here now, right, this is his second season. I am not convinced that Wirtz is going to be a success. I think I might have seen enough.”

‌



Iraola has defended the star. “He played very well against Atletico Madrid,” the Liverpool boss said ahead of the Fulham game. “The game against Ipswich in the second half he lost more balls than normal but overall I have been very happy with his performances.

“He is a good player out of possession who helps us in our press. But he runs the same as the 10 of Arsenal, the 10 of (Manchester) City, the 10 of Fulham and more or less his stats are very similar to the number 10s other teams have.”

Iraola places the blame

Iraola admitted Liverpool were lacking in forward areas against the Coattagers on Saturday afternoon. The Reds fielded an array of attacking talent, costing nearly £400m, as Alexander Isak, Bradley Barcola, Victor Munoz and Florian Wirtz all started together in the Premier League for the first time.

‌



All four were guilty of spurning chances. Afterwards, Iraola claimed his misfiring stars were the reason Liverpool came up short at Anfield.

“I think what was lacking, I think it was quite clear,” he said. “It's the first game since I'm here, I think, that we've had problems to create chances, to score goals, to make the difference offensively.

“And that's the main reason. That we couldn't create as many chances as we wanted and we haven't scored a goal, and that's why we come away with just with one point.

‌



View 3 Images Liverpool's frontline drew a blank against Fulham (Image: 2026 Getty Images)

“In the end, it's the easiest one (reason) for me, for you, for everyone. Because our players were tired. I think there is a lack of freshness, definitely. There is, we cannot hide it.

“I think it's the worst turnaround in terms of, I think 60-something hours between the games after a very big game the other day. But this is going to happen more times, maybe with one more day, maybe, but sometimes it's going to happen the same way during the season, and we have to adapt to these circumstances.

Article continues below

“And it's these kind of games that you need to win, sometimes with a set play, sometimes with a shot from the edge, sometimes from a moment of brilliance from the offensive players, and we haven't had today. We've been clearly not as good offensively as we've been other days.”
