Sports.title: Man Utd sent painful reminder in Manchester derby defeat as Enzo Maresca gets huge boost
Sports.content:
Man Utd sent painful reminder in Manchester derby defeat as Enzo Maresca gets huge boost

MANCHESTER UNITED 0-1 MANCHESTER CITY: Erling Haaland scored the goal to settle a derby which will be remembered for its controversies rather than the action on the pitch between two great rivals

View 3 Images Erling Haaland gave 10-man Manchester City victory in the derby (Image: Getty Images)

The chant from the away end was pretty damning. “We’ve only got 10 men.”

‌



Manchester City had one player less than United for more than an hour and still beat their great rivals on their own patch. That only serves to highlight the gap between the two Manchester giants. It was no wonder that, at the final whistle, loud boos rang around Old Trafford because the United faithful were so fed-up.

‌



The game was shrouded in controversy from the moment Phil Foden was sent off after just 23 minutes after lashing out at United captain Bruno Fernandes. Even City’s goal did not feel right. Erling Haaland smashed the ball in the net but this was all about whether Enzo Fernandez was interfering with play and stopped Lisandro Martinez playing the ball.

‌



Fernandez was miles offside but was deemed not to be interfering with play. The whole of the football world felt as if the officials, referee Michael Oliver and the VAR team, got it wrong. But only their decision counts.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



And yet, let’s be clear, even with a big slice of fortune, you still cannot lose at home to your neighbours when they only had ten men. United hit the woodwork twice, Bryan Mbeumo was denied by Gianluigi Donnarumma in the 95th minute.

But United were simply not good enough. Just lumping the ball into the box in desperation. They could not find a way through because they lacked quality and guile.

This was the fixture last season which proved to be Michael Carrick’s starting point. Carrick was brought in as a caretaker, he beat City in his opening game and the momentum carried them into the Champions League places. But passion and legendary status gets you so far. They have made a dodgy start to the campaign, the Carrick feel good factor has ebbed away and now it feels they are back to square one.

‌



Meanwhile, City are on the up. Elliot Anderson, City’s £116m summer signing who chose the Etihad over Old Trafford, was comfortably the best player on the pitch.

View 3 Images Man United had a numerical advantage for more than an hour after Phil Foden was sent off (Image: Catherine Ivill/AMA)

Anderson was incredible in front of England boss Thomas Tuchel in the stands. Then, at the final whistle, Enzo Maresca went over to the away end - including celebrity fan Liam Gallagher - and punched the air and celebrated in style.

‌



Maresca rarely showed such passion while in charge at Chelsea but is quickly finding his feet in the impossible job taking over from Pep Guardiola. Four wins out of four. What a start. It did not look like that would be possible when Foden got his marching orders. Foden snapped and kicked out at Fernandes, who kicked him first. Why on earth Fernandes got away scot free is anyone’s guess.

But referee Oliver had no hesitation and sent off Foden who now has more red cards (one) than goals in 2026. There is no way he gets back into the England squad anytime soon.

Marcus Rashford and Robbie Mainoo both hit the woodwork either side of half time. City sent on Iliman Ndiaye for Rayan Cherki for his work rate. Ndiaye just typified City’s determination.

‌



View 3 Images Enzo Maresca has hit the ground running at City (Image: Michael Regan/Getty Images)

The goal came after an hour. Josko Gvradiol’s cross was deflected by Patrick Dorgu who played Haaland onside. But Fernandez was yards ahead and clearly impacted on Martinez’s ability to clear the danger before the ball reached Haaland.

The officials have had a stinker. Haaland thumped into the net, celebrated and then got a second chance to celebrate when VAR allowed it to stand.

‌



United piled forward but with little imagination. Mbeumo should have scored at the death. But his wayward finishing - and a brilliant save - just typified United’s sloppiness.

This was a crash landing for United and Carrick. But it feels like lift-off for Maresca’s City.

Sports.title: Gary Neville calls for officials to apologise over Erling Haaland's controversial goal
Sports.content:
Gary Neville calls for officials to apologise over Erling Haaland's controversial goal

Erling Haaland's goal settled the Manchester Derby for City, but Enzo Fernandez's offside position and attempt to play the ball has sparked fury among the pundits

View 2 Images Gary Neville was confused by the decision (Image: The Gary Neville Podcast/Sky Sports)

Gary Neville has demanded an apology from Pro Ref after Erling Haaland's controversial goal settled the Manchester Derby. Haaland's strike saw 10-man Manchester City win at Old Trafford in a match shrouded in debate.

‌



The City striker's goal from Josko Gvardiol's deflected cross was initially ruled out for offside before VAR overturned the on-field decision. Haaland was played onside by Patrick Dorgu, but Enzo Fernandez was in an offside position when the ball passed him and the City midfield made an attempt to head it in front of Lisandro Martinez.

‌



Explaining the decision, the Premier League Match Centre wrote: "VAR checked the referee’s call of no goal for offside – and determined that Haaland was in an onside position and recommended that the goal was awarded. The VAR also deemed that while in an offside position, Fernandez didn’t play the ball."

‌



Neville was confused by the call while on co-commentary duties for Sky Sports. "The officials will be nervous about this goal," Neville said. "When they look back on this, they will recognise they got this wrong.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

"The question is does Fernandez, who is offside, stop Martinez getting the ball? He does."

‌



After hearing the explanation, he added: "They're the words that I think – emphatically – means we will see an apology from Pro Ref.

"There is no doubt that Enzo is attempting to play the ball and putting Lisandro Martinez off. It’s a really strange one. They’ll recognise they got that wrong."

Neville did concede that "Manchester City have been very good" but reiterated that there should be "a massive inquest into the goal which I think was wrongly given."

‌



View 2 Images Erling Haaland's goal was allowed to stand

The former Manchester United defender was far from the only pundit to question the decision. Wayne Rooney said on the BBC: "Surely it's offside. Martinez is impacted by Enzo's movement, and he is offside."

Replying to the Premier League Match Centre's explanation, Rio Ferdinand wrote on X: "Enzo Fernandez not played the ball?" He then shared a screengrab of Fernandez stretching to try and head the ball.

‌



Ferdinand then posted: "Martinez has to go defend the man nearest the goal whether he believes he’s offside or not. In split seconds, you make the decision. He goes to defend Fernandez - who then attempts to play the ball. Deluded from VAR!"

Ex-Manchester City defender Micah Richards said on Sky Sports: "I think it's been a bad day for referees, it's been a bad day for VAR. I think they got the Phil Foden decision wrong on 23 minutes and they got this decision wrong.

"How can you say that Enzo Fernandez is not challenging for the ball?! I've been in that situation as a defender and any slight movement can make the difference between going for the ball or not. Of course it affects it! I just think they've got it so wrong."

Sports.title: Fuming Lisandro Martinez hits out at 'injustice' after controversial Man Utd decision
Sports.content:
Fuming Lisandro Martinez hits out at 'injustice' after controversial Man Utd decision

The Manchester United defender made his feelings clear when addressing Erling Haaland's winning goal, which was allowed to stand after initially being flagged for offside

View Image Lisandro Martinez was visibly fuming after the game

Manchester United defender Lisandro Martinez hit out at what he called an 'injustice' after Erling Haaland's opener was initially ruled offside during the Manchester derby. Martinez was positioned between Enzo Fernandez and Haaland, but the Argentine launched himself toward the ball in an attempt to meet it with a diving header.

‌



Following a lengthy VAR review, it was determined that the Manchester City striker was onside and that Fernandez, despite standing in an offside position, had not played the ball, with Martinez defending behind him. Josko Gvardiol's shot deflected off Patrick Dorgu towards the back post, where the Norwegian finished smartly.

‌



A tweet from the Premier League Match Centre said: "#MUNMCI – 59’ VAR OVERTURN. VAR checked the referee’s call of no goal for offside – and determined that Haaland was in an onside position and recommended that the goal was awarded. The VAR also deemed that while in an offside position, Fernandez didn’t play the ball."

‌



Wayne Rooney slams Manchester derby VAR call as Man Utd left furious READ MORE :

The rules state that an opponent will be penalised for interfering with play if they clearly attempt to play a nearby ball in a way that impacts an opponent, or if they make an obvious action that affects an opponent's ability to play the ball.

However, Martinez did not agree with the decision to overturn the offside call.

"I think he was offside," the Argentine told Sky Sports post match. "What I can't understand is the rules, you know? He was there, I went to him because he was in front of me that's why Haaland was free but I want to be calm now, I want to control myself.

‌



"So hard because you lost the derby, three points at home. Every time they come to our club, they explain one hour, hour and a half with the rules then after five or six people doing this kind of mistake in the PL is unacceptable. You have the best players, best teams in the world and now we have to go home with this injustice.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

"For sure, it's difficult. I have two players there and I was 50/50, had to take the first guy in front. Simple as that (if Enzo isn't there goes to Haaland), let's see what they have to say, let's see, I want to hear what their decision is. Based off what? I want to hear it."

‌



United head coach Michael Carrick also slammed the decision that cost them a 1-0 defeat to City. He said: "Confused, not even confused, we've put things in place to help referees' decisions, screens, referees in an office somewhere. It's more worrying about if that's the interpretation about football.

"If we've got people in place that are meant to understand a game of football or not interfering with play or impacting an attack, throwing your body at it with a defender next to him, it's really worrying for me. It's a staggering decision. I can't understand it once I seen it then the explanation makes it worse.

"The explanation that he's not interfering with play. Incredible. It's not going to change a season, it's a major impact on the game and it's a massive game. It's a long season ahead, we've got to get back to winning football matches, that's on us, that (decision) wasn't on us today."

‌



On Sky Sports commentary, Gary Neville was baffled as the still images suggested Haaland was behind the last defender. "I'm going to need the offside law explaining to me, it's lost me," he said.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

"The question is does Enzo Fernandez put off Lisandro Martinez? I think he does because he sort of hesitates. I do think when they look back, they'll recognise they got it wrong," before adding: "Well VAR looked at this for a long, long time. They say Haaland's onside from Dorgu's foot, from where we were didn't look the case but Dorgu's foot is deeper."

Article continues below

The Premier League Match Centre on X later confirmed that this was the case following the decision.

Sports.title: Erling Haaland fires 10-man Man City to controversial Man Utd win - 5 talking points
Sports.content:
Erling Haaland fires 10-man Man City to controversial Man Utd win - 5 talking points

MANCHESTER UNITED 0-1 MANCHESTER CITY: Erling Haaland's goal, following a long VAR check for offside, is enough for City to win at Old Trafford following Phil Foden's red card

View 5 Images Erling Haaland's goal gave 10-man City the win (Image: Alex Livesey - Danehouse/Getty Images)

Manchester City shrugged off Phil Foden's first-half red card to deny Manchester United and leave Old Trafford with the derby bragging rights thanks to Erling Haaland's contentious goal.

City's task was made harder in the 23rd minute when Foden was shown the red card by Michael Oliver for kicking out at Bruno Fernandes. Yet United failed to make the most of their numerical advantage, with Marcus Rashford's long-range free-kick onto the post the closest they came in a tight first half.

Kobbie Mainoo rattled the post with a curling effort from the edge of the box before 10-man City took the lead through Haaland's back-post finish from Josko Gvardiol's deflected cross. The goal was initially ruled out for offside before VAR eventually confirmed that Patrick Dorgu had played the Norwegian onside, despite suggestions Enzo Fernandez had interfered.

‌



Senne Lammens tipped Fernandez's shot onto the post as City then threatened to go two goals up. Bryan Mbeumo headed just wide before Haaland steered a low Fernandez free-kick wide as the game finally opened up in the closing stages.

Gianluigi Donnarumma saved from Mbeumo in added time as City successfully shut up shop and claimed the spoils from the Manchester Derby to maintain their perfect record and keep pace with Arsenal at the top of the Premier League. Here are the talking points.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Foden sees red

Maybe being a local lad got the better of him, but really Foden has nobody to blame but himself. He was right to be angry at Fernandes, who had left a bit on him and at least deserved a yellow himself. But his reaction was stupid and, in the age of VAR, was only going to bring one outcome. Enzo Maresca was suddenly left ruing his instruction to 'embrace the chaos'.

The incident brought back memories of David Beckham and Diego Simeone and left his team-mates facing an uphill battle at Old Trafford. Erling Haaland's reaction, telling him to get off the pitch, told a story.

‌



View 5 Images Phil Foden was shocked by the red card (Image: Catherine Ivill - AMA/Getty Images)

10 vs 11 stalemate

The red card should have encouraged United to push on and search for the opening goal, but instead it poured water on their flames. Maresca shuffled Rayan Cherki over onto the right wing, where Foden had been, creating a 4-4-1 formation and, if anything, the away side looked the better team for the remainder of the first half.

The space that had been there beforehand, with Elliot Anderson being asked to track Fernandes and deal with Matheus Cunha dropping off the backline, was suddenly neutralised as Enzo Fernandez retreated alongside his midfield partner. And that made for a dull spectacle and a frustrated Old Trafford crowd.

‌



View 5 Images The red card took the wind out of Manchester United's sails (Image: Carl Recine/Getty Images)

Offside confusion

In essence it was a simple decision. The linesman had flagged Haaland offside - and to TV viewers it appeared a straightforward decision, with the City striker ahead of Lisandro Martinez at the back post. But it was simply a trick of the eyes, with Sky's cameras not in line.

As it often does, VAR took an age. Eventually we were treated to the semi-automated offside replay, which showed Dorgu's outstretched foot, while trying to charge down Gvardiol's cross, had just kept Haaland onside.

‌



But the theories kept on coming. "Surely it's offside. Martinez is impacted by Enzo's movement, and he is offside," Wayne Rooney said on the BBC, while Gary Neville made the same point on co-commentary for Sky Sports.

View 5 Images Erling Haaland was deemed onside for the goal

Maresca deserves credit

City have made a perfect start to the 2026/27 season, for which they deserve plenty of credit. Having lost Pep Guardiola and reshaped the squad in a busy summer transfer window, it would have been understandable if it took time for Maresca to get things moving.

‌



But they've won all four Premier League games to keep pace with defending champions Arsenal, as well as dealing with a trip to Porto in the Champions League. Since the Community Shield, they have resembled the City juggernaut of old. City always wanted Maresca to succeed Guardiola - and now we are seeing why.

View 5 Images Enzo Maresca has hit the ground running at City (Image: Michael Regan/Getty Images)

Disappointing United

Foden was sent off in the 23rd minute, yet a casual viewer would not have known City were down to 10 men, bar the little red icon below their club badge in the corner of the screen.

‌



The way City managed their lead was textbook. They frustrated United, played the percentages, won free-kicks and wasted time. United, for their part, had no answer, with Fernandes unable to conjure something, Rashford shackled and Cunha ineffective, while Mbeumo spurned two good chances.

Michael Carrick's only trump card, bringing on Benjamin Sesko, also had no effect and the sight of Joshua Zirkzee - a player unwanted by United two weeks ago - coming on in the closing stages told a story.

Sports.title: 'Obvious changes' - F1 drivers want Madring overtaking improvements
Sports.content:
Formula 1 drivers and team chiefs are hopeful there is scope at the Madring for organisers to make changes to the track to aid overtaking for future seasons.

The new home of the Spanish Grand Prix held its inaugural event over the weekend around the semi-permanent, wall-lined Madring circuit

While the 3.36-mile layout was praised for the challenge it posed on a fast qualifying lap, drivers had raised concerns ahead of the race about a likely lack of overtaking opportunities - something which largely played out in the race.

Lando Norris, who claimed the inaugural pole position and would likely have won the Grand Prix too but for an untimely Virtual Safety Car, believes "there are some obvious changes they should make" to make it a "great race track" to go with the challenge it provided drivers in qualifying.

Offering a blunt assessment on some immediate revisions he would like to see, the McLaren driver said: "They should get rid of [Turns] 18, 19. Useless. Just have more of a straight into a hairpin.

"Like, I don't know how someone looks at this design and goes, 'Mint'. Yeah, I think there's a lot of opportunity.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the 2026 Spanish Grand Prix.

"Like I said yesterday, I think they can make it into a track that's good for racing, and I'm excited to come back here next year if they can make these changes because I think it's a track that is good fun to drive and it can be a great race track."

Race winner Kimi Antonelli added: "I think there are some corners that need to be changed to create more overtaking opportunities because right now, yes, it's nice over one lap, but for sure in the race, you know, you're just stuck behind [other cars]."

Williams' Carlos Sainz, one of two Spanish drivers on the grid and who is also an ambassador of the Grand Prix, wrote on X: "The track is great. There needs to be some work done to create better passing, but it's been a great race overall, especially for a first year."

'They are totally open-minded about next year' - Wolff sure organisers will make tweaks

The inaugural race weekend at the Madring, which winds round Madrid's IFEMA exhibition centre and is located close to the Spanish capital's international airport, drew a sold-out crowd of 352,618.

Toto Wolff said he was impressed with the event as a whole and revealed organisers were already talking to the FIA, F1's governing body, about what could be improved regarding the track for next year.

"I think for the first [event], it's probably one of the best, or maybe the best that I've seen so far," said the Mercedes team principal.

"It's a temporary circuit. They've built something that is challenging for the drivers - a mini Macau or a mini Monaco - and the location is good.

Brundle expecting Madring tweaks Sky Sports F1's Martin Brundle



“I think they will make some tweaks for next year to create one or two more overtaking places.



"Everybody realises that and, perhaps, had there been more, they might have done it this year. I’m pretty sure this will evolve into a really nice event



“There’s zones around the world that always create good overtaking and we should learn from that – the last part of Istanbul, Turn Six in Hockenheim, Silverstone. It’s not just about a chicane into a long straight, it’s a combination of corners that you need.”

"We are thinking about how much more we can do next year in terms of little events here, or presentations, because we have the space and that's very rare in Formula 1.

"So I would say congratulations for a first.

"And then it's the tricky bit, doing a track that is spectacular also for the drivers and then building it in a way that there is lots of overtaking.

"I had a discussion yesterday with the CEO of the circuit and they are totally open-minded about next year and said 'we've had the discussions with the FIA. What is it we should do? How is it that we should lay the track out when it comes to overtaking?' There is a constant discussion.

"And I think that they are on it and understand 'can we tweak it a little bit here or there?' Honestly, I feel like if you try to find a hair in the soup, then you always find one. But being here for the first time, I'm very impressed."

Red Bull team principal Laurent Mekies was similarly effusive about the facility and also expressed hope that track improvements would be explored and introduced.

"It was an incredible event, that's my opinion," said Mekies.

"Incredible event, incredible venue setup. Massive paddock, massive garage area. I think it was a fantastic track in terms of being a driver's track, all sort of corner speed and all of that in between the walls.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player The F1 grid reviewed the new Madring track ahead of the weekend.

"I think the only shortfall is the overtaking opportunity. I'm guessing it is stuff that can be addressed even [with] the space that we have around the track layout.

"I'm not a track designer but I would think that there would be certainly a common desire to want to improve probably the only aspect, or the main aspect, that remains behind here which is the overtaking opportunity."

What could be changed?

Norris offered further suggested alterations to the existing layout.

"It's great in qualifying, but, you know, straight line from 17 straight to 20, have a much wider entry like Austin Turn 1 or Turn 10 in Austin, big hairpin," he said.

"You know, you'll create much better opportunities for everyone and you'll be able to enjoy the race.

"So yeah, there are some simple changes and maybe some trickier ones, like Turn 5, 6, 7. It's hard to know exactly what's the best thing.

"The fact you have to turn and brake basically defeats the whole object of racing. So, they can do some simple changes, I think, easy changes and maybe some more tricky, but I hope they do it because then it should be more exciting for everyone."

Speaking after qualifying on Saturday, Red Bull's Max Verstappen had said: "In terms of track design, I think it can be better.

"I think also input from drivers in the future on track design can also help a lot. I know they will always come back to you and say, 'Yeah, but the space,' but that's BS. There's always a way to find an overtaking opportunity around a track.

"But overall, the event itself is very cool. I mean, yes, they've done a great job.

"Also how quick, I think, they made the track available, the information that was shared for the simulator. So, from that sense, I think, yeah, it was very good. But in terms of, if you want to have better racing, overtaking, I think there can be a few corners that can be changed."

Sports.title: We know Haaland's goal was a mistake - but WHY did it happen?
Sports.content:
Erling Haaland's winning goal in Sunday's Manchester derby came in controversial circumstances - and there are still a number of questions left unanswered.

The striker's goal was initially disallowed for offside on the pitch before VAR overturned the decision.

The VAR officials deemed that Haaland was played onside by Manchester United defender Patrick Dorgu. However, Manchester City's Enzo Fernandez was in an offside position as he attempted to play the ball before it reached Haaland.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Gary Neville slams VAR's decision to give Erling Haaland's goal in the Manchester derby.

Here, we look at some of the key questions surrounding the incident...

Have Pro Ref explained why the goal was awarded?

Pro Ref - the Professional Game Referees formerly known as the PGMOL or PGMO - confirmed on Sunday night that an error was made when City's winning goal was awarded.

While acknowledging "an error of judgement", their statement only offered a partial explanation for why the goal was mistakenly awarded.

Having admitted the goal should have remained ruled out because Fernandez was offside, the statement declared: "On this occasion, the VAR did not recognise the likely impact of his position."

But the overarching question of why the VAR failed to appreciate that a player six yards from goal, making a diving header for a ball between two opponents, was not judged to have either impacted play or potentially impacted play remains unanswered.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Michael Carrick, Lisandro Martinez and Erling Haaland react to Manchester City's controversial winner against Manchester United.

Could the mistake have happened because the VAR was focused on whether Fernandez played the ball?

This, currently, appears to be the most logical explanation.

In their mid-game post on X explaining the decision, Match Centre wrote: "The VAR also deemed that while in an offside position, Fernandez didn't play the ball."

During Sky Sports' match coverage, replays were also shown of the VAR team apparently scrutinising whether or not Fernandez touched the ball as it flew across the six-yard box.

So was it the case that the VAR became distracted by fixating on a technicality that didn't actually matter given the offside rule clearly stipulates that a player can be offside regardless of whether or not he touches the ball?

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player FREE TO WATCH: Highlights from Manchester United’s match against Manchester City in the Premier League.

Why did the Pro Ref statement say the goal should have been sent for an on-field review?

According to Pro Ref, the initial offside decision was made against Erling Haaland. He, though, was onside.

The review then moved on to Fernandez, who was correctly deemed to be in an offside position by the VAR team.

The problem was that they then apparently, and incorrectly, focused entirely on whether he touched the ball.

What the VAR couldn't do, however, was confirm the goal was rightly ruled out - for the Fernandez offside - for the wrong reason - the Haaland offside.

Hence Pro Ref's assertion that the VAR ought to have requested referee Michael Oliver make an on-field review in which Oliver would have been asked to make a subjective decision on whether Fernandez impacted play.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player VAR drama as Erling Haaland fires Man City ahead!

Was Lammens also impacted by Fernandez?

Yes. Replays of Haaland's goal also show that the Manchester United goalkeeper made an initial reaction to Fernandez, raising his arms in anticipation of a header and putting him off balance for when Haaland struck the ball.

But Martinez had already been impacted by Fernandez's position, so the goal should have been disallowed regardless of whether Lammens was distracted by Fernandez's attempt to play the ball.

Image: Offside law graphic shown during coverage of Manchester United's match against Man City

Was the on-field decision wrong?

Yes and no - the yes because the offside was given against an onside player, the no because the goal should have been ruled out for offside.

So the VAR couldn't have definitively ruled out the goal?

No. Because the on-field decision was against Haaland, the only course of action, if the process was followed to the letter, was to ask the referee to make an on-field review.

Manchester United defender Lisandro Martinez to Sky Sports: "I think [Fernandez] was offside. What I can’t understand is the rules.



"He was there! I went to him because he was in front of me. That’s why Haaland was free at the back.



"I want to be calm but it is so hard.



"Five or six people (officials) doing this kind of mistake in the Premier League is unacceptable.



"We have to go home with this injustice."

Who was the VAR?

Sunday's VAR was Matt Donohue.

While Donohue has only ever refereed four Premier League games, he has substantial experience as a VAR. In 2025/26, he was the VAR for 24 Premier League matches and six as Assistant VAR.

Who were the match officials at Old Trafford? Referee: Michael Oliver

Assistants: Stuart Burt, Tim Wood

Fourth official: Paul Tierney

VAR: Matt Donohue

Assistant VAR: Blake Antrobus

Why didn't TV viewers see offside lines drawn during the game?

The Premier League is using semi-automated offside technology this season which provides a kick-point graphic for incidents under review.

This is different to the previous process in which the VAR teams would manually place crosshairs to determine offside calls and then draw lines.

Did the officials also forget they made a VAR check?

One final unanswered question from Manchester's derby is whether the officials also forgot about the VAR check when determining how much added-on time to play at the end of the game.

Haaland's goal was scored after 59 minutes and 24 seconds.

Following the lengthy review, play didn't restart until 63 minutes and 15 seconds. But despite that delay, and numerous others during the course of the half, just five minutes were added on.

Sports.title: What next for Benn? 'I don't have the answer'
Sports.content:
Conor Benn is left contemplating his next options after suffering a heavy stoppage loss to Ryan Garcia in Las Vegas.

Benn was attempting to follow in his famous father Nigel's footsteps and become a world champion when he challenged Garcia for the WBC belt at the T-Mobile Arena.

But Garcia, a top-class fighter, handed Benn a crushing loss when he dropped and stopped him in their second round.

The Briton must now rebuild.

"Everybody keeps asking: 'What's next for Conor Benn?'" he stated on social media. "The truth is, I don't have the answer.

Image: Conor Benn with Ryan Garcia after their contest in Las Vegas (Photos: Zuffa Boxing)

"If you'd asked the 19-year-old version of me whether I thought I'd be standing here 10 years later, having lived through everything I have, I'd have told you that you were crazy.

"I train hard. I sacrifice. I've given this game 110 per cent every time I've stepped through those ropes, I've wanted to give people unforgettable nights and entertain.

"That's what this has always been about for me.

"People spend their hard-earned money to come and watch guys like us fight. I've never taken that for granted. I've always wanted to be a servant of the public and give everything I have when it matters."

The signs are that he will rest, recover and take some time out before considering how to return.

"Giving everything comes at a cost," he continued. "And the people who have paid that cost more than anyone are my family and my kids.

"They've sacrificed time with their dad so I could chase this dream. They've had to share me with this sport their entire lives.

"So when people ask me what's next for Conor Benn, right now the answer is simple.

"Time with my kids."

He added: "Fight fans, thank you. Those who travelled to Vegas, those who stayed up until the early hours. I will never take your support for granted, especially on those nights things don't go to plan."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the rematch between Conor Benn and Chris Eubank Jr at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium. Pictures courtesy of DAZN.

What could be next for Benn?

Benn is only 29 years old, so while he might take some time out of boxing, he can be expected to return to the sport.

The bout with Garcia was his first fight at welterweight in over four years. After two middleweight bouts with Chris Eubank Jr, the drop back to 147lbs was severe.

All the indications are that Benn will seek to go back up in weight. He could bypass 154lbs altogether and bounce back to middleweight.

There are title belt holders at 160lbs who have championships but relatively low profiles. Aaron McKenna, the IBF champion, and Denzel Bentley, now the WBO titleholder, for instance would surely welcome a fight with Benn if he could get ranked.

Perhaps he could move even higher in weight, even though he'd be small at middleweight let alone super-middle. But having a trilogy bout with Eubank Jr at 168lbs could make sense. It would save Eubank the punishing weight cut he had at middleweight with a rehydration clause and the two are 1-1 in their series.

For Benn, his Las Vegas adventure ended in a crushing defeat to Garcia, but there will be options for him as and when he chooses to return.

Sports.title: 'Pietersen will add spark' as he begins England white-ball coaching role
Sports.content:
Kevin Pietersen is “buzzing” to be back with the England set-up, having joined the white-ball coaching staff for the series against Sri Lanka, according to interim head coach Marcus Trescothick.

Pietersen will serve as a specialist mentor through to the 2027 Cricket World Cup in Africa next year. He will link up with the squad this week ahead of England's first T20I against Sri Lanka on Tuesday, live on Sky Sports Cricket from 6pm, with the first ball at 6.30pm.

Trescothick and Pietersen were Ashes-winning team-mates during England's famous 2005 triumph, giving the former first-hand experience of the qualities and talents the latter can bring to the current team.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player England captain Joe Root expresses his delight about the appointment of Kevin Pietersen as a specialist mentor for the white-ball teams.

"He is buzzing about putting back on the England shirt or tracksuit, buzzing for the opportunity and it's really exciting," the England batting coach said of Pietersen.

"Having his presence around, and the knowledge he has about batting - he saw batting in a different light to many people - if we can tap into that and get that into our white-ball cricket, It's only going to benefit the team."

Is Pietersen appointment a risk? | 'He'll add a little more spark', says Trescothick

The appointment has raised a few eyebrows, coming 12 years after Pietersen was effectively sacked by the ECB in the wake of England's disastrous 5-0 Ashes drubbing in Australia. At the time, the ECB said he had become "disconnected" from the team and accused him of failing to support then-captain Sir Alastair Cook.

Image: Kevin Pietersen's England playing career was ended after the 2013-14 Ashes defeat in Australia under then captain Alastair Cook

Pietersen had previously been dropped in 2012 after sending text messages to members of the South African team, while he resigned as captain after just five months in 2008 following a breakdown in his relationship with then head coach Peter Moores.

Since his retiring a player in 2018, Pietersen has, at times, also been an outspoken critic of the England setup, including when accusing the white-ball team of inadequate preparation on a tour of India last January after Brendon McCullum had just taken over as head coach, who he'll now be working under.

Having hammered India 4-0 in a T20 series earlier this summer, briefly leapfrogging them at the top of the world rankings, and won their last two ODI series against Sri Lanka and India, England's decision to hire Pietersen appears a risky move at a time when the team is enjoying a strong run of form.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the fifth T20I between England and India earlier this summer as the hosts romped to a 4-0 series win.

"You can see the team moving in the right direction; we've had great results in the last sort of 18 months - in both formats," Trescothick said, before adding: "I think you're just adding a little more spark and a little bit more variety from a different coach's point of view.

"Kevin has seen white-ball cricket around the world for a long period of time, playing in all the big competitions, he's won a [T20] World Cup [in 2010], you're going to gain something extra.

"It's up to the coaching setup with Brendon to draw out the best from him.

"Management of different players, coaches and setups is is the great art, isn't it? If you get that right, then you get a lot of good things come from coaches and players alike."

Sports.title: Zverev: I am best player in the world right now
Sports.content:
Alexander Zverev believes he is currently the best tennis player in the world following his US Open victory.

‌German Zverev beat Ben Shelton in the final on Sunday to the bitter disappointment of the home crowd in ‌New York.

Zverev was playing in his sixth major final and Shelton his first, and it showed in a 6-3 7-6 (7-2) 5-7 6-2 victory that extinguished America's hopes of a first male winner since Andy Roddick in 2003.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Zverev won the US Open…and he didn't realise!!!

The 29-year-old has been the dominant player in Grand Slams in a season that has seen Carlos Alcaraz, who won this year's Australian Open, exit the US Open in a quarter-final defeat by Shelton after a long injury lay-off while world No 1 Jannik Sinner pulled out injured before the tournament began after winning Wimbledon.

Zverev finally broke through to win his first major at the French Open, then reached the final at the All England Club, losing to Sinner.

He is 25-2 in Grand Slam matches in 2026 and Zverev believes he is currently the best in the world.

"You have to take everything into consideration," he said. "With Jannik Sinner being injured and Carlos Alcaraz coming back from injury after four months, right now, probably yes. Both of them healthy and both of them at the top of their game, maybe not.

"But if we say right, right now with Jannik being injured and Carlos coming back from injury, maybe. I mean, four, five months ago when both of them were healthy, I wasn't. I was losing to Jannik all the time. So if everyone is healthy, I think Jannik is still ahead. It's as simple as that."

Sports.title: Zverev ends Shelton’s run and American dreams with US Open triumph
Sports.content:
Top seed Alexander Zverev dashed American dreams on Sunday, overcoming Ben Shelton in a four-set battle to claim his maiden US Open title.

The German proved too strong for the eighth-seeded American prevailing 6-3 7-6 (7-2) 5-7 6-2 in the final at Flushing Meadows.

Zverev added the New York title to his collection after winning the French Open earlier this year. In a bizarre ending, Shelton's return sailed long on match point, but Zverev, seemingly unaware that he had won, hit the balls back to the other end of the court, ready for another game.

It was only when Zverev glanced up at the big screen that he realised he had actually won.

Alexander Zverev

2 Grand Slam titles



1 Olympic gold medal



2 ATP Finals titles



7 ATP Masters 1000 titles



26 singles titles



World No 1 🔜 ?



Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Alexander Zverev won the US Open and didn't even realise!

"I feel like there was so much suffering for the Zverev family at Grand Slam level, that maybe 2026 is the year we should just enjoy," Zverev told Sky Sports Tennis. "Everything is going perfectly. I am unbelievably happy.

"Three months ago if I was told you are going to win one Grand Slam in your career and nothing else, I would have signed the paper straight away and never questioned it.

"Now standing here with two Grand Slam trophies in the space of the months is incredible."

And on not realising he had won it on Championship point, he admitted: "I thought the score was 5-1! I knew that I had broken him twice, but I thought he only held once.

"I was thinking: 'Okay, I'm going to have a relaxed service game here and then I'll get tight on the next one.' "It was lucky for me!

"It's actually funny, teachers in tennis say play each point and forget about the score. Well I forgot about the score and it helped me!"

Shelton was bidding to become the first American man to win a Grand Slam singles title since Andy Roddick in 2003, while also aiming to become only the second black man to triumph at this level after Arthur Ashe in 1975. He walked onto the court to a rapturous reception from a partisan crowd of 23,000 spectators inside the stadium named in Ashe's honour.

Among the star-studded crowd were actors Brad Pitt and Rami Malek, as well as James Bond star Pierce Brosnan, who received a mischievous camera shot from the TV director with the match clock showing just 0.07.

Despite spending 19 hours and 38 minutes on court en route to the final - the fourth-longest total recorded by a player reaching a Grand Slam final since 1991 - Zverev made a blistering start. He broke in the opening game and then broke again on set point to seize control.

Shelton could not even earn a break point in the opening two sets, as Zverev, the No 1 seed at a Grand Slam for the first time, relied on his powerful serve to keep the American at bay.

Shelton had lost all five of his previous meetings with Zverev, but he had also arrived in New York having never beaten Stefanos Tsitsipas or, most notably, Carlos Alcaraz - until this tournament. That run gave him plenty of reason for optimism heading into Sunday's final at Flushing Meadows.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Ben Shelton ended on the floor as Alexander Zverev hit a brilliant passing shot in the US Open final.

But Zverev, now playing with freedom after shedding the unwanted tag of the 'best player never to win a major' with his French Open triumph earlier this year, dominated the second-set tie-break to move within touching distance of the title.

Shelton dug in, to his credit, and finally brought up three break - and set - points as the Zverev serve suddenly faltered, and the crowd were in full voice again when he converted the second.

But the match was effectively over as a contest when Zverev, who has capitalised on the fitness struggles and absences of Alcaraz and Jannik Sinner at various points this year, broke early in the fourth set.

His incessant ball-bouncing - statistics showed he spent around three hours of his 23-plus hours on court this fortnight bouncing the ball between serves - finally resulted in a time violation.

Meanwhile, Shelton's girlfriend Trinity Rodman pulled off a logistical miracle, making the 200-mile trip from a football pitch in Washington to Queen's, arriving in time to slip into her other half's box.

But it proved to be a wasted trip as Zverev held his nerve to clinch Grand Slam title No 2, and his first in New York, in three hours and 33 minutes. After a brief pause to take it all in, he finally began to celebrate.

Shortly after his victory, Zverev reserved his most heartfelt thanks for his mother Irina, a former professional tennis player, crediting her with ​refusing to let type 1 diabetes dictate his future.

"When your four-year-old son is diagnosed ⁠with diabetes and doctors in the office tell you ⁠that life and sports will be very limited for that child, it takes a very strong mother to say 'my son will be whatever he wants ‌to be'," Zverev said.

"If he wants to be a tennis player, he'll be a tennis player. If he wants to do something else, he'll do something else but this illness will not define us.

"I'm happy ‌that we worked through it and we're doing things that we're doing right now. My mother is the most important and strongest person I know because it takes an unbelievably strong woman to do what she did."

"This was your first Grand Slam final but I already told you you're going ​to be back here many more times and if I would have to bet all my money on it, I would bet that you would lift this ‌trophy one day."

Sports.title: 'You can't lose focus' | Why did VAR get Haaland goal so wrong?
Sports.content:
Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player

Former Premier League referee Dermot Gallagher and former Coventry striker Jay Bothroyd dissect the biggest talking point of the weekend and ask how VAR got Erling Haaland's winner for Manchester City against rivals United so wrong.

Sports.title: Premier League: 10 talking points from the weekend’s action
Sports.content:
1 Carrick fails to take advantage …

The 199th Manchester derby was defined by two refereeing decisions: Phil Foden’s first-half red card for kicking out at Bruno Fernandes, and the intervention by the video assistant referee to award Erling Haaland’s winning goal despite Enzo Fernández appearing to interfere with play from an offside position. In both cases, a healthy dose of common sense might have led to a different outcome and Pro Ref admitted that Haaland’s goal should not have stood. Still, it is tough to argue that the final result was harsh on United. Foden’s dismissal gave the hosts a huge opportunity they failed to take, their best chance falling to Bryan Mbeumo in stoppage time. Michael Carrick began his reign with a 2-0 home derby win against 11 men in January, so this felt like a backward step for the manager, unable to find a way to control the game. Carrick also bemoaned City’s two days of extra rest after Champions League games, but chose to keep Fernandes and others on for 90 minutes in the 4-0 stroll past Sabah. United’s next two league games are away at Fulham and at home to Spurs. Carrick will need to be smarter to stop an early-season wobble becoming something more serious. Niall McVeigh

2 … while Maresca’s master plan pays off

Foden’s red card also posed a big test for Enzo Maresca, overseeing his first derby as Manchester City manager. After a solid but unspectacular start to the league season, this could have become a painful afternoon with his team down to 10 men. Instead, the Italian made smart decisions to secure a galvanising result and keep pace with Arsenal, both teams already edging clear of their expected rivals. Maresca made just one change in the first 80 minutes, but bringing on Iliman Ndiaye for Rayan Cherki gave his team a more direct threat on the break. Fellow new signings Enzo Fernández and Elliot Anderson have settled quickly, the latter imperious in midfield during a second half where City rarely looked short-handed. At the back, Marc Guéhi barely put a foot wrong as City showed a solidity that had been lacking. The manner of Haaland’s winner was fortunate, to say the least, but the visitors’ second-half display deserved all three points. NMc

View image in fullscreen Enzo Maresca celebrates with Ruben Días after a statement win for Manchester City. Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The Guardian

3 Free-scoring Seagulls dunk on Coventry

On another day, any of the excellent individual goals from Charalampos Kostoulas, Malick Yalcouyé and Yasin Ayari could have been the showstopper in Brighton’s rout of Coventry. But none could compare with Lewis Dunk’s sensational 35-yard pile-driver into the top corner. For a centre-back to even consider shooting from where he did is ridiculous, but Dunk insisted he has “that sort of shot in my locker”, with Fabian Hürzeler saying everyone at the club knows all about the shooting technique he possesses. Dunk was one of five goalscorers on Sunday as Brighton continue to show they can do things differently to last season, when Danny Welbeck was their chief attacking threat with 13 Premier League goals. Eight players have scored in four league games and who really needs a star striker when your centre-back can hit a ball like that? Ben Bloom

4 Arteta’s ‘sadness’ unfair to Sunderland

Referees are supposed to be clamping down on grappling, holding and shirt-pulling at dead balls this season, but until the 58th minute at the Stadium of Light on Saturday Sunderland and Arsenal got away with plenty at corners and throws. The irony was that when John Brooks penalised Ezri Konsa for hauling Dan Ballard down at a throw and awarded Sunderland a penalty, subsequently endorsed by a VAR check, it proved contentious. There was a strong case for arguing that Ballard’s clever “judo roll” had landed the admittedly far from innocent Konsa in deep trouble. No matter that David Raya’s brilliant save ensured Enzo Le Fée’s penalty proved academic; Mikel Arteta subsequently cut a study in righteous indignation. Going over the top, he said he felt “sad” for football and talked about wanting to “protect the game”. When, two minutes after Le Fée’s miss, Bruno Guimarães curled in a superlative shot Arsenal were en route to a 2-0 win sealed by Bukayo Saka’s late penalty and their immaculate start to the season continued. Sunderland, though, had played well and deserved more credit from a less than magnanimous Arteta. Louise Taylor

View image in fullscreen ‘A study in righteous indignation’: Mikel Arteta talks to fourth official Elliot Bell. Photograph: Scott Heppell/Reuters

5 Midfield fragility haunts Iraola

Andoni Iraola will inevitably discover some unwelcome truths in the learning stage of his Liverpool reign. A second successive Premier League draw at Anfield – their seventh from 12 games in 2026 – revealed several, from Kostas Tsimikas’s unreliability as a starter to the porous nature of a central midfield pairing of Ryan Gravenberch and Dominik Szoboszlai. Iraola had to make changes given the tight turnaround from Wednesday’s Champions League win over Atlético Madrid, his first experience of having to do so with Liverpool, and the absence of Alexis Mac Allister had more of a destabilising effect than he might have imagined. Gravenberch and Szoboszlai offered minimal resistance to a Fulham team that cut through with ease and, together with Florian Wirtz, offered little to an ineffective Liverpool attack assembled at huge expense. There will be further changes when Tottenham visit in the Carabao Cup on Tuesday. Teenage midfielder Trey Nyoni, impressive in pre-season, should get an opportunity to show he can be a viable alternative the next time Mac Allister is rested. Andy Hunter

6 Miss and Tel: De Zerbi’s Spurs still scoreless

Roberto De Zerbi insisted there “is not a problem” between him and Mathys Tel, when nobody had seriously suggested there was. “I love Mathys as a player, as a guy,” the Tottenham manager said. Still, it was not a good day for Tel against Everton. Dropped from the starting XI, he received an on-pitch tutorial from De Zerbi in how to play as a No 9. The Tottenham manager had moved Tel there in the closing stages after initially introducing him in his favoured left-wing role. Play on the shoulder, attack the six-yard box, was the gist of De Zerbi’s advice. Spurs’ toothlessness at the sharp end of their formation was not on Tel. The real worry was Dominic Solanke and how he ghosted through another Premier League game. Omar Marmoush was also ineffective; first on the left, then briefly as the No 9 after Solanke was withdrawn. Solanke has been undermined by injuries, but 12 league goals since his £55m arrival in August 2024 is not good enough. David Hytner

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

View image in fullscreen Tottenham manager Roberto De Zerbi gives Mathys Tel his post-game review on the pitch. Photograph: Andrew Couldridge/Action Images/Reuters

7 Sage wisdom under scrutiny at Palace

Crystal Palace’s defenders committed the cardinal sin of not playing to the whistle when they allowed Ipswich to equalise during the first half of Saturday’s costly 3-2 defeat. It was just the latest example of the bad habits that are creeping in since Pierre Sage’s arrival as manager. While the Frenchman promised to speak to Axel Disasi after his reckless red card in the first half cost Palace dear, it was surprising to hear Sage say: “I had this discussion with them because they did the same thing in a session. I told them to continue to play. Because of the VAR now, I prefer they deflect the ball [out] for a corner and then ask the referee if they were offside or not.” Palace are lacking leadership at the back after selling Maxence Lacroix to Chelsea and have conceded seven goals in their first two matches at home. Sage must find a solution to their defensive woes without Disasi, who will miss their next three Premier League matches due to suspension. Ed Aarons

8 Chelsea’s defence remains unserious

Chelsea do not relish the art of defending enough. Hull’s first goal on Saturday was a case in point. Malo Gusto was outmuscled by Ryan Giles and Mohamed Belloumi equalised when Jorrel Hato misjudged the Hull left-back’s cross. Xabi Alonso called it soft. The Chelsea manager replaced Hato at half-time, but the problems are not down to one individual. Emiliano Martínez, signed as Robert Sanchez’s replacement, is yet to convince in goal. Wesley Fofana still flatters to deceive, Levi Colwill is feeling his way back from injury and Maxence Lacroix was surprisingly on the bench against Hull. Chelsea have conceded 12 goals in Alonso’s first six games in all competitions. They remain unserious. Jacob Steinberg

Match report: Chelsea 2-2 Hull

View image in fullscreen The Chelsea captain, Reece James, looks forlorn after Hull City’s second goal at Stamford Bridge. Photograph: Peter Cziborra/Action Images/Reuters

9 McAtee finally finds his feet at Forest

Oliver Glasner consistently name-checked James McAtee before a ball was kicked this season, adamant the £30m arrival from Manchester City last summer could finally make a splash in a Nottingham Forest shirt. His performance in their first victory of the season, at Aston Villa on Saturday, was further evidence of a player revitalised. Glasner is convinced the 23-year-old can thrive in the quarterback role he gave Adam Wharton at Crystal Palace. McAtee has started all four league matches this season, twice as many as he managed in the last campaign; he was hooked at half-time in successive starts against Utrecht and Wrexham either side of the turn of the year. But against Villa, McAtee oozed confidence and relished dictating the game. Glasner represents McAtee’s fifth Forest manager in 13 months, but in the Austrian he has one of his biggest fans. Ben Fisher

Match report: Aston Villa 1-2 Nottingham Forest

10 Rose still winless despite positive signs

“Many teams struggle against Bournemouth,” said Brentford’s Vitaly Janelt. That has been true of all four opponents faced in Marco Rose’s Premier League tenure. And yet the wait for a first win continues. “If you watch our games, I think it’s a joy,” said Rose. This week, his squad jets off to face Real Sociedad in the Europa League, fulfilling the dream of fans and the club’s owner. Bill Foley. Rose, one of the game’s optimists, refused to cast blame on Djordje Petrovic’s goalkeeping errors for Kevin Schade’s double, instead looking ahead to Thursday: “A special night for the club against top opposition. It’s a tough stadium. Top atmosphere, intense opponent, a good team with Spanish national team players.” Bournemouth may well find life easier in Europe. As Justin Kluivert said: “It’s lovely to play in this team. We are front-footed, we press, we don’t just let it be a slow game, we go for it.” John Brewin

Match report: Bournemouth 2-2 Brentford

Sports.title: ‘An error of judgement’: Pro Ref admits mistake in awarding Haaland’s derby winner
Sports.content:
Pro Ref admitted Erling Haaland’s winner in Sunday’s Manchester derby should not have been allowed after the video assistant referee ruled Enzo Fernández was not interfering with play in the build-up. The elite officiating body will review the decision and has contacted Manchester United.

Haaland’s 60th minute goal for Manchester City at Old Trafford was initially ruled offside before the VAR’s intervention. It came after Josko Gvardiol’s cross hit Patrick Dorgu’s boot, passed Fernández and the United defender Lisandro Martínez, and was finished by the City No 9. VAR decided Fernández was not interfering despite Martínez marking the midfielder.

A Pro Ref statement said: “Following the incident in the 60th minute of Sunday’s Premier League fixture between Manchester United and Manchester City at Old Trafford, we can provide clarification regarding Erling Haaland’s awarded goal.

“The on-field decision was offside against Haaland – that was checked by VAR and he was found to be in an onside position.

“In the same attack, it was established that Fernández did not play the ball and therefore that makes any offside offence subjective, however, on this occasion, the VAR did not recognise the likely impact of his position and should have recommended an on-field review.

“Contact has been made with Manchester United this evening to acknowledge what we deem is an error of judgement. A review of the incident will take place.”

After the match but before the Pro Ref statement, an unhappy Michael Carrick expressed concern over Haaland’s winner.

Quick Guide Play our football trivia game, On the ball Show The Guardian's daily football game, On the ball, is now live in the app for both iOS and Android. Can you identify the Premier League star from the clues? Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

“At the time I hadn’t totally seen it. But the explanation I got was he wasn’t interfering with play, so I just don’t get it,” the United manager said. “I can’t understand how they’re trying to help referees and putting so many layers behind them with so many people, screens, and so many whatever offices to try and come up with the right decisions.

“If that’s how the rules are interpreted, that you’re not interfering with play because you’ve thrown yourself at the ball six yards from goal and pretty much nearly touched it, which then Lisandro has to react from – it’s worrying if that’s really how the game’s seen by those who are officiating it.”

Carrick was asked if an apology from Pro Ref would be welcome. “Yeah, that’d be great, that. Yeah, I can’t wait for that one,” he said. “I don’t really know how you go and get another explanation on that one. I think we all understand what that rule means [regarding interfering with play], and it’s pretty obvious. It’s as obvious as it gets.”

Enzo Maresca, though, was adamant that Fernández was not interfering. “Yeah – and the fourth official said Erling is onside,” the City manager said.

The 199th Manchester derby’s other controversial decision was Phil Foden’s 23rd-minute red card. The forward kicked Bruno Fernandes in the stomach, but only after United’s captain had kicked him. Maresca backed Michael Oliver’s red card but suggested the referee should also have sent off Fernandes.

“Phil Foden red card is a red card, but I also think it is red card from Bruno,” City’s manager said. “Reviewing the action, it is a clear red card for Phil because it is a reaction but you can also see Bruno’s [action].”
