Sports.title: Premier League Heroes and Villains: Man United star should never play for club again as Michael Carrick criticised
Sports.content:
Premier League Heroes and Villains: Man United star should never play for club again as Michael Carrick criticised

Four draws, no home wins, four red cards and one of the worst VAR decisions in Premier League history.

There is never a dull weekend of top-flight football as we saw a change at the top of the table, while two clubs are still without a goal.



10 Bruno Guimares scored in a 2-0 win against Sunderland to help Arsenal move into top spot Credit: Getty

A total of 24 goals have been scored across nine matches so far, with Leeds vs Newcastle - live on talkSPORT on Monday night - wrapping up the fixtures for Matchweek 4.

What were the Premier League results this weekend?

Fulham were told they should be docked points last week following their 3-2 defeat to Crystal Palace, but they showed their fighting spirit to hold Liverpool to a 0-0 draw at Anfield to register their first point of the season.

Elsewhere, Ipswich fought back from a goal down to nick a late 3-2 win away at Palace, who saw Axel Disasi sent off in the first half for a horror challenge.



An equally exciting game was played out at Stamford Bridge, as a topsy-turvy match saw Chelsea and unbeaten Hull share the spoils in a 2-2 draw.

And it was the same scoreline at the Vitality Stadium as Bournemouth yet again were forced to settle for a point despite leading for the fourth game running against Brentford.



Aston Villa meanwhile registered their first goal of the Premier League campaign, but it failed to matter as they lost 2-1 to Nottingham Forest - their third defeat this term.

But Tottenham created unwanted club history by failing to open their account this season as they drew 0-0 to Everton.



In Saturday's late match, Arsenal moved to the summit after grinding out a battling 2-0 win away at ten-man Sunderland [Reinildo - two yellow cards] which saw Bruno Guimaraes score his first goal for the club - and in some style.

Moving onto Sunday, and ten-man Coventry [Taiwo Awoniyi straight red] remain without a goal since their promotion as Brighton eased to a 5-0 win on the road.

Manchester City, who saw Phil Foden sent off in the 23rd minute, beat rivals Manchester United 1-0 in a game marred by VAR controversy.

10 Mohamed Belloumi scored twice for Hull in a four-goal thriller in west London Credit: Getty



10 It's no wins and zero goals scored for Tottenham from their opening four Premier League games Credit: Getty

With plenty to discuss from the weekend's football, talkSPORT's Sam Matterface, Alex Crook and Troy Deeney dissect the drama in our Premier League All Access show.

Picking out their heroes and villains, here's what they had to say...

Who are talkSPORT's Premier League Heroes?

David Raya

The Spaniard once again showed why many consider him to be the world's best goalkeeper as he put in a man of the match display at the Stadium of Light.

A highly contentious penalty saw Mikel Arteta rage at the officials in his post-match interview, but he would have felt justice was served when Raya tipped Enzo Le Fee's penalty onto the post.



It proved to be the turning point in the game as Guimaraes would fire the visitors ahead just two minutes later as the Gunners ended up making it nine Premier League wins in a row - stretching back to last season - for the first time in 22 years.

Lauding the World Cup winner, Matterface stated: "David Raya, penalty save was absolutely sensational.

"Also made another save from [Nordi] Mukiele really late in the game. Absolutely superb.

"He's just absolutely excellent and Arsenal really have progressed because he is the goalkeeper.



"He's added so much to them, he was terrific."

10 Raya somehow pushed Le Fee's effort on the post for his first Premier League penalty save since December 2023 Credit: Getty

Gianluigi Donnarumma

United only had two shots on target at Old Trafford, but the towering Italian goalkeeper had to be alert to deny the Red Devils a late draw deep into stoppage time.

Bryan Mbeumo was sent through in the dying embers, only for Donnarumma to parry away his strike to compound a miserable Manchester derby for the hosts.

Quick to give 27-year-old his flowers, Deeney said: "Donnarumma, what a save, I think if you think back to the Charity [Community] shield [3-0 defeat to Arsenal], a lot of people were talking about he wasn't that good, he should have made more saves.



"I said to you at the time, getting scored on in the six-yard box, not really a goalkeeper's fault at that point.

"So many people talking about, 'Ah, James Trafford, a bit of a mistake letting him go [to Leeds in £40million deal].'

"That's why you bring him in, because now, like David Raya, you can put two points by the goalkeeper.

"There's two points that he's just made there for the team and that's why you keep them in there.



"That's why Chelsea went and got [Emiliano] Martinez, yes, they will make mistakes, but also these guys will do more games than they lose."

10 Donnarumma helped City maintain their 100 per cent start to the top-flight campaign with a late save Credit: Getty

Zian Flemming

The 20-year-old was a late signing for the Tractor Boys, who splashed out £20m to bring him to Portman Road.

Having banged in 11 Premier League goals last campaign, the Dutchman got his first top-flight strike this season after scoring the winner at Ipswich Road.



Reacting quickest to Leif Davis' header ricocheting off the post, the ex-Ajax youth star prodded home a tap-in beyond the outstretched arms of Walter Benitez.

Commenting on the centre-forward, Crook said: "I'm going to go for Zian Flemming as a hero.

"They're not easy to score those tap-ins.

"But I think he'll end up with double figures again, I think he's a good player Flemming."

10 Flemming opened his account for Ipswich to help the Suffolk outfit claim their second win this term Credit: Getty



Who are talkSPORT's Premier League Villains?

Matt Donohue

The biggest talking point of the weekend was undoubtedly at the Theatre of Dreams, which saw Erling Haaland score the only goal of the game in highly controversial fashion.

Originally flagged for offside, the Norwegian was found to be onside after Patrick Dorgu played him on, though Enzo Fernandez was clearly offside in the build-up.

The midfielder made a diving header attempt, and though he failed to make contact, he stopped Lisandro Martinez from making an attempt to clear the ball - allowing Haaland to fire home at the back post.

Having initially stated that Fernandez wasn't interfering with play, refereeing governing body Pro Ref later came out and insisted the goal should never have been given.



And with Donohue on VAR duty for the incident, Matterface wasted no time in naming and shaming him, as he also touched on Sunderland's penalty, which saw Dan Ballard drag Ezri Konsa to the ground, only for the decision to go in his favour.

He said: "For me, Matt Donohue, I mean VAR... the Ballard situation is such a massive failing and the goal that Enzo Fernandez influenced that Haaland scored, massive failing.

"And from an FA Sam point of view, I'm sorry, I love you, I will be better next time.

"Seriously, just apologise, keep your head down, it was a bad weekend for VAR."



10 Fernandez was somehow adjudged to be onside before Haaland fired City ahead Credit: Sky Sports

10 The midfielder then looked to get on the end of the delivery, with Martinez unable to clear away the danger

Patrick Dorgu

The Denmark international failed to impress after coming into the team to replaced injured left-back Luke Shaw.

Dorgu was given a 2/10 rating by Crook - the lowest of any United player in the derby - as he labelled his defending for Haaland's winner as 'criminal'.



And the United fan singled the versatile player out for criticism as he issued a damning verdict on the 21-year-old.

He declared: "My main villain of the weekend is our good friend Patrick Dorgu.

"Who might be the worst Manchester United defender that I've seen since Eric Cantona persuaded Fergie [Sir Alex Ferguson] to sign his mate William Prunier.

"He played one game against Tottenham, got hammered on New Year's Day [4-1 defeat in 1996], we never saw him again.



"I fear we might see Dorgu in United again, but I think he should be subjected to the same treatment."

10 Dorgu has flattered to deceive for the Red Devils since joining from Leece in February 2025 for £29m Credit: Getty

Michael Carrick

The United boss cruised to victory over the Citizens in his first game in charge last term, but his side were second best this time around - despite having an extra man advantage for the majority of the match.

It's now four points in as many games for United, who have lost twice, with Deeney critical of his tactical set-up for the Manchester derby.



The ex-Watford skipper remarked: "I'm going to go for Michael Carrick, the blueprint's there, you've shown us that you can make it work.

"You [should have] put [Matheus] Cunha on the left-hand side, put [Benjamin] Sesko through the middle.

"But his inability to make the harsh calls and drop [Marcus] Rashford, because it's a Manchester derby, 'You need the local lads there,' and all of that nonsense that comes with it, cost them the game.

"Because Rashford coming off the bench when they've got ten men would have been better than Rashford starting."

Sports.title: Sydney Sweeney hit by another huge backlash as her naked betting advert is criticised for 'sexualising women's sport' and branded 'a kick in the face' by Olympic athletes
Sports.content:
See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Sydney Sweeney has been accused of sexualising women’s sport by female Olympians after she posed naked in a betting advert.

The actress, 29, featured in a promotional video for bookmaker Novig in which she used various pieces of sports equipment to cover herself up.

The advert has drawn criticism from across the world of women’s sport, with former Australian Olympic swimmer Ariarne Titmus saying: 'I can’t describe how infuriated I feel when I watch this.'

The four-time gold medallist added: 'Not only is it a kick in the face to every woman who had dedicated her life to perfecting her craft, but every women who enjoys sports for what it really is – teamwork, friendship, dedication, excellent, unity.

'How do we live in a world where monetising a women’s body and sexualising women’s sport is still a thing?'

British sprinter Amy Hunt used her post-race interview at the inaugural World Athletics Ultimate Championship to criticise the actress.

After finishing fourth in her 200m race, Ms Hunt said: 'It was incredible to be part of such an incredible race. Sydney Sweeney, this is what women's sport looks like!'

The 24-year-old – who has previously called herself 'sexy and aggressive' – shot looks straight down the camera as if to address Ms Sweeney directly.

'Hard work, sweat, blood, tears,' Ms Hunt continued. 'This is a beautiful evening.'

Sydney Sweeney has been accused of sexualising women’s sport by female Olympians after she posed naked in a betting advert

American gymnast Gracie Kramer also led the backlash against Ms Sweeney, posting a response on social media that read 'this is what a woman in sport looks like'.

It prompted a wave of responses from female athletes, including American diver Kassidy Cook, and has been liked more than a million times.

Fellow Australian Olympian Matilda Kearns shared a video montage featuring clips of the country's women's water polo team training and competing alongside the words: 'I absolutely f**king hate Sydney Sweeney's new sports ad.'

In the caption, she said: 'Like what are we doing… so much worse than I imagined too. Here's some real women's sports content.'

Australian world champion boxer Skye Nicolson said the advert made a 'mockery' of women in sport. She added on Instagram: 'There’s a big difference between looking "sexy" because you do sport compared to using sex to sell "sport".

'There is nothing wrong with looking good and doing sport and there’s nothing wrong with embracing your femininity while also being a badass athlete.'

British sprinter Hannah Williams also criticised the actress, posting a clip of runners with the caption: 'Hey Sydney Sweeney, this is women in sports.

'The ad is such a disgrace for woman in sports... constantly trying to be respected in a male dominated field.'

Ms Sweeney, 29, featured in a promotional video for bookmaker Novig in which she used various pieces of sports equipment to cover herself up

British sprinter Amy Hunt used her post-race interview at the inaugural World Athletics Ultimate Championship to criticise the actress

Olympic weightlifting coach Danielle Bagacay: 'The sexualisation of women in sport [and in life] is an ongoing issue that most [if not, all] women face.

'This issue disproportionately focuses on physical appearance and, instead, overshadows our achievements, hard work and ability to reach athletic goals.

'My purpose and mission as a coach is to focus on improving my athletes' ability, capacity and capability to reach their strength and performance goals.

'Less about the number on the scales or how they look, and more about feel and empowerment.

'I hope whatever Sydney Sweeney is trying to portray will be overshadowed by other women speaking/posting against the brand campaign.'

Fitness influencer Angela Everington wrote: 'Congratulations Sydney Sweeney, you've just rattled every woman in sport.

'45 per cent of teenage girls say they don't feel they have the 'right body shape' for sport.

'A study of women found 70 per cent had seen girls drop out of sport because of sports kit or body-image concerns.

'I'm sure your marketing would have performed just as well if you used your platform to share what the body can do rather than sexualise it.'

Olympian Matilda Kearns shared a video montage of the Australian national women's water polo team, which was captioned: 'I absolutely f**king hate Sydney Sweeney's new ad'

However, some have voiced support for Ms Sweeney, with one commenter writing on Ms Kearns' post: 'Easy to hate someone you are also jealous of.'

Another said: 'It still brought attention to women's sports... stop being such haters to another woman. Full stop. The end.'

'Why all the hate? What ever happened to women supporting women? She didn't kill her kids or anything,' someone else wrote.

The criticism comes after Novig founder and CEO Jacob Fortinsky revealed that Ms Sweeney, who holds an equity stake in the company, had pushed to appear nude in the campaign.

The Euphoria actress was reportedly drawn to the platform because it focuses strictly on sports predictions, while other platforms allow users to make predictions on a broader range of topics.

'She said, "I'm uncomfortable with other platforms that have markets on what colour underwear I'm going to wear",' Mr Fortinsky recalled in an interview with Front Office Sports.

He added: 'Sydney is great at captivating audiences and being the centre of attention.

Ms Sweeney defended herself by pointing out that male and female athletes have posed nude before

'In some sense, it forces us into the national discourse.'

Ms Sweeney has since hit back at critics of the advert, sharing a series of Instagram Stories that highlight female athletes who have appeared nude.

The actress posted photos of Serena Williams, Ronda Rousey, Sue Bird, Megan Rapinoe and Caroline Wozniacki posing for magazines.

She added that some male athletes have also previously posed nude .

It's not the first time an advertising campaign featuring Ms Sweeney has sparked fierce backlash.

Last year she starred in a controversial American Eagle jeans commercial which some deemed racist due to a pun linking 'jeans' and 'genes'.

The label's campaign featured the tagline: 'Sydney Sweeney Has Great Jeans.'

'Genes are passed down from parents to offspring, often determining traits like hair colour, personality and even eye colour... my genes are blue,' she said an accompanying video.

Last year the actress starred in a controversial American Eagle jeans advert which some deemed racist due to a pun linking 'jeans' and 'genes'

In the fallout, critics of the advert said it promoted eugenics, while US President Donald Trump showed his support for the actress and the brand.

Ms Sweeney told GQ that she found it 'surreal' that the scandal grew so big as to attract attention from the White House.

She said: 'I did a jean ad... I mean, the reaction definitely was a surprise, but I love jeans.

'All I wear are jeans. I'm literally in jeans and a T-shirt every day of my life.'

Critics accused the brand of echoing eugenicist language around 'good genes' and 'genetic superiority', claiming it appealed to Right-wing and white-nationalist groups online.

In August, American Eagle defended the campaign, insisting it 'always was about the jeans – her jeans, her story.'

Sports.title: Worryingly flat on the pitch and mutiny festering in the stands, this was a painful derby defeat for Man United, writes CHRIS WHEELER - Michael Carrick's big Benjamin Sesko call backfired and there's little sign of progress
Sports.content:
Worryingly flat on the pitch and mutiny festering in the stands, this was a painful derby defeat for Man United, writes CHRIS WHEELER - Michael Carrick's big Benjamin Sesko call backfired and there's little sign of progress

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

On this day of all days, when Manchester United should have been united, the fans arrived at Old Trafford with the scent of flares in the air and mutiny in the ranks.

At three o’clock, an hour and a half before kick-off in the 199th Manchester derby, 500 of them gathered at The Bishop Blaize pub around the corner from the stadium and began to march.

Specifically, it was to demonstrate over the club’s clampdown on ticket touting which, according to protest group The 1958, has targeted innocent fans without sufficient evidence.

But discontent has been festering for some time now over United’s attitude to match-going supporters, and longstanding hatred towards the Glazer family has been directed towards minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe and Ineos.

Both ownership groups came under fire as the protesters made their way to Old Trafford, holding banners and setting off flares. Only when they crammed into the Munich Tunnel did their ire turn on Manchester City and the usual derby day chants could be heard.

At roughly the same time, inside Old Trafford another supporters’ group were preparing a message of their own. The Red Army provide and pay for the flags and banners inside the Stretford End, which have been increasing in number and impact in recent years.

On a day when Manchester United should have been united, they were anything but amid fan protests in the stands

Hatred towards the Glazer family has recently been directed towards minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe (pictured) and Ineos

But on this occasion they decided to go with one simple banner displayed above the players’ tunnel. It read: ‘The way you treat us is a disgrace.’

United fans are not militant by nature and it takes a lot for them to turn on the club in this way – and in a game of this magnitude. It demonstrates the level of ill feeling and genuine concern over the way United are being run.

Michael Carrick counts himself as one of them, and didn’t try to duck the issue after a painful derby defeat that will only have darkened the mood among fans.

‘I definitely appreciate the supporters,’ said Carrick. ‘If they do feel that in certain ways, I want to try and make them happy.

‘They are everything for this football club and I’m feeling for them today on the back of losing. I’ll never take them for granted. It means a lot to me.’

Against this backdrop, Carrick was trying to repeat his rousing first game as head coach of United, a 2-0 win over Pep Guardiola’s City here in mid-January.

It set the tone for an excellent run of results under the former United midfielder, which ended with the club returning to the Champions League and Carrick landing the job on a full-time basis.

Instead, this was further evidence that United are still some way short of where they need to be, and that juggling European football with the demands of the Premier League has created a far greater challenge for their head coach.

Michael Carrick did not dodge the topic after the game, admitting 'they are everything for this football club'

After an inauspicious start in the league, taking four points from the first three games against Hull, Ipswich and Everton, the derby came three days after United’s opening Champions League tie against Sabah. It was an easy enough start, but City had two more days to prepare.

Carrick’s side looked worryingly flat against Hull last month and it was a similar story here, even after Phil Foden was sent off in the 23rd minute.

It was puzzling how little threat they posed to City’s ten men for more than an hour of a Manchester derby that was there for the taking.

Yes, Marcus Rashford and Kobbie Mainoo – two homegrown players who could hold their heads up high – hit the post in either half, but it was deep into injury-time when the disappointing Bryan Mbeumo forced Gianluigi Donnarumma into his only real save of the game, and a fine one at that.

This was the first time United have failed to score at Old Trafford under Carrick.

‘In all the games we've won here, we've scored at least two goals,’ he argued. ‘We've lost one game and we scored in that game. At some point you have a game when we haven't scored, so I can't be too critical of the players.

‘Of course, we would hope for more in general from the team. We could have been a little bit more creative. We could have finished the game better, for sure.’

The big call for Carrick was bringing back Matheus Cunha as a false nine for Benjamin Sesko, a more conventional centre forward who got his first start of the season against Sabah and scored for the second game in a row.

It was puzzling how United provided so little threat against the 10 men of their local rivals

It didn’t work. Cunha doesn’t offer enough of a threat centrally, and it was perhaps no coincidence that he also scored against the team from Azerbaijan after reverting to a position on the left flank.

Carrick switched to that game plan when Sesko came on for Youri Tielemans in the 67th minute, but Enzo Maresca already had the measure of his opponents.

The other issue going into this game was the absence of Luke Shaw. United opted against buying cover for Shaw in the summer, possibly encouraged by the fact he started every single Premier League match last season.

It was never going to happen again, and Shaw lasted just four games before going down. When he missed training before Sabah, it was described as a designated day off. But he was sat in the stands on Thursday night and again for the derby.

Patrick Dorgu deputised on both occasions but the Dane is not a natural left back, and questions were asked of him when Erling Haaland scored the controversial winner.

After United’s £155million midfield rebuild this summer, it hasn’t taken long for their issues in defence and attack to surface – and for the fans who protested on Sunday, the lack of progress on the pitch is just one more reason to worry.

Sports.title: Wayne Rooney delivers scathing rant on 'horrendous' VAR after officials' 'baffling' decision to allow Erling Haaland's Manchester derby winner
Sports.content:
Wayne Rooney delivers scathing rant on 'horrendous' VAR after officials' 'baffling' decision to allow Erling Haaland's Manchester derby winner

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Wayne Rooney launched a furious rant against the 'horrendous' VAR decision to let Erling Haaland's winning goal stand against Manchester United.

Referee chiefs have admitted that the call was a mistake in a grovelling apology to United after failing to penalise Enzo Fernandez for straying offside.

The Manchester City midfielder clearly interfered with play immediately before Haaland's goal, challenging Lisandro Martinez for the ball.

But VAR official Matt Donohue allowed the goal on the basis that City’s new £125million signing did not touch it.

And Rooney told Match of the Day: 'I'm just so sick of this VAR. I think it's horrendous.

'It's taken all the emotion out of the game, the energy which the game is played with.

Erling Haaland has put Manchester City ahead in the derby after a VAR check ⚽️ pic.twitter.com/V0DCwryhFy — Sky Sports Premier League (@SkySportsPL) September 13, 2026

Wayne Rooney called the VAR decision to allow Erling Haaland's goal 'horrendous'

Pro Ref have apologised to Manchester United Erling Haaland's controversial derby winner was allowed to stand

'To not see that and recognise that Enzo Fernandez is in an offside position, anyone who's played the game at any level understands and knows that he's in an offside position.

'To get it so wrong, it's just baffling.'

The VAR check was initially into Erling Haaland, who appeared offside from the initial cross, but was actually being played onside by Patrick Dorgu.

Fernandez was let off the hook for his interference, but the rules state that a player in an offside position must be penalised if they affect an opponent by attempting to play the ball.

Joe Hart – who played 348 times for Man City – was gobsmacked at the incident, which led to the club continuing their winning start in the Premier League under Enzo Maresca.

'The fact that Enzo Fernandez is there and makes an attempt to go for the ball, that affects him,' Hart said on Premier League Productions.

'So therefore, by the letter of the law... I can't believe, I absolutely cannot believe that all the people that are involved in making this decision and they've come up with that Enzo Fernandez did not impact the play, because anyone involved in football will tell you right there that he did.'

One man who was certainly disquieted by the decision was United boss Michael Carrick.

Haaland's goal was given after a VAR review, with it having originally been ruled offside

Enzo Fernandez was offside and attempted to go for the ball, but this was overlooked

'If that's the interpretation of not interfering in the game now, that's really worrying for me. It's a staggering explanation,' he said.

'I just don't get it. I really don't get it. I can't understand how they're trying to help referees and putting so many layers behind them with so many people, so many bodies, so many screens, and so many whatever offices they are to try and come up with the right decisions.

'If that's how the rules are interpreted, that you're not interfering with play because you've thrown yourself at the ball six yards from goal and pretty much nearly touched it, which then Leif has to react from.

'On top of that, the line was a bit dubious where they drew the line to start with. It's worrying if that's really how the game's seen by those who are officiating it.'

Martinez added: 'It's the best league in the world, you have the best teams in the world, the best players in the world, and now we have to go home with this injustice.

'I think it was offside. What I can't understand is the rules. He (Fernandez) was there, in front of me, and I went to him. So that's why Haaland was free at the back.

'It's so hard because you lose a derby and you lose three points at home. Every season they're coming to our club and explaining the rules for an hour-and-a-half. They look so confident, and then after that five or six people are making these kind of mistakes. It's unacceptable.'

Pro Ref, formerly known as the PGMOL, said: 'Following the incident in the 60th minute of Sunday's Premier League fixture between Manchester United and Manchester City at Old Trafford, we can provide clarification regarding Erling Haaland's awarded goal.

Join the discussion Should controversial VAR decisions be overturned after the match to restore fairness?

A furious Lisandro Martinez claimed that United were the victims of an 'injustice'

'The on-field decision was offside against Erling Haaland – that was checked by VAR and he was found to be in an onside position.

'In the same attack, it was established that Enzo Fernandez did not play the ball and therefore that makes any offside offence subjective, however, on this occasion, the VAR did not recognise the likely impact of his position and should have recommended an on-field review.

'Contact has been made with Manchester United this evening to acknowledge what we deem is an error of judgement. A review of the incident will take place.'

Sports.title: West Ham legend Ludek Miklosko dead aged 64: Tributes pour in for 'gentle giant' as former Hammers goalkeeper and coach passes away after long battle with cancer
Sports.content:
West Ham have announced the death of their legendary former goalkeeper and coach Ludek Miklosko aged 64.

The Czech star, who played in 373 matches for the Hammers between 1990 and 1997, has passed away after a battle with cancer.

Miklosko, known by supporters as 'Ludo', last visited the London Stadium in December 2024 as a Guest of Honour against Liverpool, having confirmed his cancer diagnosis.

Since then, fans have sung his ‘my name is Ludek Miklosko, I come from near Moscow, I play in goal for West Ham’ chant at each match.

'The giant goalkeeper will forever hold a special place in the hearts of the West Ham family,' the club said.

'Everyone at West Ham United would like to extend their sincere condolences to Ludek’s family and loved ones and this very sad time.'

Legendary former West Ham goalkeeper Ludek Miklosko has died aged 64 after a cancer battle

The much-loved Czech 'gentle giant' made 373 outings for West Ham and also played for QPR

Miklosko won two promotions with the Hammers, reached the semi-finals of the FA Cup and League Cup, and even prevented Sir Alex Ferguson's Manchester United from winning the Premier League in 1995 with a man-of-the-match performance.

He also played for Queens Park Rangers in English football.

The 'gentle giant' also made 42 appearances for his country, and played for Hvezda Cheb and Banik Ostrava in his homeland. Most recently, he headed up the sports department at the latter, one of the biggest Czech clubs.

Tributes have been pouring in for Miklosko.

Former West Ham team-mate Julian Dicks wrote on X: 'Very sad news today, the passing of Ludo, I will see you again one day my friend. Plus don’t forget to have a Czech Bud waiting for me.'

David Trunda, the head of the Czech football association, said: 'With deep sorrow, I received the news of the death of Ludek Miklosko, one of the prominent figures of Czech football.

'Ludek Miklosko has significantly inscribed himself into its history with his performances as well as his approach to football, earning respect not only in the Czech Republic but also abroad.

'His name will forever be associated with a significant era of Czech football and with the values that he represented as both a player and a person. On behalf of the Football Association of the Czech Republic and on my own behalf, I express my sincere condolences to his family, loved ones, friends, and all those who had the opportunity to know Ludek and collaborate with him.

'Ludo', left, was a hugely popular figure at West Ham and tributes have been pouring in for him

'Honour to his memory.'

Talksport broadcaster Ian Abrahams wrote: 'A gentle giant, a phenomenal goalkeeper, I was lucky enough to meet Ludo on a few occasions and he was a great gentleman. Thoughts with his friends, family and all at West Ham.'

One fan wrote: 'Such sad news today of the passing of Ludek Miklosko. Often signed my programme from behind the North Bank goal at Upton Park, and fortunate enough to have met him after his playing days. A goalkeeping phenomenon. RIP 'Big Ludo.'

Author Mick Clifford added: 'Devastated to hear the sad news that club legend Ludek Miklosko has passed away. Condolences to his family and friends at this difficult time.'

Miklosko had an operation to remove a lump on his hip in 2021 but another tumour developed in his stomach.

He opted against chemotherapy, saying: 'I decided not to undergo chemotherapy because I want to live a normal life.

'When they told me what chemotherapy would entail, it would mean that I would not be able to work or be with my colleagues for about six months, I would not be able to travel and so on. I said no, I don't want that

'I have great people around me, I have my job and football, which is my life. Everything I know. I want to continue doing it as long as I can.'

Aussie fitness star Joanna Wietrzyk has sparked a storm of controversy after powering to victory in a HYROX race despite appearing to suffer a shocking bowel incontinence accident mid-event.

Wietrzyk, 22, refused to stop during the gruelling Beijing competition over the weekend, continuing with what appeared to be faecal matter running down her legs as she completed burpees, lunges, and wall balls.

Her decision to push on and ultimately win triggered biohazard concerns and fierce criticism online, with viewers questioning why officials allowed her to continue competing.

An unapologetic Wietrzyk posted an image while recovering in hospital, saying: 'Go hard or go home they say ... a win is a win.

'In all seriousness, thank you for all the support. I'll be back soon.'

HYROX China said affected areas and race lanes were immediately closed and isolated, then thoroughly disinfected.

Aussie fitness star Joanna Wietrzyk has sparked a storm of controversy after powering to victory in a HYROX race despite appearing to suffer a shocking bowel incontinence accident mid-event

Wietrzyk refused to stop during the gruelling Beijing competition over the weekend, continuing with what appeared to be faecal matter running down her legs as she completed burpees, lunges, and wall balls

Cleaning continued until the day's racing concluded, while affected equipment was removed from the venue.

Waste was disposed of under local regulations, with organisers saying the measures were intended to strengthen hygiene safeguards.

Carpets would be replaced after the day's events, followed by a deep clean and disinfection of the entire venue.

'We ask all participating athletes to compete with peace of mind, and we wish everyone the ideal performance and a smooth completion of the race,' organisers said in a statement.

However, some viewers questioned why Wietrzyk had been allowed to continue, given HYROX explicitly bans spitting, snot rockets and littering during the race.

HYROX China said affected areas and race lanes were immediately closed and isolated, then thoroughly disinfected

Another said: 'Disgusting. This person is not a hero. She is super selfish. Not a care for any other competitor that has to follow.'

A third demanded her removal from the event, writing: 'She should've been immediately disqualified with her nasty ass.'

Others argued that the stakes for a professional athlete helped explain her decision.

'She is a professional - so this race performance gives her income for months and years to come,' one supporter wrote.

One podcast host discussing the footage also questioned the potential impact on athletes following her through the exercise stations.

The HYROX format sees competitors alternate between a 1km run and a functional workout station, repeated eight times. Wietrzyk completed the event covered in faecal matter

She went on to win the race despite the accident

Join the discussion Should athletes risk competitors' health to finish a race at all costs?

'Because of the nature of this sport, you go to different stations. So you do running, you do burpees, you do row machine ... you do stuff like this with the medicine ball,' the host said.

'If you are doing burpees and this person in front of you has stuff on their legs, you don't know what you're putting your hands on.'

The host acknowledged volunteers' efforts to clean behind the competitor but questioned how thoroughly that could be done while racing continued.

'But at the same time, it's like, you're in the middle of a race, how thorough can they be if they want to keep the race going at the pace it's supposed to be going?'

The eight workout stations are 1,000m SkiErg (simulating Nordic skiing), 50m Sled Push. 50m Sled Pull, 80m Burpee Broad Jumps, 1,000m row, 200m Farmer’s Carry (walking while holding heavy kettlebells or weights), 100m Sandbag Lunges, 100 Wall Balls (squatting and throwing a medicine ball to a target).

HYROX has surged in popularity in recent years, especially among ageing millennials and office workers, and now stages events around the world.

Sports.title: Tennis stars END protests over Grand Slam prize money - after almost £80MILLION was available to players at US Open
Sports.content:
Tennis stars from both the men’s and women’s tours have formally ended their year-long protests against the four Grand Slams over increased prize money.

Their public objections have ceased after they secured a negotiating council to work with the majors directly.

Top players including Jannik Sinner, Jessica Pegula, Aryna Sabalenka, and Carlos Alcaraz joined the calls for prize money to reflect 22 per cent of each tournament's revenue. Stars raised awareness with media boycotts.

But with the conclusion of New York’s Grand Slam, the players involved have now announced the end of the ‘public phase’ of their campaign, following a number of staggering prize money hikes since the protests began.

Early positive discussions warded off disruptions in Melbourne, but at the French Open, players involved in the protests limited their media appearances to 15 minutes for press conferences and broadcast interviews, in a bid to highlight how the £53.3million prize pot was just 15 per cent of the tournament’s total revenue.

Additional protests were planned for Wimbledon and set to stretch from the media weekend into the first week of the Championships.

Tennis stars have ended their 'public' protests over Grand Slam prize money

Alexander Zverev and Elena Rybakina (above) won $5.5million (£4.08m) for their US Open titles - $500,000 more than the 2025 champions

But following more positive communications between the two entities, and a year-on-year 20 per cent prize money boost – the biggest rise in its history, to £64.2million – these were called off at the 11th hour.

Wimbledon chair Debbie Jevans had previously brushed aside suggestions that the Championships’ prize pot could be sensibly linked to the tournament’s revenue due to its role in sharing profits with British grassroots tennis.

‘Revenue does not take into the investment that we give,’ she said in June. ‘We are not-for-profit, and very different to a Masters 1000.’

An eye-watering £79.2million ($108million) purse available to players in New York, as well as £1.47m ($2m) pledged towards a player welfare fund, took protests off the table for the final major of the year.

Shortly after that bumper rise was announced came news that the majors would form a Grand Slam Player Advisory Council to ‘serve as the forum for direct communication, feedback, and collaboration between the Grand Slams and the players’.

Although a founder of a separate organisation, the Professional Tennis Players Association – which he has since stepped away from – Novak Djokovic was not among the players to take part in the protests. Alcaraz is believed to have stepped away before the tournament began at Flushing Meadows.

Those involved in the protest, many of whom rake in millions in prize money and lucrative sponsorship deals, have taken pains to explain that they are not looking to boost their own coffers, but to ensure that lower-ranked players are able to fund their season with a Grand Slam appearance.

'I don’t really see how it can be possible to cross these two completely different worlds. And as I said before, prize money, it’s not like it’s about me at all,’ Sabalenka said in Paris when asked how she could square sporting £120,000-worth of jewellery on-court with demanding greater riches.

‘It’s just fighting for players, lower ranked players who are really struggling to survive in this tennis world. It has nothing to do with me that I’m fighting for the prize money. Everyone knows that I’m okay.

‘It’s just that we are fighting for a fair amount fair percentage out of the revenues and also for the lower ranked, players coming back after injuries, the next generation to be more comfortable coming into the top-10. So it’s not about me.’

Sports.title: Moment Noel Gallagher's nepo baby son Sonny, 15, puts his middle fingers up at fans after Erling Haaland scores goal during Man City vs Man United match
Sports.content:
Moment Noel Gallagher's nepo baby son Sonny, 15, puts his middle fingers up at fans after Erling Haaland scores goal during Man City vs Man United match

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Noel Gallagher's 15-year-old son was spotted giving the middle finger to Man United fans after Man City's Erling Haaland scored the controversial deciding goal at Old Trafford.

Sonny Gallagher celebrated alongside his brother Donovan, 18, and their Oasis rockstar father Noel, 59, in the stands 62 minutes into the game, with City a man down after Phil Foden's red card.

The teenager flipped off rival fans in the stands and jeered as star striker Haaland netted in the second-half what later proved to be the winner.

His gesture will have rubbed salt in the wounds as it came after a lengthy VAR check that the home supporters thought would rule out the strike for offside. But the goal was incorrectly awarded and gave City a lead they held on to.

Sonny's father, meanwhile, punched the air in jubilation and chanted, clapping as his youngest son gave both middle fingers to their opponents.

The Gallaghers are known for being die-hard Manchester City fans, and have been supporters long before the club became the dominant Premier League force it is today.

Oasis have been the musical backdrop of the successes that City has amassed since Sheikh Mansour bought the club in 2008.

Gallagher and his brother, Liam, have become the team's most recognisable supporters.

Sonny Gallagher (pictured in a blue jacket, second from left) gave the middle finger to Man United fans after his team scored a goal

He was watching the game alongside his brother Donovan (pictured second from left, in a grey jacket) and rockstar father Noel (third from left)

The moment Erling Haaland scored a goal against Man United, taking his team to a 1-0 victory

Noel is even close friends with the club's former manager, Pep Guardiola, who transformed the club over his nearly decade in charge.

On Sunday, Noel's sons were recognisable in the crowd, with Sonny donning a navy and blue jacket in his father's Mod rocker style.

It is the brothers' second outing with their celebrity father this week, after making an appearance at the premiere of Oasis: Don't Look Back In Anger in London.

Sonny was the spitting image of his rocker dad after borrowing his vintage 2008 Stone Island jacket for the event - with a matching haircut to fit.

Noel had worn the jacket at a press conference in Wembley to announce a stadium tour nearly two decades ago.

He declared at the time the shows would be 'the gigs of next year, if not the decade' after announcing they would perform for three nights at the arena.

Liam and Noel Gallagher proved that all past feuds were behind them by appearing together, fresh from an eight-minute standing ovation at the Venice Film Festival last weekend.

Liam and Noel's nepo baby brood were out in force earlier this week to support their fathers' upcoming documentary (from left to right: Lennon, Donovan, Anais, Molly, Sonny and Gene Gallagher)

They posed with their broods in Leicester Square, with the two brothers' children being united with their cousins after their parents' 15-year public spat.

The brotherly appearance was a far cry from the days of backstage bust-ups, walk-outs and booze-fuelled arguments in the public eye.

Beaming and wrapping their arms around each other on Monday night were Liam’s son Lennon, 26, Noel’s son Donovan, 18, and his model daughter Anais, 26.

They were joined by Liam’s daughter, Molly, 28, Sonny and Liam’s other boy Gene, 25.

The new Disney+ documentary chronicles their split and reconciliation, while following the band on their reunion tour last year.

Noel tells the Disney+ documentary that he and Liam’s children didn’t even know each other before the reunion tour.

'Donovan and Sonny had never met Gene and Lennon. Lo and behold they’re best friends now,' he said. Liam joked: ‘They’re off their heads every night. F****** spangled.'

Sports.title: Goading, running himself into the ground and feeding off Man United disdain - Enzo Fernandez showed what £125m buys you and his innate desire to win at all costs is gold dust for City
Sports.content:
Goading, running himself into the ground and feeding off Man United disdain - Enzo Fernandez showed what £125m buys you and his innate desire to win at all costs is gold dust for City

A goal up and a man light, there is a specific type of person required when the heat of a derby tumble dryer is dialled up that little bit higher. Certainly not a shrinker.

Probably the sort of person who might goad opposition supporters by cupping his ears and pulling a frankly ridiculously stupid face in a World Cup semi-final. That guy. The sort who craves and feeds off rival disdain.

The sort of guy who, after a 22-minute masterclass following Erling Haaland's disputed winner, might grin his way off the Old Trafford pitch when substituted. The sort of guy who will enjoy playing the villain at Premier League stadiums all year.

He may have joined on deadline day for a British record fee but Sunday was when Enzo Fernandez arrived as a Manchester City player, the exact personality Enzo Maresca needed to engineer an away victory that can serve as a springboard for a new project given the circumstances.

It wasn't necessarily the buying of two free kicks in quick succession just inside Manchester United territory but those symbolised the management of the lead. It wasn't intercepting Diogo Dalot's errant pass and driving City forward 25 yards, ending in a foul, but that symbolised a determination.

It wasn't riling up Harry Maguire during a mild flashpoint, nor was it almost bending in a second goal from outside the box. It was all of these things and more that made Fernandez such an integral aspect of a win that saw Maresca dancing down the touchline like a certain Portuguese all those years ago.

There is a specific type of person required when the heat of a derby tumble dryer is dialled up - and that person is Enzo Fernandez

At the time that the fourth official's board beamed Fernandez's number – 17, formerly Kevin De Bruyne's – nobody had covered more ground than his 10.2kilometres. This was a shift alongside the commanding Elliot Anderson, that was non-negotiable if City were to emerge with a positive result. Nobody broke up play more than Fernandez and, given United's penchant for fast breaks through central areas, City's back four are under significantly more stress without that.

They are the little things that add up to £125million and that fee buys you somebody who can do everything, with the Argentine's role before Phil Foden's sending off more attacking and more lateral. As evidenced by the assist for Haaland in Porto on Tuesday, he fancies that side of the box-to-box role.

'Look at our midfield, if there is something they like to do, it is to fight,' Haaland said with a twinkle down the Old Trafford tunnel. He meant the collective, although his body language suggested a clear focus on one of them specifically. We all know who that is.

And for Fernandez, this has been a rewarding first fortnight in sky blue, while the animosity among those in royal blue shows no real sign of abating. There has been amusement in City circles over the past few days at noises emanating from Chelsea about two written transfer requests handed in by Fernandez to force a move and the accusation that he told the hierarchy that his relationships with team-mates had deteriorated, seemingly beyond repair.

A gentle bemusement as to why, some time after the transfer window closed, the 25-year-old continues to be such a hot topic of discussion. Especially after Xabi Alonso had praised his attitude and application after the mid-August deadline to complete a £120m deal passed without incident.

It has been a summer – nay, a year – of blue on blue in this respect. Acrimony between Chelsea and City over Maresca, for starters.

Then the saga attached to the failed attempt to lure Bunny Shaw away from City amid a reported £1m contract on the table. And to cap it, losing their best player to City as well. This after asking Hugo Viana to walk away from a deal to sign Ayyoub Bouaddi from Lille during negotiations for Fernandez and suggesting a swap of Nico O'Reilly for Malo Gusto – suggestions that are denied by Chelsea, who lost last season's FA Cup final to Antoine Semenyo's clever flick.

Chelsea – who in April announced the highest pre-tax losses (£262.4m) in Premier League history – have made it known that they could have pulled the plug on Fernandez's move north after their own pursuit of Monaco's Lamine Camara collapsed.

Fernandez, who clashed with Harry Maguire, was described as 'unbelievable' by his manager, Enzo Maresca

They didn't and that is to Maresca's benefit. 'Enzo was unbelievable,' he said at Old Trafford, Fernandez right in the middle of the winner after standing in an offside position, a contentious moment.

City could have avoided the broader contention with Chelsea, having watched Fernandez extensively while at River Plate before he joined Benfica in 2022. So it is not only Maresca's whim that has demanded he join.

What they have in him is this innate desire to win at all costs. There has been an argument that since the Treble campaign, City have lacked that bit of extra competitive spirit, the darker arts. The sort of player who burrows under the skin of those who love to hate him.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."

Collins: Ireland must build on World Cup near miss

Ireland captain Nathan Collins is confident his side have laid the foundations to qualify for future tournaments having seen hopes of reaching this summer's World Cup finals come to an end.

Collins and his team-mates were agonisingly close to the play-off final when they led the Czech Republic 2-1 in Prague on Thursday evening with just four minutes of normal time remaining.

Image: A dejected Nathan Collins and head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson

However, Czech skipper Ladislav Krejci's late equaliser took the tie to extra-time and ultimately to penalties, where the hosts prevailed 4-3 to extend Ireland's wait for a first return to the big stage since 2002.

Asked about their progression to the play-offs, which was secured by back-to-back wins over Armenia, Portugal and Hungary, Brentford defender Collins said: "I'm not seeing many positives right now because we're in the gutter.

"But what we've created, the environment created with the fans and country, has been special. That's something we need to keep growing, to get even better at.

"That can help us get better on the pitch. We can push that and get fans to more tournaments."

Ireland had hoped to return to the Aviva Stadium on Tuesday for a showdown with either Denmark or North Macedonia for a place in the finals, but the Czechs will now host the Danes, who were 4-0 winners in Copenhagen.

Instead, Heimir Hallgrimsson's side face a friendly against the Macedonians.

Collins said: "The motivation has to be the same. We've to win to keep improving as a team and country. Any game we play at home is a big game."

Sports.title: 'Pain' - Irish heartbreak as Czech Republic win on penalties
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland's World Cup hopes were cruelly and heartbreakingly dashed as Czech Republic came from 2-0 down - to then beat them on penalties.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, who went two goals up after 23 minutes in Prague, were four minutes plus stoppage-time away from victory - before Wolves defender Ladislav Krejci headed in a corner to force extra-time.

Ireland were also a handful of penalties away from going through, as penalty saving expert Caomhin Kelleher saved from Mojmír Chytil in the shoot-out to give them a momentary advantage.

But Finn Azaz and Alan Browne both missed their spot kicks, allowing Patrick Schick and then Jan Kliment to win it for the hosts.

As a result, Czech Republic will go on to face Denmark on Tuesday for a spot at the World Cup - as Ireland's wait for a first World Cup appearance since 2002 goes on.

After Wales and Northern Ireland's semi-final exits, it also means England and Scotland will be the only teams from Great Britain and Ireland at the World Cup this summer.

Image: Ireland's players walk off the pitch after defeat

World Cup play-off finals - Europe Bosnia & Herzegovina vs Italy

Sweden vs Poland

Kosovo vs Turkey

Czech Republic vs Denmark

How Ireland threw away their lead

Ireland came flying out the blocks flying in Prague. Four shots in the opening ten minutes, including Nathan Collins crashing a shot off the bar from range, set the tone for a brilliant display - and they got their rewards.

A long throw caused chaos and Nathan Collins was deemed to have been caught slightly late by Vladimir Darida by VAR, who sent referee Glenn Byberg to the monitor for a review.

Troy Parrott, who else, crashed in the penalty for his sixth goal in the last three Ireland matches. And it got better for Ireland four minutes later.

Ryan Manning's corner found Dara O'Shea at the back post and his header across was cleared off the line by Vladimir Coufal - but off goalkeeper Matej Kovar and over the line.

Image: Czech Republic goalkeeper Matej Kovar scores an own goal to give Ireland a 2-0 lead

Ireland were in dreamland but a moment of Manning madness brought the Czech Republic back into it. The defender's needless tug back on Krekci - when the ball was heading out of play - was penalised by referee Byberg, with Patrick Schick pulling one back from the spot.

Ireland did, however, manage to settle the nerves down - right throughout the second half. Despite sustained Czech pressure in the second half, they barely threatened.

It was Ireland who had the better chances after the break, with Jayson Molumby striking the post and Parrott denied by a solid Kovar save at a corner. But then heartbreak struck with four minutes of normal time remaining, as Krejci bundled the ball in at the near post from a set piece.

Krejci could have even won it with the last kick of the game but scuffed his finish, as extra-time came.

Substitute Tomas Soucek missed a glorious chance for the hosts, with Adam Idah was denied a one-on-one chance by a goal-saving challenge from Stepan Chaloupek. Penalties came and the lottery fell in the hosts' favour.

Image: Jan Kliment scored the winning goal in the penalty shoot-out

Hallgrimsson confident in Ireland future despite 'pain'

Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson:

"One word is pain. I feel pain. I feel pride for the performance of the players. They gave it all. I feel gratitude for all the supporters who supported us through the whole game, even after the loss. I feel pride being a part of that group. Personally, I know all the players will feel pain now. Only pain.

"We take with us that we can play teams higher in the FIFA ranking and can punch above our weight: Portugal, Hungary and here. We can compete with these teams. We came here with three wins in a row, a long time since that happened for this national team.

"So there's growth in this squad. It's maturing. These are been the biggest game most of these players have played. That's encouraging to know we're growing. It's strange to say that after we lost today.

"I know I'm biased in this, all the statistics and metrics of the team have improved. Big games, being on the line, crunch times all the time, we've managed to go through this. It showed the resilience, character of these players, that's why I feel confident going on."

Sports.title: Wilson key for Wales, NI aim for big upset while history beckons for ROI
Sports.content:
Sky Sports assesses Thursday's 2026 World Cup play-off semi-finals as Wales host Bosnia-Herzegovina, Northern Ireland go to four-time winners Italy and the Republic of Ireland face Czech Republic in Prague.

Thursday 7.45pm: Wales vs Bosnia-Herzegovina (winner will play Italy or Northern Ireland)

Harry Wilson is not the new Gareth Bale, but he's doing the job of Bale at his best, especially for Wales.

Fans have long been excited about Wilson's natural talent, but are now seeing his influence in the Premier League on a weekly basis for Fulham. This season, he has 10 goals and six assists for club, while for country, his stats are even better with five goals and two assists in his last five games.

If Wilson starts running the show, his confidence will feed to the other players and to the home crowd, and Wales will be very difficult to stop on their own patch.

Which World Cup group would Wales be in? If Wales qualify for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Craig Bellamy wanted to create an identity for Wales when he took over as head coach. It's now clear: he wants front-foot football coupled with intensity and energy.

Bellamy doesn't always see that in international football as he finds it slower at times compared with club football, but his Wales side will not be ponderous. You could see during the qualification campaign that Wales' intensity in winning the ball back very quickly and holding possession grew. Now it's about consistently doing it.

Apart from consistency in play, there needs to be consistency in selection. Much is always made about the 'spine' of a good team, from the goalkeeper to the glory hunter! Leeds United provide a fair chunk of Wales' spine with 'keeper Karl Darlow on form and in receipt of the No.1 keeper's jersey. Joe Rodon is the rock at centre-back that success relies upon, while team-mate Ethan Ampadu's versatility means he can link anywhere between defence and midfield. Throw in one of the in-form Premier League stars, Harry Wilson, and a strong spine can take a team a long way.

Ask Bellamy if he has thought about preparing for the play-off final against either Italy or Northern Ireland and you'll get glared at. It's Bosnia, Bosnia and Bosnia. He won't entertain anything beyond Bosnia until the game is over. It's a danger, a banana skin he wants to avoid. Thinking too far ahead isn't good on this occasion.

Geraint Hughes

Thursday 7.45pm: Italy vs Northern Ireland (winner will play Wales or Bosnia-Herzegovina)

On paper, perhaps in reality, it's David vs Goliath.

Northern Ireland enjoy David vs Goliath. Once upon a time it was David (Healy) vs England and David (Healy) vs Spain.

For smaller nations there is comfort in being the underdog. A loss would be met without a major backlash, a win makes you a hero. That's how Michael O'Neill's side will approach Thursday's assignment in Bergamo against Italy.

Which World Cup group would Northern Ireland be in? If Northern Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Conor Bradley and Daniel Ballard are out. Between them they represent 50 per cent of the Northern Ireland players currently plying their trade in the Premier League.

The pair's absence is as much a blow to Northern Ireland's attacking prospects as it is defensively. Ballard represents their best aerial threat from set-pieces, Bradley their most dynamic player on the ball.

And yet for some reason that only football can explain, hope remains. The four-time World Cup winners are heavy favourites but far from the Azzurri powerhouse of old.

If Northern Ireland have it their way, it's unlikely to be a pretty spectacle. But can they frustrate their hosts? 0-0 at half-time? Pounce on the sense of angst that will exist among the home support?

To call it a free hit would be to downplay the importance of the game. But Northern Ireland are free from the weight of expectation.

Daring to dream of a result that becomes instant folklore.

Michael Morrow

Thursday 7.45pm: Czech Republic vs Republic of Ireland (winner will play Denmark or North Macedonia)

Image: Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson and captain Seamus Coleman spoke to the media in Prague

History beckons for the Republic of Ireland here in Prague.

Make no mistake, this will be the biggest game to date for a lot of these Irish players as they attempt to take another step to this summer's World Cup but they must get past Czech Republic to do so.

Which World Cup group would Republic of Ireland be in? If the Republic of Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group A with co-hosts Mexico, South Africa and South Korea.

Still coming off the euphoria of the incredible back-to-back wins against Portugal and Hungary last November, this is an Irish team full of confidence.

Having spoken to a few people around the Czech Republic team, those results have been noted and they are particularly worried about Irish striker Troy Parrott, who scored five goals in those two games in November - including the 96th-minute winner against Hungary.

Head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson spoke ahead of this game about one of the key aspects is visually and mentally being ready for the challenge ahead of them, he seemed as calm and confident as usual.

However his key selection dilemma is does he bring back the experienced, tried and tested players such as Seamus Coleman, Robbie Brady and Chiedoze Ogbene - all three have had limited game-time this season for a variety of injuries.

Coleman and Brady especially are the only two players in the squad who were part of Ireland's last team in a major tournament which was in 2016 - their experience could prove vital.

Image: Can Troy Parrott recreate his Irish heroics in Prague on Thursday?

Their opponents are in a state of flux.

Czech Republic have a new head coach who takes charge of his first game on Thursday, with West Ham's Tomas Soucek also being stripped of the captaincy after November's internationals having caused shockwaves in the local media - Wolves' Ladislav Krejci has replaced him.

The pressure feels like it's all on the home side which could play into Ireland's advantage as they look to take another step to qualify for this summer's World Cup - their first since 2002.

Danyal Khan
