World.title: Writing matric finals soon? Here are 6 free study resources you can use
World.content:
Getting ready for matric finals? These free online resources offer past papers, study guides, textbooks and revision help. Image: canva

With the 2026 matric final exams approaching, Grade 12 learners are entering one of the most important parts of the school year.

While there are plenty of paid tutoring services, study platforms and revision courses available, learners do not necessarily need to spend money to get extra help.

Several free resources are available online, including official past examination papers, study guides, textbooks and revision programmes.



Here are some worth knowing about.

1. Past matric exam papers from the Department of Basic Education

One of the most useful resources for any matric learner is also completely free: past examination papers.

The Department of Basic Education (DBE) provides previous National Senior Certificate (NSC) examination papers online, including papers from recent years.

The papers allow learners to familiarise themselves with the format of the exam and identify areas where they need more practice.

The DBE currently provides papers going back to 2021, as well as older examination papers.

Learners can also use past papers under timed conditions to simulate the real examination.



Find the free study resource here: https://www.education.gov.za/Curriculum/NationalSeniorCertificate(NSC)Examinations/NSCPastExaminationpapers.aspx

2. Mind the Gap study guides

The DBE’s Mind the Gap study guides are another useful free resource.

The guides were developed specifically to help Grade 12 learners prepare for their NSC examinations and cover a range of subjects, including Mathematics, Mathematical Literacy, Physical Sciences, Life Sciences, Accounting, Economics and Geography.

There are also English language and literature guides covering prescribed works.

Rather than trying to work through an entire textbook again, learners can use these guides to focus on important curriculum content and revision.

Find the free study resource here: https://www.education.gov.za/Curriculum/LearningandTeachingSupportMaterials(LTSM)/MindtheGapStudyGuides.aspx

3. Siyavula

For learners who need additional help with Mathematics and Physical Sciences, Siyavula offers free online resources.

Its practice platform includes past-paper-style questions, automatic marking and step-by-step solutions. Learners can work through complete papers or practise specific topics where they are struggling.

Siyavula also provides open textbooks for South African CAPS subjects, which can be read online or downloaded.

There is another useful benefit for learners trying to save data: Siyavula says its website is currently zero-rated on MTN and Cell C in South Africa, although learners still need mobile connectivity and external links may use data.

Find the free study resource here: https://www.siyavula.com/products/learners

4. The DBE’s Second Chance resources

The DBE’s Second Chance Programme is not only for people rewriting matric.

Its online resources include examination readiness material, Grade 12 exemplars, past papers, Mind the Gap guides, Siyavula textbooks and various revision materials.

The programme also provides multimedia resources, including video tutorials and radio and television lessons.

This makes it particularly useful for learners who prefer watching or listening to explanations rather than simply reading through notes.

Find the free study resource here: https://www.education.gov.za/Programmes/SecondChanceProgramme.aspx

5. Woza Matrics

Learners can also make use of Woza Matrics, a DBE programme designed to provide matric learners with additional lessons and study support.

The programme provides learning materials and lessons through television, online platforms and radio.

According to the DBE, from 1 September, Woza Matrics broadcasts four hours of catch-up lessons a day, seven days a week, covering six key subjects.

For learners who are struggling with a particular subject, these lessons can provide another way of going over the work before the exams.

Find the free study resource here: https://www.education.gov.za/WozaMatrics.aspx

6. Don’t overlook free study-planning resources

Studying more does not necessarily mean studying better.

The DBE’s Thutong education portal also provides advice on study skills, including planning and scheduling revision.

Its guidance recommends breaking study time into specific sessions and setting out exactly which subject or section will be covered during each session.

This can be particularly useful during the final weeks, when learners have multiple subjects competing for their attention.

Find the free study resource here: https://www.thutong.doe.gov.za/LearningChannelStudySkills/tabid/5059/Default.aspx

World.title: Fifth woman found dead as Kempton Park serial killer fears intensify
World.content:
Police have found a fifth woman dead near Kempton Park, while SAPS specialists examine whether the latest case is connected to four other women’s deaths under investigation. Image: Pexels

Police have found a fifth woman dead near Kempton Park, adding fresh urgency to an investigation that has already prompted fears of a possible serial killer.

Authorities discovered the woman’s body in Olifantsfontein on Monday morning, 14 September.

SAPS national spokesperson Brigadier Athlenda Mathe said the woman had visible bruising and was not fully clothed. Her body had not decomposed. Preliminary observations also suggested she may have died elsewhere before someone left her at the scene.



The latest discovery brings the number of women found dead in and around Kempton Park to five in about two months.

The cases have fuelled fears of a possible serial killer, but SAPS has not confirmed that one person is responsible or that all five cases are linked.

Mathe said specialists still need to analyse the cases before police can reach that conclusion.



“Our experts must paint a picture to confirm that we are dealing with a serial killer,” she said.

Fifth body changes scope of Kempton Park probe

As The South African previously reported, police initially launched a multidisciplinary investigation after officers found four women dead between July and September.

SAPS released details about each case on Sunday, 13 September.



Police found the first victim, a 37-year-old woman, near the R21 on 15 July. She was naked and restrained with cable ties. Detectives arrested a suspect on 17 July. He remains in custody in connection with that case.

a 37-year-old woman, near the R21 on 15 July. She was naked and restrained with cable ties. Detectives arrested a suspect on 17 July. He remains in custody in connection with that case. Police found the second victim, a 32-year-old woman , near the R21 on 24 August. She was partially clothed.

, near the R21 on 24 August. She was partially clothed. Officers discovered a third woman on 10 September. Her body was naked and in an advanced state of decomposition. Police had not formally identified her when they briefed the media on Sunday.

on 10 September. Her body was naked and in an advanced state of decomposition. Police had not formally identified her when they briefed the media on Sunday. The fourth woman, aged 38, was found behind a hotel in Rhodesfield on 12 September. Police confirmed that she was wearing sports clothing and was partially clothed. Her identity remained subject to formal confirmation by her family.

Monday’s discovery has now forced the task team to consider a fifth case. The multidisciplinary team held an urgent meeting in Midrand following the discovery.

Are the deaths linked?

Police have repeatedly cautioned against drawing conclusions too early.

Acting Gauteng Police Commissioner Major General Fred Kekana said on Sunday that similarities existed in some of the cases, but investigators did not yet have enough evidence to establish a common perpetrator.



“We are not limiting ourselves to one suspect or one theory,” Kekana said during the briefing.

Investigators are comparing dockets, timelines, locations, victim profiles and forensic evidence. SAPS has also brought in its Investigative Psychology Unit to examine behavioural patterns and possible connections.

The latest case means investigators must now determine whether the Olifantsfontein death has any connection to those already under review.



Missing runner’s family awaiting answers

The investigation has also unfolded alongside the disappearance of Kempton Park runner Elizabeth “Tsontso” Moselakgomo, 38.

Moselakgomo went missing on 9 September after leaving her Rhodesfield home for a routine run. She did not return.

After authorities found the fourth woman on Saturday, Moselakgomo’s family said they could not confirm whether the body was hers and urged members of the public not to circulate unverified information.



As of Sunday, the family was awaiting the formal mortuary identification process.

Police have not publicly confirmed that the fourth victim is Moselakgomo.

Separate dating-app warning

Kempton Park police have also raised concern about a separate series of crimes involving dating apps and social media.



Police recorded about 10 cases in which victims allegedly met people online before suspects lured them to locations and robbed or sexually assaulted them.

SAPS has not linked those cases to the women’s deaths.

Police deploy maximum resources

SAPS has deployed detectives, forensic specialists, tracking teams, K9 Search and Rescue members and investigative psychology experts.



Police have also urged women in Kempton Park and surrounding areas to remain cautious, particularly when walking or running alone in isolated places.

The discovery of a fifth woman has intensified public concern. Residents gathered in Kempton Park on Monday amid calls for police to find those responsible.

For now, police say the evidence must determine whether investigators are dealing with one offender, several perpetrators or unrelated cases.

World.title: Suspected poacher killed by elephant in Kruger National Park
World.content:
A suspected poacher was found dead inside the Kruger National Park after allegedly encountering a herd of elephants. Image: Wikimedia Commons

A suspected poacher was found dead inside the Kruger National Park after allegedly encountering a herd of elephants while illegally inside the protected area.

SANParks said KNP Rangers received information on Saturday, 12 September 2026, about two suspected poachers who had allegedly entered the park through the Pafuri area on Friday.

READ | Poacher jailed after death of pregnant pangolin Naledi



Preliminary information indicates that the pair encountered a herd of elephants and fled in different directions, losing contact with one another.

One of the suspects later returned home and reported that his accomplice was missing. He allegedly told authorities that he had heard the man screaming during the incident.

The matter was reported to the South African Police Service (SAPS), with assistance from members of the local community.

One suspect was subsequently arrested and allegedly admitted to participating in the unlawful entry into the Kruger National Park.

He then accompanied SANParks Rangers from the Pafuri Ranger Post to the area where the incident was believed to have taken place.

Rangers followed tracks from the Luvuvhu River for approximately six kilometres into the park, where they discovered the body of the missing suspect.



During the search, they also found the remains of a buffalo believed to have been illegally hunted.

Forensic processes

SANParks said SAPS has been informed and will continue with the necessary investigative and forensic processes.

The circumstances surrounding the man’s death will form part of the investigation, while authorities will also investigate the suspected illegal hunting of the buffalo.

The incident once again highlights the risks associated with illegal entry into protected wildlife areas, where encounters with dangerous animals can have fatal consequences.

World.title: N1 crash update: Motorists face 200km detour as highway stays closed
World.content:
Emergency and forensic teams work at the scene of the deadly N1 crash between Prince Albert and Leeu-Gamka, where 21 people died and four others were seriously injured. Image: X/@WCLiveTraffic

Motorists travelling through the Central Karoo face a 200km detour as authorities keep the N1 between Laingsburg and Beaufort West closed following Sunday night’s deadly crash.

Western Cape Mobility Minister Isaac Sileku warned that officials would not reopen the busy national route soon because of the severity of the collision.

“Because of the seriousness of the crash, the road will remain closed for some time,” Sileku said.



The collision between Prince Albert and Leeu-Gamka claimed 21 lives and left four people seriously injured.

Two minibuses and a station wagon were involved.

Crews continue work at crash scene

Emergency, medical, traffic and forensic teams continued working at the scene on Monday morning.



“Our traffic and emergency response teams are working tirelessly at the scene under challenging conditions,” Sileku said.

Authorities need to complete forensic investigations and clear the wreckage before they can safely reopen the highway.

Only alternative adds 200km

The Western Cape Government has urged motorists to avoid the N1 between Laingsburg and Beaufort West.



Drivers who cannot postpone their journeys must travel via Prince Albert Road Station, take the R407 towards the N12 and continue on the N12 towards Beaufort West.

Officials have asked truck drivers and long-distance operators to stop at the nearest town or truck stop rather than join growing queues around the closure.

Motorists already caught in traffic should keep emergency lanes clear and obey instructions from traffic officers.



Authorities have not yet announced when the N1 will reopen.

World.title: Kaizer Chiefs transfer window: Da Cruz makes his position clear
World.content:
Kaizer Chiefs head coach Fernando Da Cruz has not ruled out the possibility of the club making further signings before the transfer window closes.

Amakhosi have already brought in Renaldo Leaner, Thabo Moloisane, Adolf Mtasingwa, Faiz Abrahams and Langelihle Phili during the current transfer window. Khanyisa Mayo, who joined the club on loan last season, has also been signed on a permanent deal.

After six matches in the Betway Premiership, Chiefs currently sit fourth on the league table.



Despite the club’s activity in the transfer market, Da Cruz says he is satisfied with the squad at his disposal. However, the French coach remains open to strengthening his team if the right player becomes available.

Kaizer Chiefs signed six players this transfer window

“If a player is going to arrive, I think I would take the opportunity, but I don’t want to take a player just to take him. If it is to take someone, it is someone that will be useful,” Da Cruz said.

“For the moment, I am very happy with the squad that we have. We are moving forward; we are disappointed with the result.

“But we are on the right path in terms of the quality of the game, in terms of the modelling of the game, in terms of what we want to show. We must continue, we must not give up.”

With only a few days remaining before the transfer window closes, Chiefs could still make a surprise addition to their squad.

The left-back and attacking midfield positions appear to be areas where Amakhosi could use more depth and quality, potentially making one or two late additions possible before the deadline.

World.title: Horror Bloemfontein discovery sparks urgent police manhunt
World.content:
Police in the Free State are hunting for the mother of a newborn baby after a disturbing discovery in Bloemside: Image Pexels

A Bloemfontein community was left reeling this week after residents made a discovery no one could have prepared for.

It has since triggered an urgent police manhunt – and there are still more questions than answers.

The horror unfolded in Bloemside on Wednesday when a resident spotted a pack of dogs dragging a newborn’s severed head along the street.



Days later and the rest of the infant’s remains still haven’t been found.

Free State Community Safety, Roads and Transport MEC Jabu Mbalula did not hide his shock, saying: “I have come across terrible things in my life, but nothing comes close to this.”

WHAT POLICE HAVE CONFIRMED SO FAR

Mbalula has instructed senior police management in Mangaung to act.



Detectives have been deployed to trace the baby’s mother and locate the rest of the remains.

Free State police spokesperson Lieutenant-Colonel Thabo Covane confirmed on Friday that the body had still not been found.

He added there is “a possibility that the body was devoured by the beasts.”



A case docket of concealment of birth has been opened. It is still not known how the baby died, or how its head ended up in the dogs’ possession.

THE APPEAL BEHIND THE INVESTIGATION

Mbalula used the moment to point struggling mothers toward existing support structures rather than judgment alone.

“Our public health institutions are available for women to address matters such as unwanted pregnancies, and we encourage them to make use of those facilities.”



Authorities have appealed to anyone with information about the mother’s whereabouts, or the location of the baby’s remains, to come forward.

Honestly, stories like this stop me in my tracks.

A newborn should never end up as a headline like this one, and I hope whatever led to this is uncovered soon, for that child’s sake.

World.title: Task team formed to investigate Kempton Park women's deaths
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Police have assembled a dedicated multidisciplinary team to investigate the deaths of women in and around Kempton Park.

The team is currently holding an urgent meeting in Midrand following the discovery of a fifth woman’s body near Kempton Park on Monday morning.

The partially clothed body was found by a passerby on the side of the road in Olifantsfontein.

Police suspect the woman was killed between Sunday night and the early hours of Monday morning.

The discovery was made about 20 minutes from where police found the bodies of four other women in Kempton Park over a period of two months.

The latest development comes as police intensify efforts to locate missing jogger Elizabeth “Tsontso” Moselakgomo, who disappeared last week after leaving her home for an afternoon run.

Her disappearance has heightened concerns in the area, with authorities continuing to search for her.

Police say the four previous cases share similarities, but have not confirmed whether they are linked.

“We will rely on the experts to advise accordingly,” police spokesperson Brigadier Athlenda Mathe said.

“The detectives and investigative psychology unit will have to look at all the evidence that will be gathered from all the scenes. They will map out exactly what is happening,” Mathe added.

World.title: Fuel pain: Motorists face another steep price hike in October
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Fuel costs are showing no signs of easing, with rising oil prices and a weaker rand keeping pressure on motorists.

Mid-month Central Energy Fund data points to a petrol price hike of around R2.29 a litre in October.

That could push inland petrol prices above R29 a litre.

This is blamed on the usual macro suspects of higher oil prices and a weaker rand.

Brent crude is trading above 108 dollars a barrel and the rand near R16.25 to the dollar.

Diesel is also under pressure, with wholesale prices projected to rise by more than R2 a litre.

While there are calls for fuel price relief, Treasury says any help would need to be balanced against other government spending needs.

World.title: End to spam calls? Consumer Commission preparing new Opt-Out Registry
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - South Africans bombarded by unwanted telemarketing calls and text messages could soon have a new way to fight back.

The National Consumer Commission (NCC) is preparing to roll out its Opt-Out Registry, a system designed to help consumers block unsolicited marketing communications.

The registry will allow consumers to create profiles and indicate that they do not want to receive unwanted direct marketing calls and messages.

But for the system to work effectively, direct marketers will also have to play their part.

The NCC says all direct marketers are expected to register on the platform to ensure compliance with the Consumer Protection Act.

NCC spokesperson Phetho Ntaba urged consumers to visit the Commission’s website and create their profiles ahead of the launch.

READ | Growing calls for crackdown on spam calls

“What you need to do right now is to visit our website at the NCC. You will be able to create a profile as a consumer.”

The Commission is currently engaging with direct marketers and selected industries as part of its preparations for the launch.

Ntaba says the system is ready, with the official launch date to be announced soon.

The NCC is also calling on technology companies and other suitable partners to help make the Opt-Out Registry accessible to as many South Africans as possible.

“We want to make sure that the system is accessible to as many South Africans as possible,” Ntaba said, describing the technology partnerships as part of the Commission’s preparations for the rollout.

The NCC says direct marketers must also register on the platform for consumers to effectively opt out of unwanted communications.

“Without direct marketers in the system, it’s not going to be easy for you to opt out,” Ntaba said.

World.title: SAFA to pursue legal costs from Ledwaba, Mohlabeng
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The South African Football Association (SAFA) is preparing to pursue former presidential challengers Ria Ledwaba and Solly Mohlabeng for legal costs incurred during a series of court battles against the association.

Under re-elected president Danny Jordaan, SAFA says it will take legal steps to recover money spent defending multiple challenges brought by the duo.

The association is expected to send its first claim to Ledwaba and Mohlabeng in the coming days.

The move follows the recent dismissal, with costs, of their Constitutional Court application for leave to appeal.

Ledwaba and Mohlabeng had sought to overturn the outcome of SAFA’s 2022 presidential election. They also challenged their loss of standing within the association’s structures.

Their latest legal setback resulted in a costs order against them, which SAFA now intends to pursue.

The development comes shortly after Jordaan secured another term as the head of South African football’s governing body.

Jordaan was re-elected for a fourth term at SAFA’s elective congress this past weekend, defeating challenger Sandile Zungu.

He received 157 votes, while Zungu secured 82.

World.title: India cricketers refuse Asia Cup trophy from top Pakistan official
World.content:
DUBAI - India's women refused to collect the Asia Cup trophy from Pakistan Cricket Board chief Mohsin Naqvi after the team won a record-extending eighth continental title.

India hammered Sri Lanka by 72 runs in the T20 final in Dubai on Sunday but Harmanpreet Kaur's side skipped the trophy presentation, repeating the stance of the men's team last year.

On both occasions, the trophy was supposed to have been handed over by Naqvi in his role as head of the Asian Cricket Council.

Naqvi is also Pakistan's interior minister and head of the country's cricket board.

There are long-running tensions between nuclear-armed neighbours India and Pakistan.

A year after beating Pakistan in the final, the men's side have still not collected their trophy.

"That stand has been taken by BCCI (Indian cricket board), and we stand by it," Indian women's coach Amol Muzumdar told reporters.

"We are the champions, that's good enough."

Sunday's presentation was delayed by nearly 50 minutes, after which Naqvi distributed medals to the runners-up before the ceremony ended abruptly.

BCCI secretary Devajit Saikia and vice-president Rajeev Shukla were at the ground as India presented medals to their players themselves.

World.title: Is it possible to slow down the development of AI?
World.content:
WASHINGTON - Top AI executives say they want to slow the breakneck pace of artificial intelligence development, but competition, US government reluctance and geopolitical factors stand in the way.

- What are AI leaders proposing? -

On Saturday, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei advocated for a coordinated slowdown of AI development to better understand the risks arising from the technology's capabilities.

He received public support from his counterpart at OpenAI, Sam Altman, as well as from Elon Musk and Google DeepMind chief Demis Hassabis.

- Why now? -

In recent months, OpenAI and Anthropic have reported several incidents in which AI systems spontaneously broke out of their confined environments to access the internet and attack websites and platforms.

These AI systems demonstrated the ability to coordinate, establish hierarchies among themselves, cheat and erase traces of their actions.

Meanwhile, on Tuesday, Jacob Coxon -- who resigned from Anthropic and previously worked at OpenAI -- publicly accused both startups of lax security standards and "gambling with our lives."

- Will they slow down on their own? -

Competition among the industry's leading players is so fierce, with hundreds of billions of dollars in investment at stake, that none of them is willing to risk easing off the accelerator alone.

Amodei has expressed a willingness to coordinate with rivals, excluding China.

When asked by AFP about potential discussions to this end, Anthropic, OpenAI and Google did not immediately respond.

For now, the only concrete measure adopted by both Anthropic and OpenAI is the inclusion of independent observers who will internally verify the companies' work regarding AI safety.

- Is this a PR stunt? -

While many in the industry welcomed Amodei's message, others questioned his motives.

For Brian Roemmele, an entrepreneur and figure in the AI sector, it amounts to a sales pitch delivered just weeks before Anthropic is likely to take shares public.

"That is the IPO story in essay form: we are the responsible firm; we are the cure; buy the safety premium," he posted on X, referring to widely expected initial public offering.

Several figures in tech private equity also accused Anthropic of "regulatory capture" -- seeking to have public authorities cement, through regulation, a hierarchy with the startup at the top.

"Stop pretending the motivation to slow down is purely altruistic," said David Sacks, a former AI advisor to President Donald Trump who remains influential at the White House.

"You face massive product-liability exposure if your products enable a truly damaging cyberattack," he said.

- Can AI slow down without the Trump administration's support? -

On Sunday, Trump dismissed the warnings from AI industry leaders as "negative forces."

Several Republicans have expressed reluctance to actively regulate the technology, fearing it could stifle innovation and risk letting China win the AI race, according to House Speaker Mike Johnson.

On Sunday, Amodei reiterated the need for government oversight of AI. Like Altman and Hassabis, he believes that rules set by the industry itself would be insufficient.

- Can the brakes be applied without China? -

Anthropic's Amodei suggests limiting coordination to democratic countries, excluding China.

However, the AI race and China's advances in the field create "the toughest dilemma" regarding whether or not to slow down AI development, he noted on CBS on Sunday.

The United States plans to discuss AI safety on the sidelines of Chinese leader Xi Jinping's late September visit to Washington. But China is wary of any US attempt to impose its own regulatory framework, according to several media outlets.

This divergence is particularly pronounced given that China encourages the emergence of so-called "open" AI-systems that are freely accessible and modifiable -- in contrast to the "closed" models favored by major US companies.

Open AI models are, by definition, harder to control, as users can alter their parameters -- potentially for malicious purposes.

To allow leading non-Chinese companies to ease off the accelerator, Amodei urges stricter export controls on the most advanced US chips to China and better safeguards against the misappropriation of Western AI technology by Chinese laboratories.

World.title: 'Fed up': Thousands march against Sinaloa Cartel violence
World.content:
MEXICO CITY - Chanting and waving banners, thousands marched Sunday in the Mexican city of Culiacan to protest the deaths of people caught up in a war between two rival factions of the infamous Sinaloa Cartel.

Dressed in white, the protesters released dozens of white balloons into the sky before marching to the cathedral in the capital of Sinaloa state, shouting, "We want peace," and carrying signs saying, "I'm fed up with living in fear."

Culiacan's bishop, Jesus Jose Herrera, called on the gang members to stop the violence: "No territory and no ambition is worth more than a human life."

The protest was organised by the Catholic Church along with business leaders and families of missing persons.

Since September 2024, the state has been gripped by a bitter war between rival factions loyal to the families of Joaquin "El Chapo" Guzman or Ismael "El Mayo" Zambada, co-founders of the cartel who are both now serving life sentences in the United States.

Internal accusations of betrayal sparked the violence between factions.

Daily shootouts and roadblocks have led to closed businesses and the suspension of classes as Sinaloa became known as the most dangerous city in Mexico.

In two years, the death toll has surpassed 3,000, including many civilians caught in the crossfire.

World.title: 'Practical Magic 2' breaks Spidey spell over box office
World.content:
LOS ANGELES - The A-list witches of Warner Bros.' "Practical Magic 2" cast away Sony's "Spider-Man" from its weeks-long perch atop the North American box office, industry estimates showed.

Nearly three decades after the beloved original, Sandra Bullock and Nicole Kidman return to star in "Practical Magic 2," whose estimated $30 million debut ended Spidey's six-week run in first place.

The film resurrects the story of sisters Sally and Gillian Owens, modern-day witches who face a curse that sees any man they fall in love with doomed to an early death.

The witch sisters summoned another $16 million outside of North America, for a total global estimate of $46 million.

The original 1998 film hardly enchanted critics upon its debut, but went on to conjure a cult following that had kept hopes of a sequel alive ever since.

"Critics' reviews are weak like they were the first time, but the audience score is very good," said industry watcher David A. Gross.

The "cast is what drives these movies' success, and Nicole Kidman, Sandra Bullock, Maisie Williams and Joey King are strong."

But it wasn't all bad news for Sony's "Spider-Man: Brand New Day."

After swinging from victory to victory, the Tom Holland and Zendaya-led blockbuster caught second place this weekend, bringing in another $8.4 million, for a global total of $2.45 billion over its seven weeks in cinemas.

Christopher Nolan's "The Odyssey" sailed into a close third place, drawing another $7.4 million domestically, for an epic $1.64 billion over its nine-week global box office journey.

"Runner," an action comedy led by Alan Ritchson and Owen Wilson, debuted in fourth place, with the heroes fighting a cartel to get a sick young girl a lifesaving organ transplant.

It brought in $6.4 million domestically for Angel Studios.

"Coyote vs Acme" took fifth place, with Will Forte and an animated Wile E. Coyote snaring another $5.6 million for Falling Forward Films.

World.title: Edwin Sifuna rides Gen-Z anger as he takes aim at Ruto ahead of 2027
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Linda Mwananchi leaders Nairobi Senator Edwin Sifuna, Embakasi East MP Babu Owino and Siaya Governor James Orengo during a rally in Nairobi on September 13, 2026. [AFP]

A 44-year-old senator, Edwin Sifuna, has emerged as a rising challenger to Kenya's President William Ruto ahead of next year's election as he channels anger over political violence and corruption.

The east African country goes to the polls in August 2027 and a clear candidate has yet to emerge from a busy opposition playing field.

Many Kenyans are furious at the entrenched corruption under Ruto, and the extreme violence used against any hint of protest, including more than 100 deaths and dozens of abductions blamed on security forces in the last two years.

Sifuna earned goodwill among Kenya's young "Gen-Z" voters when he actively sought to stop police violence during the biggest protests in June 2024.

Now, the former lawyer is drawing huge crowds as he tours the country, including in the capital Nairobi on Sunday, though he has yet to officially declare a run for the presidency.

So far, his message has been almost entirely focused on criticising Ruto, who he accuses of overseeing a culture of "impunity".

"(Ruto) doesn't believe in the rule of law. He doesn't believe in democracy. He doesn't believe in freedom," Sifuna told AFP in an interview at his Nairobi office.

Sifuna's popularity has made him a target. Rallies have been violently disrupted by gangs of young thugs -- a common tactic used by all sides of the political spectrum in Kenya.

"It has been quite amazing to see the people showing up to our meetings, despite all the threats, all the intimidation," Sifuna said.

"This spectre of attacking people's motorcades, killing and maiming people, it's the lowest we have sunk in our politics," he added.

Many remain sceptical about Sifuna's chances, however, saying he is too young and inexperienced, and lacks any defined policies.

"He has not come out as a compelling presidential candidate who means business," political analyst Javas Bigambo told AFP, noting that he has failed to stake out ground on any major political talking point.

He also said Sifuna has among the "shortest" profiles in Kenyan politics, having only served a single term as senator.

But he previously served as the secretary-general of ODM, Kenya's longest serving opposition party, and some believe he could rally similar support to late leader Raila Odinga, a huge figure in Kenyan politics.

For a man whose name is on the lips of much of Kenyan society, Sifuna can seem uncomfortable with the limelight.

He admitted to feeling awkward while having his photo taken by AFP -- the moment only relieved when a group of waiters gathered for a nearby event spotted him and started shouting "Sisi ndio Sifuna" ("We are Sifuna").

"I'll be honest with you, my life has changed dramatically," he said. "(But) if you allow fear to paralyse you, you will never do anything."

He dodged questions about his policies, saying he was working with experts to build a manifesto.

"We accept there are people who know things better than us, and they need to be given the opportunity to help you run a government," he said.

And he dismissed questions about his age, pointing out he has served as a senator for longer than Barack Obama did before he was president: "How is it a criticism to be young?"

Sifuna's eager young team say they are receiving small donations from ordinary citizens -- almost unheard-of in Kenyan politics.

His opponents say the real money is coming from former president Uhuru Kenyatta, an ally-turned-rival of Ruto.

Sifuna denies he is anyone's puppet, and says the 2024 protests "fundamentally changed" Kenyan politics as young people mobilised around economic and political issues, rather than ethnic divides and the power of old money.

On Sunday, he drew huge crowds in Nairobi, including Joshua Kebwago, 32, who said Sifuna represented a break in establishment politics.

"He's here to uplift the poor, reduce taxes and the cost of living," he said. "We want something better."

Kenya's median age is just 20, and Sifuna admits he is riding a wave that is highly volatile: "There is this new energy that everybody is aware of, but is also untested," he said.

He is determined to try: "The only pressure you feel is that there are more people to disappoint... You cannot mess it up."

World.title: Police to restrict access to CBD during Linda Mwananchi Nairobi rally
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Linda Mwananchi officials during a rally. [Courtesy]

Organisers of the Linda Mwananchi rally and their supporters will not be allowed to access Nairobi’s Central Business District (CBD), Nairobi Regional Police Commander Issa Mohamud has warned.

According to Mohamud, police had received notification of the planned rally, which is scheduled to take place at Jacaranda Grounds on Sunday, through Embakasi East MP Babu Owino.

However, he warned that the CBD would remain off-limits, saying police would not allow Nairobi to become a battleground for political supremacy.

“The National Police Service respects the constitutional right of every Kenyan to assemble, demonstrate, express political views, and participate in public affairs, but that right must be exercised peacefully, lawfully, and with respect to the rights and safety of other Kenyans,” Mohamud stated.

According to Mohamud, they had received a tip that some individuals were planning to mobilise goons to disrupt the rally, prompting the directive to keep the CBD out of bounds.

“We have received some information, some credible information, that some individuals may seek to mobilise groups of unruly youths and goons to outnumber and intimidate and confront rival groups.”

“Therefore, I make a direct appeal to all political leaders, organisers or influencers to restrain their supporters and control their crowds. No political objective is worth the blood of a Kenyan,” he added.

Mohamud assured the organisers and those planning to attend the rally that police would provide security throughout the event and facilitate all lawful activities.

The Linda Mwananchi movement is set to hold its Nairobi rally on Sunday, September 13. The procession will start at All Saints Cathedral before proceeding to Jacaranda Grounds.

World.title: ODM vows not to interfere with Linda Mwananchi rally in Nairobi
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Linda Mwananchi leaders during a rally in Western Kenya. [Linda Mwananchi, X]

The Orange Democratic Movement (ODM) has said it will not disrupt the planned Linda Mwananchi rally scheduled for Sunday at Jacaranda Grounds.

In a statement on Friday, September 11, ODM Nairobi Chairman George Aladwa said the party had no business interfering with the rally, noting that Linda Mwananchi had a right to speak to Nairobi residents.

“I want to make it clear that nobody in ODM has any intention of disrupting or interfering with the Linda Mwananchi rally,” Aladwa stated.

He added: “We believe that political competition should be about ideas, policies and the ability to convince Kenyans, rather than confrontations between supporters of different political formations.”

Aladwa said ODM’s opponents had a right to tell Nairobi residents what they stood for and what they intended to offer Kenyans.

“The people are intelligent enough to listen to different political messages and make their own decisions,” Aladwa said.

At the same time, Aladwa said ODM was engaged in an extensive programme to market and strengthen the party across Nairobi as it prepared for activities to commemorate the anniversary of the death of its former party leader, the late Raila Amolo Odinga.

The chairman lauded Odinga for his contribution to Kenya’s democracy, the struggle for constitutional reforms and the political transformation of the country, saying his contribution could not be erased.

“His legacy remains an important part of ODM and Kenya’s political history. As we approach the 2027 General Election, our responsibility is to ensure that ODM remains strong, organised and firmly rooted across Nairobi,” the chairman stated.

“We will continue engaging residents in all constituencies and wards and explaining the party’s agenda to the people. I appeal to ODM supporters to remain calm and focused. Do not allow yourselves to be provoked into unnecessary political confrontations,” he added.

World.title: Ndindi Nyoro tells Ruto to keep off Tata Chemicals
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

PPK leader Ndindi Nyoro addresses a rally at Nambale market in Busia on August 30, 2026. [Benjamin Sakwa, Standard]

Kiharu MP Ndindi Nyoro has cautioned President William Ruto against meddling in the affairs of Tata Chemicals, Africa’s largest soda ash plant in Lake Magadi, Kajiado County.

Nyoro, who is the Peoples’ Party of Kenya leader, has accused President Ruto of an alleged plot to take control of Tata Chemicals through a shareholding scheme.

He said Ruto’s directive on Tata Chemicals closure raises concerns over the future of multinational firms and their operations in the country.

Speaking during a tour of Wote, Makueni County, on Thursday, Nyoro termed the Head of State’s move selfish, saying even if he had since softened his stance on the firm, it remains wanting for investors.

“His utterances were and remain wanting for external and internal investors. We don’t want investors to work in a bad political environment. Even if he seems to have made a U-turn on the matter, we are aware he has been pushing to be a shareholder in the company. We don’t want investors to be interfered with politically because we must create an environment where our people have access to job opportunities. It is almost reaching a catastrophic level in terms of lack of jobs for our people,” he said

The PPK leader warned that the country is in a bad economic state with a Sh13.5 trillion debt that is projected to grow further by next year.

“When Ruto exits next year the debt will be more than Sh15 trillion. The next president, who will be coming from the opposition, will have hard times in running this country. For every Sh100 that will be collected as tax from 2028, Sh91 will be used to repay government debts. We should not have time now to fight as opposition and also as Kenyans. We must hold hands and send the president back home because of his failures,” Nyoro said.

The MP urged opposition leaders to put aside their political differences and unite behind a single presidential candidate ahead of the 2027 General Election, saying that a united opposition would have a better chance of defeating President Ruto.

“If the opposition wants to defeat President Ruto, they must come together and present one presidential candidate. I am ready to talk to all the opposition principals,” Nyoro said.

Nyoro also outlined a raft of proposals he says could help revive Kenya’s economy and ease the financial burden on ordinary citizens.

Among his proposals is the use of the National Social Security Fund (NSSF) to strengthen the health sector. He argued that Kenyans should be able to access quality healthcare without being forced to bear the full cost of medical services.

Nyoro further proposed changes to the way education is financed, suggesting that bursaries currently administered through the National Government Constituencies Development Fund (NG-CDF) and county governments be channelled towards financing free primary and secondary education.

He said such an approach would create a more uniform education financing system and ensure that children from poor households are not disadvantaged because of their parents' inability to meet school-related expenses.

Nyoro's proposals come amid growing debate over the country's economic direction, the cost of living, access to healthcare and the financing of education.

World.title: Mama Tutam acquitted of Sh25m fraud, says Nigerian tycoon cost her marriage
World.content:
Nairobi Woman Representative aspirant Faith Mwikali Ndiwa, alias Faith Nguthu addresses journalists at the Milimani Law Courts in Nairobi on September 9, 2026. [David Gichuru, Standard]

A Nairobi Woman Representative aspirant has confessed the frustrations and embarrassment that befell her after befriending a wealthy Nigerian businessman who later accused her of defrauding him of Sh25 million.

Faith Mwikali Ndiwa, alias Faith Nguthu, popularly known as Mama Tutam, said she was kicked out of her marriage after the father of her three children discovered reports linking her to an alleged love affair with Nigerian investor Jude Olabayo Veracruz.

World.title: Sifuna hits back at Ruto over opposition agenda
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Nairobi Senator Edwin Sifuna promised to introduce austerity measures if the opposition takes power.

Nairobi Senator Edwin Sifuna has hit back at President William Ruto after the Head of State accused the united opposition of lacking a clear policy agenda ahead of the 2027 General Election.

Speaking in the Senate, Sifuna, who has been fronted as a potential presidential candidate in the coming elections, said the opposition’s immediate plan was to restore meritocracy in government and remove Ruto from power.

Sifuna also questioned government spending, citing claims that Sh12 billion had been spent on hospitality at State House at a time when the country was facing financial constraints.

“We are being told that Sh12 billion was spent on hospitality at State House, in a country where we are told we have no cash for capitation. So those of you who ask us for a plan, ours is to send you home,” Sifuna said.

The senator further promised to introduce austerity measures if the opposition takes power, arguing that government spending could be streamlined to free up resources for essential services.

“I believe in the first 100 days after we kick this government out, we should be able to cut out the fat that is being utilised at State House so that we can pay our teachers and fund our hospitals,” he said.

Sifuna’s remarks came a day after Ruto accused opposition leaders of using ethnic profiling and intimidation to influence voters in areas perceived to be opposition strongholds.

Speaking in Ngong and Ongata Rongai in Kajiado County, Ruto defended the broad-based UDA-ODM political arrangement, saying the pact was aimed at promoting national unity and ensuring equitable distribution of national resources.

“They are intimidating people along ethnic lines, telling them they must vote a certain way. Do not allow yourselves to be divided through tribalism and hatred. Their agenda is to spread tribalism and hatred,” Ruto said.

The exchange comes as political parties and leaders intensify preparations for the 2027 General Election, with the opposition seeking to consolidate its support base while the Kenya Kwanza administration defends its record and broad-based political arrangement.

World.title: Aggression against Arab nations must cease, says Sisi to Iran’s president
World.content:
Egyptian President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi reaffirmed his nation’s firm position in support of efforts to restore stability in the region.

The president emphasized Egypt’s expectation that Iran will exert all possible efforts to halt escalation and reach a comprehensive, sustainable, and peaceful settlement to the war—one that ensures the sovereignty of regional states and protects the resources and well-being of their peoples.

These remarks were made during a meeting between Sisi and his Iranian counterpart Masoud Pezeshkian, on the sidelines of the 18th BRICS summit held in New Delhi, India.

The Egyptian President underscored the imperative of halting any acts of aggression against Arab nations, in order to maintain good relations and and strengthen the historical and cultural ties uniting the region.

Meeting with Modi

Sisi on Sunday also met with Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi to discuss ways to advance Egyptian-Indian relations and build upon the growing momentum witnessed since ties were elevated to strategic partnership in 2023.

He emphasized the importance of taking concrete steps to strengthen this partnership, including increasing the volume of trade to $12 billion and boosting Indian investments in Egypt—particularly in the manufacturing, technology, clean energy, and automotive sectors.

The Indian Prime Minister affirmed his country’s commitment to further developing bilateral relations across various fields.

Edited translation from Al-Masry Al-Youm

World.title: Video: Celine Dion breaks down in tears at first concert after six-year hiatus
World.content:
Canadian superstar Celine Dion experienced an emotional moment on stage in Paris, moved to tears during her comeback concert—her first live performance before an audience after a years-long absence due to health issues.

The star affirmed that she had kept her promise to return to the stage and stand once again before her fans.

Dion performed at the La Défense Arena in Paris on Saturday, kicking off a series of shows in the French capital and marking her return to a full concert performance for the first time in nearly six years.

Her emotion was palpable as she stood before tens of thousands of fans who welcomed her with cheers and applause— a reflection of the immense anticipation surrounding her return to the stage.

Addressing the audience, Dion said: “I made a promise to return.”

“It is wonderful to be together,” she added, amidst an enthusiastic response from the crowd, before continuing: “Here I am, singing for you and singing for myself.”

The superstar thanked her fans for standing by her over the past few years, saying: “Thank you so much for your support and patience. I am who I am today thanks to your love.”

Dion’s return to the stage follows a long hiatus from performing, which began after she announced in December 2022 that she had been diagnosed with Stiff-Person Syndrome (SPS)—a rare neurological condition that affects movement and causes muscle stiffness and spasms.

Her health condition forced the Canadian artist to cancel her “Courage” world tour; she had previously cancelled a series of Las Vegas concerts in 2021 due to health issues.

Since announcing her diagnosis, Dion has spoken on several occasions about the difficulties she endured, all while maintaining her desire to return to singing and perform before her audience once again.

Paris Olympics

Despite a long hiatus from performing, Céline Dion made a public appearance in 2024 when she took part in the opening ceremony of the Paris Olympic Games, delivering a vocal performance that garnered widespread global attention.

Her appearance at the Olympics signaled her readiness to gradually resume her artistic career after years of focusing on her health.

Sixteen-Concert Run

Dion’s comeback has generated immense public interest, reflected in her Paris concert schedule; the series of shows has been extended to a total of 16 performances, running through October 14.

During these concerts, the artist will perform a selection of her most notable songs in both French and English, including “My Heart Will Go On,” “Think Twice,” and “It’s All Coming Back To Me Now.”

The announcement of Celine Dion’s return to the stage was made on her birthday, March 30, via an Instagram post in which she expressed her excitement about returning to her audience.

World.title: Scientific committee in Egypt recommends dismantling Ramesses II statue
World.content:
A specialized Egyptian scientific committee has recommended re-evaluating the sections used to complete the statue of King Ramses II, located in front of the Second Pylon at the Karnak Temple Complex in Luxor, RT reported on Sunday.

The committee also recommended studying the feasibility of dismantling the restored section atop the statue’s base, so long as it is confirmed that doing so will not impact the original part of the statue.

This recommendation follows from the committee’s comprehensive study of the statue, which revealed discrepancies in the type and color of certain blocks used in the restoration compared to the statue’s original sections.

Furthermore, the committee recommended conducting laboratory analyses on samples taken from the statue’s base—a section still in its original position—and comparing them with samples from the blocks used in the restoration.

This aims to verify whether the blocks belong to the same statue; should the results fail to match, those pieces would be excluded as having no confirmed connection to the statue.

Re-evaluation needed

The study also revealed discrepancies in the anatomical proportions of the restored section; its dimensions exceeded the statue’s presumed natural proportions.

Consequently, the committee recommended a scientific study to assess the feasibility of detaching this section, while ensuring the preservation of the original part and avoiding any damage to it.

At the same time, the committee instructed specialists at the archaeological site to search for missing fragments of the statue—including the upper part of the crown and a portion of the leg—and to examine any such pieces found to verify that they belong to the statue.

If the missing original parts are not found, an archaeological study will be conducted to determine their probable form and proportions, followed by an assessment of the archaeological feasibility of completing the statue, in accordance with international laws and charters governing restoration work.

The study concluded that completing the statue is not feasible; therefore, the discovered archaeological fragments will be preserved and stored rather than used in a speculative reconstruction of the statue.

World.title: PM stresses strengthening Egypt’s pharmaceutical industry, regulatory system
World.content:
Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly stressed that the pharmaceutical sector is one of the vital sectors receiving significant state attention, given its direct role in meeting citizens’ essential needs.

He underscored the need to continue efforts to strengthen the capacity of Egypt’s domestic pharmaceutical industry, support the localization of pharmaceutical and medical-supplies production, and increase local output in a way that helps secure market needs, reduce reliance on imports and open new prospects for Egyptian pharmaceutical exports, while maintaining the highest standards of quality and efficacy.

Madbouly made the remarks during a meeting on Sunday, September 13, 2026, with Egyptian Drug Authority (EDA) Chairman Ali al-Ghamrawy to review several of the authority’s work files and the latest efforts to develop Egypt’s pharmaceutical system and strengthen the sector’s capabilities.

During the meeting, al-Ghamrawy reviewed the EDA’s efforts to secure World Health Organization (WHO) recognition in regulating locally manufactured medicines and vaccines. He noted that the authority had attained Maturity Level 3 for medicines, following its attainment of the same level for vaccines in March 2022, making Egypt the first country in Africa to achieve the milestone in both fields.

Al-Ghamrawy said that WHO’s continued recognition of Egypt’s pharmaceutical regulatory system at Maturity Level 3 reflects the efficiency, stability and integration of the regulatory framework and its ability to perform its functions in line with international standards.

He noted that the recognition brings several benefits, including consolidating Egypt’s leadership at the Arab and African levels and strengthening its role in shaping the global pharmaceutical landscape. It also enables Egypt to participate more effectively in developing global pharmaceutical policies and standards through its engagement with relevant international and regional organizations and bodies.

The EDA Chairman added that the authority is continuing work on a number of improvements and upgrades required to advance to WHO-accredited Maturity Level 4. He reviewed key findings from the WHO’s assessment visit, which showed higher levels of implementation across the authority’s various regulatory functions and areas of responsibility.

He affirmed that Egypt is proceeding along the normal course of WHO reassessment processes, supporting continuous improvement and the sustainability of the maturity level achieved by the Egyptian pharmaceutical regulatory system.

Al-Ghamrawy also pointed to the EDA’s success in obtaining WHO prequalification and accreditation for the authority’s pharmaceutical control laboratories, describing it as a new international achievement that reflects the development of the authority’s technical and regulatory capabilities and strengthens confidence in Egypt’s pharmaceutical regulatory system.

Madbouly congratulated al-Ghamrawy and all EDA employees on the distinguished international achievement. He stressed that Egypt’s continued attainment of WHO Maturity Level 3 for medicines, alongside its attainment of the same level for vaccines, represents a global achievement reflecting the progress of Egypt’s pharmaceutical system and the ability of state institutions to meet leading international standards.

The Premier praised the EDA’s significant efforts to advance the regulatory and supervisory framework governing the pharmaceutical sector, commending the authority’s employees for their continued efforts toward development and ongoing improvement.

Madbouly stressed the importance of continuing efforts to preserve the gains achieved and advancing the development process toward higher levels of excellence and international recognition, further strengthening Egypt’s position and leadership in the pharmaceutical sector at the regional and international levels.

World.title: Egypt, Thailand explore advancing economic, investment, and trade ties
World.content:
Deputy Prime Minister for Economic Affairs Hussein Issa affirmed the Egyptian government’s keenness to develop cooperation with Thailand across various sectors, especially economic, industrial, educational, and cultural fields, noting that the state prioritizes attracting foreign investment by enhancing business competitiveness and offering necessary incentives to support investor expansion.

This came during a meeting on Sunday, September 13, 2026, between the Deputy Prime Minister and Second Deputy Speaker of the Thai House of Representatives Lertsak Pattanachaikul and his accompanying delegation, attended by Minister of Parliamentary Affairs Counselor Hany Hanna, Thai Ambassador to Cairo Thanawat Sirikul, and Assistant Foreign Minister for Asian Affairs Amr Hamza.

The meeting focused on upgrading Egyptian-Thai relations and expanding bilateral cooperation in economic, investment, parliamentary, and educational domains, while exploring mechanisms to increase trade volumes and encourage Thai investments.

Welcoming the delegation, Issa praised the growing momentum in bilateral relations rooted in long-standing friendship, voicing Cairo’s commitment to building on shared achievements toward broader horizons.

Issa highlighted Egypt’s competitive strengths, including its strategic location as an export hub to Arab, African, and global markets; its free trade agreements; and recent infrastructure upgrades in transport and energy that position Egypt as an ideal manufacturing and re-export base.

He urged Thai firms to seize local market opportunities in priority sectors, affirming government readiness to provide full facilities to support their expansion and boost bilateral trade.

For his part, Pattanachaikul affirmed Thailand’s interest in advancing ties across trade, investment, education, and parliamentary fields.

He highlighted Thai companies’ interest in expanding in Egypt to leverage promising market opportunities and increase bilateral trade exchange.

He also voiced appreciation for Egyptian support given to Thai students in Egypt, stressing the importance of high-level visits and direct air routes to spur tourism, trade, and cultural ties.

Both sides concluded by underscoring the need to capitalize on positive bilateral momentum to broaden investment, expand trade, and serve mutual interests.

World.title: FM reaffirms Egypt’s rejection of attacks on Saudi Arabia
World.content:
Minister of Foreign Affairs, International Cooperation and Egyptian Expatriates Badr Abdelatty reaffirmed Egypt’s firm rejection of any violations or attacks against Saudi Arabia.

This came during a meeting on Sunday, September 13, 2026, with Saudi Foreign Minister Prince Faisal bin Farhan bin Abdullah Al Saud.

During the meeting, held on the sidelines of the BRICS Summit in India, Abdelatty stressed Egypt’s full solidarity with Saudi Arabia and its support for the Kingdom in confronting anything that threatens its security, sovereignty, or territorial integrity.

The two ministers discussed a number of issues, foremost among them the fraternal bilateral relations between Egypt and Saudi Arabia, including high-level exchange of visits and ways to advance institutional cooperation frameworks in line with the strategic nature of relations between the two countries.

They also exchanged views on recent regional developments, including efforts to de-escalate tensions in the region and promote regional security and stability.

World.title: Health minister, NCERI officials discuss developing technical education, labor market skills
World.content:
Minister of Health and Population Khaled Abdel Ghaffar held talks with officials from the National Council for Education, Research, and Innovation (NCERI) on developing technical education, university programs, scientific research and the skills needed for the labor market.

Abdel Ghaffar met Salma al-Bakry, Head of the council’s Technical Secretariat, and Secretariat member Mahmoud Hamza at the ministry’s headquarters in the New Capital.

Health Ministry Spokesman Hossam Abdel Ghaffar said the meeting addressed the council’s role in coordinating education, scientific research and innovation, as well as preparing qualified professionals to keep pace with scientific and technological developments.

The talks covered plans for cooperation with the Ministry of Education and Technical Education to develop technical education and coordinate efforts on the National Qualifications and Skills Framework and the National Labor Market Index.

Officials also discussed cooperation with the Ministry of Higher Education and Scientific Research to develop new university specializations.

The meeting further covered plans to establish a research and studies unit within the council’s Technical Secretariat, as well as a committee to assess and develop university and pre-university education.

The legal status of the Technical Secretariat and its proposed budget for the 2026-2027 fiscal year were also discussed.

World.title: Hot, humid weather expected for Egypt on Monday
World.content:
The Egyptian Meteorological Authority (EMA) forecasts hot, humid weather during the day on Monday across the north of the country, extending to Greater Cairo, while conditions will be intensely hot in South Sinai and the south of the country.

The felt temperature is expected to soar to 46C in the south during daylight hours.

Temperatures will be moderate at night and during the early morning across most regions.

Weather maps indicate a likelihood of low-level clouds forming over scattered areas of the North Coast, Greater Cairo, Lower Egypt, and the Suez Canal cities; these may be accompanied by light, inconsequential drizzle in some locations.

There is also a chance of very light rain—occurring intermittently—in parts of Halayeb and Shalateen, as well as areas south of Aswan.

Satellite data indicated intermittent wind activity across Greater Cairo, the Lower Egypt, the northern coasts, Upper Egypt, South Sinai, and the Red Sea Governorate; these winds may help moderate temperatures in some areas during the evening.

The EMA warned of the potential impacts associated with the expected weather conditions, urging citizens to monitor its latest updates and take necessary precautions and preparations.

Expected temperatures for Monday:

Greater Cairo: 35C (Felt 37C).

Northwestern Coasts: 31C (Felt 34C).

Northeastern Coasts: 32C (Felt 36C).

Lower Egypt: 34C (Felt 36C).

Northern Upper Egypt: 38C (Felt 40C).

Southern Upper Egypt: 45C (Felt 46C).

Edited translation from Al-Masry Al-Youm

World.title: Liberian Officials Post Vulnerable Children’s Data to “Prove” Aid Programs Work
World.content:
Monrovia – In Liberia, showing your work used to mean something simple — a photo of a handshake, a ribbon-cutting, a smiling child holding a new backpack. This week, several government officials, among them Mo Ali, Managing Director of the Liberia Water and Sewer Corporation, took “showing your work” somewhere it should never go: they published spreadsheets. Full names. Ages. School enrollment lists. Home addresses. The names of caregivers. All of it, posted to Facebook, as proof that the government’s social protection programs for vulnerable children are real.

By Rodney D. Sieh, [email protected]

The backlash was immediate. Commenters accused the officials of playing politics with children’s lives. But the deeper story here isn’t really about a bad social media post. It’s about what happens when a country still carrying the scars of two civil wars treats a child’s location as a talking point.

A generation that has already been found — and lost — before

Look closely at who’s on these lists, and a pattern emerges. These aren’t just any children. Many were flagged as “out-of-school” or “street-connected” — bureaucratic terms that, in Liberia, often sit quietly on top of a much harder story: family separation, displacement, exploitation. Decades after the guns went silent, the trauma from those years hasn’t simply evaporated. It shows up today in the same places — kids without stable homes, kids vulnerable to being used, moved, or sold.

These are precisely the children a protection program exists to shield. Publishing their addresses and school names doesn’t just embarrass an agency. It can hand a map straight to whoever they were removed from in the first place.

The law is not vague about this

Cllr. Moriah Yeakula, an outspoken voice in the opposition Alternative National Congress, didn’t mince words: “Vulnerable children’s data cannot be used as a chess piece in the cesspool of political buffoonery,” she said. “Not only were their names published, but their schools, addresses, and even their parents’ and caretakers’ information. That’s a violation of the Children’s Law, and the Ministry must investigate this breach.”

She’s not reaching. Liberia’s Children’s Law of 2011 grants every child a right to privacy, and the guidelines built into that law specifically address the disclosure of a child’s personal information to outside parties — the exact thing that happened here. This isn’t a gray area dressed up as one for political effect. It’s the kind of breach the law was written to prevent.

UNICEF’s fingerprints are on this too — and that matters

The project behind these lists is funded by UNICEF, which raises the stakes further. The international standard that guides child protection work in exactly these situations — the Minimum Standards for Child Protection in Humanitarian Action, built with UNICEF’s own participation — says that information on vulnerable children should only move with informed consent from children and their caregivers, and only under real confidentiality protocols. Nobody asked these families first. UNICEF’s own global data policy says much the same: personal data on the people it serves should only be processed for a legitimate, protective reason — not to win an argument on Facebook.

That gap between policy and practice is now a donor’s problem too. A breach at this scale — names, schools, addresses, caregiver contacts, all in one place — is the kind of thing that tends to trigger uncomfortable questions from funders about who, exactly, their local partners are trusting with sensitive data.

The quiet damage no one’s talking about

Beyond the legal violation, there’s a slower harm that will outlast this week’s outrage cycle. A child publicly tagged as “removed and reunified” carries that label into a new school, a new neighborhood — a target for bullying, or worse, for someone who remembers a name from a Facebook post. Caregivers who took in a child at real personal risk — grandmothers, aunts, foster families — now have their contact details sitting in public view, reachable by whoever they were protecting that child from.

And there’s a longer-term cost still: trust. Families who might otherwise report abuse or accept help from these programs will think twice if the lesson they’ve just learned is that their children’s private details can end up as a political prop. Once that trust breaks, it is notoriously hard to rebuild — and the children who need these programs most are the ones who pay for it.

For a country still working to heal from war, that’s not a cost Liberia can afford to shrug off.

World.title: Liberia: Saclepea Mayor Under Fire After Admitting GOL Awarded MDR Contract in Nimba, Then Backtracks
World.content:
SACLEPEA, Nimba County — In Saclepea, Nimba County, the promise of newly paved streets should ordinarily be a welcome development. Instead, a government road project has become the subject of an increasingly heated political argument after the acting city mayor initially identified the Movement for Democracy and Reconstruction as the successful bidder, only for the party to later reject the claim and the mayor himself to clarify his earlier statement.

By Selma Lomax, [email protected]

The controversy has transformed what began as an announcement about the pavement of five streets into a broader debate about government procurement, political influence, and the responsibility of public officials to provide accurate information about projects financed with public resources.

Acting Saclepea City Mayor Wallace Zigbuo was initially categorical in describing the development. According to his first account, MDR had submitted a bid for the road project and emerged successful.

He said preparations were already being made for implementation, including a meeting concerning the project, and indicated that construction could begin within weeks. For residents awaiting better roads, the announcement carried the promise of visible change.

But the name attached to the alleged winning bid immediately made the development politically sensitive. MDR is a political party, not a conventional construction company. Vice President Jeremiah Kpan Koung, one of the most influential figures in President Joseph Boakai’s administration, hailed from the party.

That political connection transformed the story from a local infrastructure announcement into a national governance question. If the party itself had won a multimillion-dollar government road contract, critics argued, the issue would extend beyond Saclepea’s streets to the integrity of Liberia’s public procurement system.

The opposition Congress for Democratic Change quickly seized upon the report. In a September 12 statement, the CDC accused the government of awarding what it described as a US$3.5 million road contract to MDR and characterized the alleged arrangement as an unacceptable conflict of interest.

The party questioned how a political organization could participate in a government construction project and raised concerns about whether the contract had been competitively advertised and awarded. For the CDC, the controversy was not merely about whether roads would be constructed.

It was about the possibility that political affiliation could influence access to government resources. The opposition argued that MDR’s position as a political party and its association with the ruling Unity Party establishment made the reported contract especially troubling. The party also questioned whether MDR possessed the legal and technical standing to operate as a contractor for a public road project.

The CDC called for the alleged contract to be terminated and demanded greater transparency from the government. But before the political storm could settle around the original statement, MDR issued its own response.

In a statement signed by National Secretary General Jonathan S. Jackson, MDR said it had taken note of reports and social media posts claiming that the party had won a Ministry of Public Works bid to pave five streets in Saclepea. The party described those reports as false, misleading and inaccurate. MDR emphasized that it remains a political party registered and accredited by the National Elections Commission and said it has never been, and will not become, a construction company.

The party further insisted that it does not participate in bidding for public works contracts. That denial fundamentally changed the nature of the controversy. What had initially appeared to be a question of whether a political party should have won a government contract became a question of whether the party had been correctly identified in the first place.

And that is where Mayor Zigbuo’s subsequent clarification became significant. The acting mayor later returned to clarify his earlier comments concerning MDR and the road project. Rather than maintaining that MDR, as a political party, had been awarded the contract, the clarification sought to explain that his initial statement should not be understood as confirmation that the party itself was the government’s road contractor.

The attempt to clarify the matter, however, did not erase the original statement. Instead, it left the public facing two competing versions of the same development. The first was that MDR had submitted a bid and won. The second was that the reference to MDR should not be interpreted as the political party itself receiving a construction contract. MDR’s own statement went even further, saying the party had not participated in such a bidding process at all.

That gap between the initial announcement and the subsequent denial is now at the center of the Saclepea debate. The Ministry of Public Works is therefore being placed under increasing pressure to provide the documentary answer.

The ministry’s procurement records establish that road rehabilitation in Saclepea and Bahn was the subject of a formal government procurement process. An open domestic bidding notice was issued for the project, with prospective bidders invited to submit bids under established procurement requirements.

The existence of that process is important because it shows that the road project itself was not invented by the controversy. There is a real government infrastructure project.

The unresolved issue is the identity of the successful bidder and whether the name “MDR” was ever legitimately connected to the bidding process. A procurement notice does not automatically mean that the organization named in a political statement won the contract.

Similarly, a mayor’s announcement does not substitute for an official award notice, evaluation report, or signed contract. Those documents are what would ultimately determine what happened.

The Ministry of Public Works, as the government institution responsible for the project, holds the most important piece of the puzzle.

If MDR was not a bidder, the ministry can establish that through its bid records. If another construction company won the contract, the ministry can identify that company. If the procurement process reached only the evaluation stage, that too can be clarified. For the Ministry of Public Works, the matter should ultimately be resolved through procurement documents.

A simple announcement about road construction has become a controversy involving the opposition, a political party led by the vice president, a local government official, and the Ministry of Public Works. It is also a reminder that public officials operate in an environment where their words can carry consequences far beyond their immediate audience.

For Mayor Zigbuo, the challenge is now not merely to clarify what he meant but to help explain how the original information came to be presented as fact. For MDR, the challenge is to demonstrate through the procurement record that its denial is supported by the official process. For the CDC, the challenge is equally clear: to substantiate its allegation with documentary evidence rather than political suspicion.

And for the Ministry of Public Works, the simplest route out of the controversy may be the most powerful one—release enough information for the public to independently determine who bid, who won, and who is legally responsible for constructing the five streets.

World.title: Liberia: Former Solicitor General Cephus Calls on Boakai to Apologize to Ex-VP Taylor Over Arrest
World.content:
MONROVIA — Former Solicitor General of Liberia, Cllr. Sayma Syrenius Cephus, has called on President Joseph Nyuma Boakai to publicly apologize to former Vice President Jewel Howard Taylor over what he described as the degrading manner in which she was arrested and detained in connection with Liberia’s multimillion-dollar drug investigation.

By Gerald C. Koinyeneh, [email protected]

Taylor, a former First Lady, Senator and Vice President, has been charged with drug trafficking, money laundering and other offenses following the government’s investigation into a major cocaine seizure.

She was initially placed in pretrial detention at the Monrovia Central Prison before the court later granted her compassionate release.

In a national address before her release, President Boakai said Taylor would be afforded due process and a fair trial, while reaffirming his administration’s commitment to leaving no stone unturned in the fight against drugs and other illicit substances.

But Cephus, while expressing support for the administration’s anti-drug campaign, said the government’s pursuit of justice must not come at the expense of due process, dignity and the presumption of innocence.

In a strongly worded statement titled “Mr. President, You Owe Madam Jewel Howard Taylor an Apology,” Cephus said he was not asking the President to apologize for the allegations against Taylor, but for the manner in which she was treated during her arrest.

“I fully support the President’s war on drugs,” Cephus said. “If anyone, including former officials, is found to be part of a drug network, let the full weight of the law apply.”

However, he argued that “process matters as much as outcome,” warning that the treatment of former officials accused of crimes must not resemble practices associated with Liberia’s past military regimes.

“The way Jewel was arrested is exactly how the PRC operated in the 1980s,” Cephus said, referring to the People’s Redemption Council, which seized power in 1980.

He questioned whether a former constitutional Vice President needed to be arrested in a manner he said appeared degrading while the allegations against her remained subject to judicial determination.

“Do we need to effect the arrest of a former First Lady, a former Senator, and a former constitutional Vice President in a manner that appears degrading, when what is being said about her remains an allegation?” he asked.

‘Why Was She Arrested That Way?’

Cephus also questioned aspects of the government’s handling of Taylor’s case, including its decision to seek bail after initially placing her in detention.
